## Part A — Campaign-wide rules

### A1. World constants

| Item | Decision |
|---|---|
| Amani's unit | **Special Cases Unit (SCU)**, fictional, based at the fictional **Tausi Lane Police Station**, Nairobi. Not the real DCI, not a real station. |
| OB number format | `OB 41/14/03`: entry number / day / month. No year anywhere in the game, so it never dates. Format to be checked by the cultural reader. |
| Calendar | The campaign runs about 21 months: region 1 in March–May, region 5 over Christmas, region 6 in February–March of the second year, region 10 ending in November–December. Weather, school terms and holidays follow the real Kenyan calendar. *(Revised during region 6: the original "one year" didn't fit five regions after January.)* |
| Money | Kenya shillings, written `KSh 2,300`. Realistic prices only (matatu fare KSh 50–100, smokie KSh 30, tea KSh 20). |
| Mobile money | Fictional service **"PesaPap"** on the fictional network **"Jamii Mobile"**. Till and phone numbers are fictional formats that can't belong to a real person (`Till 880 214`; phone `07xx` numbers from a reserved fake range listed in `_campaign.json`). |
| Businesses | Every business is fictional, even on a real street (Omar Printers on real River Road). No real company is shown doing wrong. Real public places (Jeevanjee Gardens, Railway Station, City Market, Uhuru Park, Machakos Country Bus) appear only as settings, never as culprits. |
| Newspaper | Fictional **"Taifa Daily"** and its afternoon edition **"Taifa Jioni"**. |
| Spine thread IDs | `t_mvua` (the shell company and its till number), `t_stamp` (the forged registrar seal), `t_kivuli` (the name itself), `t_registry` (missing files), `t_fundi` (the enforcer), `t_joseph` (Amani's father). |

Boss cases sit at the top of their region's range or one step above it.

### A3. Region 1 rules (clarifications added to the design doc §2.10)

- **Evidence types:** physical and witness only. "Physical" includes **found paper**: receipts, tickets, logbooks, registers, notes, a printed photo. Official records you have to *request* (statements, phone and mobile-money logs) start in region 3.
- **No checkable lies.** Suspects tell the truth or give a flat denial ("I didn't touch him"). A flat denial is not a fact the player can contradict. Lying, and pressing claims with evidence, start in case 11. This keeps region 1 about one skill: reading evidence and placing people in time and space.
- **No credibility stamps, warrants or gated actions.** Wrong charge submissions still cost stars (§2.9), and the folder shows the stamps as a greyed-out row with a "from case 11" label so the player knows they're coming.
- **Every case teaches one new interface beat** (listed per card), so the region doubles as the tutorial and never shows a wall of instructions.

### A4. Spine detail schedule (all 100 cases)

From §4.3: about one case in four carries a Kivuli detail that isn't needed to solve it. Planned placement:

### A5. Fairness audit targets (checked by `tools/audit.mjs`)

| Dimension | Target across 100 cases |
|---|---|
| Culprit gender | Neither gender above 65% |
| Culprit community (by name origin, tagged provisionally and confirmed by the cultural reader) | No single community above 18% of culprits. Every community that appears as a culprit also appears at least as often as a victim, witness or helpful character |
| Victim gender | Neither above 65% |
| Motive | No category above 22%. Categories: money/debt, cover-up, business rivalry, land/inheritance, revenge, relationship/jealousy, protecting someone, fraud exposure, commissioned (spine) |
| Occupation | No occupation is the culprit more than 3 times (stops "the matatu guy did it" becoming a pattern) |
| Age | Culprits span 20s to 70s; no band above 35% |
| Setting | Every region's cases use at least 7 distinct settings |
| Recurring names | No full name reused anywhere; no surname reused within a region except for family members in the same case |

**Region tags are provisional.** Name origin is an imperfect proxy for community, and the tags exist only to stop accidental patterns. Every tag in Part L is reviewed by the cultural reader.

### A6. Case card format (used for every case below)

Header line, then: **OB entry**, **Setting**, **Victim**, **Cast**, **What really happened**, **Evidence**, **Proof**, **Eliminations**, **Red herrings / twist**, **Charge sheet**, **New interface beat**, **Kenyan texture**, **Spine**, **Glossary**, **Images**, **Audit tags**.

Times are 24-hour. "Window" means the time-of-death window the evidence establishes.

Short, contained cases inside a few streets: Ngara, Moi Avenue, River Road, Luthuli Avenue, Jeevanjee Gardens, City Market, the Railway Station, Uhuru Park. March into the April long rains. ### Case 1 — The Last Fare

`case-001` · Nairobi CBD · boss: no · 5 min · suspects 2 · chain 2 · herrings 0 · liars 0 · groups WHO

**OB entry.** OB 41/14/03, 22:52. Stage marshal Kassim Juma reports a matatu driver found unresponsive behind his parked vehicle at Ngara stage. Pronounced dead at the scene.

**Setting.** Ngara matatu stage, Friday night, 22:40. Fictional sacco **Ngara Line Sacco**, route **9N** Ngara–Kencom. Sodium lights, a smokie vendor's cart, two matatus parked, the rest out on trips.

**Victim.** **Moses Wafula**, 41, driver of matatu `KDK 418T`. Single blow to the back of the head with a heavy object. Fare pouch still on him with KSh 2,300, phone in pocket: not a robbery.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link to victim | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Peter Kamau | 38 | Suspect | Fellow 9N driver; owes Moses KSh 30,000 from the drivers' chama | **Culprit** |
| Brian Otieno | 24 | Suspect | Moses's makanga (conductor); they argued that afternoon over his daily cut | Innocent: at Kencom all night |
| Kassim Juma | 55 | Witness | Ngara stage marshal; found the body | Innocent |
| Mercy Chebet | 30 | Witness | Smokie vendor at the stage | Innocent |
| Wanjiru Gathoni | 47 | Witness (statement only) | Kencom stage marshal | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Peter had skipped three chama contributions and borrowed against his share. Moses, the chama treasurer, told him that evening he'd report it to the sacco chairman on Monday, which would cost Peter his route. At about 22:20, with only their two matatus parked, Peter took the wheel spanner from his own tool roll, followed Moses behind his vehicle and struck him once. He threw the spanner under the next matatu and drove off on his 22:30 trip.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Scene | Blow to back of head; fare pouch KSh 2,300 untouched |
| ev_spanner | Physical | Under the neighbouring matatu | Wheel spanner; handle painted **9N-K** (sacco drivers mark their tools with route and initial) |
| ev_toolroll | Physical | Peter Kamau's matatu (he lets you look) | Canvas tool roll with one empty slot the shape of a spanner; other tools marked 9N-K |
| ev_ngara_tally | Physical (found paper) | Kassim's tally book | Vehicles parked 22:00–22:30: only `KDK 418T` (Moses) and `KCZ 902M` (Peter). Peter departed 22:31 |
| ev_kencom_tally | Physical (found paper) | Brought from Kencom | Matatu `KBT 551Q` waiting to fill 21:50–22:45, makanga **B. Otieno** |
| ev_mercy | Witness | Mercy Chebet | Heard a shout about 22:20; saw a man in a **maroon** sacco jacket walk from behind Moses's matatu towards the other parked matatu. Kassim was at her cart buying a smokie at that moment |
| ev_kassim | Witness | Kassim Juma | Last saw Moses alive 22:10; found him 22:40. Sacco drivers wear maroon jackets, makangas wear green |
| ev_gathoni | Witness | Kencom marshal | Otieno never left the Kencom queue; she could hear him shouting for passengers the whole time |

**Proof**
1. `ev_spanner` + `ev_toolroll` → the weapon came from Peter's tool roll.
2. `ev_mercy` + `ev_kassim` + `ev_ngara_tally` → the attacker wore a driver's jacket, and the only other driver at the stage was Peter → **WHO = Peter Kamau**.

**Eliminations.** Brian Otieno: `ev_kencom_tally` + `ev_gathoni` (at Kencom 21:50–22:45). Kassim Juma: `ev_mercy` (at her cart at 22:20). Mercy Chebet: `ev_kassim` (he was standing at her cart).

**Red herrings / twist.** None. The afternoon argument with Brian is mentioned in the OB entry, but every early case lets the evidence speak plainly.

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Moses Wafula at Ngara stage.` Person words in bank: Peter Kamau, Brian Otieno, Kassim Juma, Mercy Chebet (4; passes rule 9's region-1 minimum).

**New interface beat.** The whole loop, guided once: read the OB entry → tap hotspots → watch facts drop into the notebook → open the charge sheet → drag a name → submit → Halima's verdict → reconstruction. Mwalimu narrates each step by voice-note; every later case runs without guidance.

**Kenyan texture.** Stage marshal's tally book, chama debt, maroon vs green sacco uniforms, tools marked with route numbers, the smokie cart, the 22:30 "last trips" rush.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** makanga (conductor), sacco (savings and transport cooperative), chama (savings group), smokie pasua (smokie sausage split and filled with kachumbari), stage.

**Images (6).** Portraits: Moses (victim), Peter, Brian, Kassim. Location: Ngara stage at night. Evidence photo: the marked spanner on tarmac. Mercy and Wanjiru are statement-only cards.

**Audit tags.** Culprit M, 30s, Kikuyu-origin name, motive money/debt. Victim M, 40s, Luhya-origin name.

### Case 2 — Wet Paint

`case-002` · Nairobi CBD · 6 min · suspects 3 · chain 2 · herrings 0 · liars 0 · groups WHO

**OB entry.** OB 07/18/03, 06:41. Cleaner Nancy Akinyi reports the night guard of Kilele House found at the foot of the 4th-floor stairwell.

**Setting.** **Kilele House**, a fictional six-storey office block on Moi Avenue. The 4th-floor corridor is being repainted; drop cloths on the floor, the front door locked from inside at 19:00 every night by the night guard.

**Victim.** **Francis Mutua**, 52, night askari. Head injury consistent with a blow, then a fall down the stairs. His torch is broken beside him. A cream-coloured paint smear on his sleeve.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rehema Salim | 41 | Suspect | Accountant at fictional Bidii Freight, 4th floor | **Culprit** |
| Isaac Kiprotich | 33 | Suspect | Painter contracted for the 4th floor | Innocent: signed out 17:10 |
| Collins Wekesa | 27 | Suspect | Day askari; had argued with Francis about shift swaps | Innocent: off duty, at home |
| Nancy Akinyi | 44 | Witness | Morning cleaner who found him | Innocent |
| Ali Hussein | 60 | Witness | Night askari at the building next door | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Rehema had been skimming client payments at Bidii Freight. An audit was due Monday. She came back at 20:40 to take the cash ledger out of the office. On the way down at about 21:15, carrying the ledger and her shoes in a bag, she walked through the wet corridor in her office court shoes, met Francis on his rounds and panicked when he asked what she was carrying. She shoved him; he fell down the stairwell. She left by the side fire door. The ledger is gone.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Stairwell | Blow and fall; torch broken; cream paint smear on sleeve |
| ev_register | Physical (found paper) | Ground-floor desk | Visitor register after 19:00 lock-up: **R. Salim, Bidii Freight, in 20:40**, no sign-out. Kiprotich signed out 17:10. No other entries |
| ev_tin | Physical | 4th floor | Paint tin, "Ivory Cream", label: touch dry 4–6 hours. Painter's work note: final coat 16:50 |
| ev_print | Physical | Drop cloth in the 4th-floor corridor | One shoe print in wet paint: a narrow heel, about size 38, a women's court shoe |
| ev_bin | Physical | Bidii Freight office bin (cleaner shows you) | A pair of size 38 court shoes, cream paint on one heel |
| ev_ali | Witness | Ali Hussein | Saw a torch moving on the 4th-floor stairwell window, heard a shout at about 21:15. Saw only one person enter Kilele House after 19:00: a woman with a laptop bag, about 20:40 |
| ev_wekesa_wife | Witness | Collins's wife (statement only) | Collins was home in Kayole all evening; their neighbours' kesha kept everyone awake past midnight |
| ev_nancy | Witness | Nancy Akinyi | The fire door was unlatched when she arrived; it is always latched at night |

**Proof**
1. `ev_tin` + `ev_print` → whoever left the print walked through the corridor while the paint was still wet (after 16:50, before about 21:00–23:00), wearing a size 38 women's court shoe.
2. `ev_register` + `ev_ali` + `ev_bin` → the only person in the building after lock-up was Rehema Salim, and her shoes carry the paint → **WHO = Rehema Salim**.

**Eliminations.** Isaac Kiprotich: `ev_register` (out 17:10) + `ev_ali` (only one person entered after 19:00). Collins Wekesa: `ev_wekesa_wife` + `ev_ali`. Nancy Akinyi: arrived 06:30 (register morning entry), long after the 21:15 shout. Ali Hussein: never entered (his own guard book shows him at his post).

**Red herrings / twist.** None. The painter covered in cream paint is a natural first suspicion, but the timing removes him cleanly.

**Charge sheet.** `{who} caused the death of Francis Mutua at Kilele House.` Person words: Rehema Salim, Isaac Kiprotich, Collins Wekesa, Nancy Akinyi, Ali Hussein (5).

**New interface beat.** **Found paper.** The register opens as a full-screen ruled book you scroll through. Facts are lifted out of it line by line. Also the first **time window** in the notebook: Ali's 21:15 shout gets a clock icon.

**Kenyan texture.** Night askari culture, the visitor register every Nairobi office block keeps, a neighbourhood kesha (night vigil) as an alibi, Moi Avenue office life.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** askari (security guard), kesha (all-night prayer vigil), mzee (elder; respectful term for an older man).

**Images (5).** Portraits: Francis, Rehema, Isaac, Collins. Location: Kilele House stairwell at night with drop cloths.

**Audit tags.** Culprit F, 40s, Coastal/Swahili-origin name, motive cover-up (embezzlement). Victim M, 50s, Kamba-origin name.

### Case 3 — Seat Fourteen

`case-003` · Nairobi CBD · 6 min · suspects 3 · chain 2 · herrings 0 · liars 0 · groups WHO

**OB entry.** OB 19/21/03, 05:58. A passenger reports the booking clerk of Tana Express found behind the counter at Machakos Country Bus station; cash box missing.

**Setting.** Machakos Country Bus station, 05:00–06:00, buses warming up, fictional bus company **Tana Express** (Nairobi–Kitui, Nairobi–Garissa). Booking office with a counter, a carbon ticket book and a steel cash box.

**Victim.** **Ruth Nyokabi**, 35, booking clerk on the early shift. Struck once with the office's own steel ticket punch. Cash box (night's takings, about KSh 46,000) gone.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stephen Musyoka | 46 | Suspect | Former Tana Express tout, sacked in February after Ruth reported him for selling fake tickets | **Culprit** |
| Kevin Omondi | 29 | Suspect | Driver of the 06:00 Garissa bus; Ruth had complained about his lateness | Innocent: with the mechanic 05:00–05:50 |
| Lilian Jeptoo | 31 | Suspect | Night-shift clerk, handed over to Ruth at 05:00 | Innocent: left at 05:04 |
| Mwikali Nzioka | 52 | Witness | Tea vendor at the booking office door | Innocent |
| Gideon Kirui | 40 | Witness | Tana Express mechanic | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Stephen came to the counter at 05:20, bought a ticket for seat 14 on the 05:45 Kitui bus so he'd have a reason to be at the counter, and at 05:22 reached over for the cash box while Ruth was writing the counterfoil. She grabbed his sleeve; he hit her with the ticket punch and left with the box. He dumped the empty box in the luggage bay of the rival company's bus where he now works, and never boarded the Kitui bus.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Behind counter | Struck once; the steel ticket punch beside her |
| ev_counterfoil | Physical | Torn counterfoil in Ruth's hand | **05:45 Kitui, Seat 14**, issued **05:22**, the last entry in the ticket book |
| ev_ticketbook | Physical (found paper) | Counter | Carbon book: last ticket 05:22 (seat 14); previous 05:09 |
| ev_manifest | Physical (found paper) | Kitui bus conductor | Seat 14: **S. Musyoka**, Kitui. Marked "no show"; bus left 05:51 with the seat empty |
| ev_cashbox | Physical | Luggage bay of a rival company's bus | Tana Express cash box, forced open, empty |
| ev_mwikali | Witness | Tea vendor | Stephen Musyoka bought a ticket about 05:20: "He never travels, that one. He lives here." |
| ev_gideon | Witness | Mechanic | Kevin Omondi did the pre-trip check with him from 05:00 to 05:50 under the Garissa bus |
| ev_gatelog | Physical (found paper) | Station gate askari's book | L. Jeptoo out 05:04 |

**Proof**
1. `ev_counterfoil` + `ev_ticketbook` → the last person Ruth served, at 05:22, bought seat 14 on the Kitui bus.
2. `ev_manifest` + `ev_mwikali` → seat 14 was Stephen Musyoka, who bought a ticket and never boarded → **WHO = Stephen Musyoka**. (`ev_cashbox` in the bay where he works supports it.)

**Eliminations.** Kevin Omondi: `ev_gideon`. Lilian Jeptoo: `ev_gatelog` (out 18 minutes before the 05:22 sale). Mwikali Nzioka: she was serving tea to the queue the whole time (Gideon's statement mentions his 05:30 cup). Gideon Kirui: with Kevin under the bus.

**Red herrings / twist.** None.

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Ruth Nyokabi at the Tana Express booking office.` Person words: Stephen Musyoka, Kevin Omondi, Lilian Jeptoo, Mwikali Nzioka, Gideon Kirui (5).

**New interface beat.** **The map.** Two locations for the first time (booking office, the bus yard) and moving between them. Also **matching two pieces of paper**: the notebook shows the counterfoil and manifest side by side when both are tapped.

**Kenyan texture.** Country Bus at dawn, carbon ticket books and seat numbers, manifests, touts, tea vendors at the door, the gate askari's logbook.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** manamba (tout), stage, chai (tea).

**Images (5).** Portraits: Ruth, Stephen, Kevin, Lilian. Location: Machakos Country Bus at dawn.

**Audit tags.** Culprit M, 40s, Kamba-origin name, motive revenge (for the sacking) plus theft. Victim F, 30s, Kikuyu-origin name. *Note for the audit: this is the only "tout" culprit allowed in region 1, and his motive is personal, not a comment on touts.*

### Case 4 — Stima Imepotea

`case-004` · Nairobi CBD · 7 min · suspects 3 · chain 2 · herrings 0 · liars 0 · groups WHO

**OB entry.** OB 33/27/03, 00:14. The owner of Mapumziko Hotel reports his night receptionist found dead at the front desk after a power blackout.

**Setting.** **Mapumziko Hotel**, a fictional budget hotel off Haile Selassie Avenue. Three floors, 14 rooms, one old lift. A citywide blackout hits at 23:10 and power returns at 23:55.

**Victim.** **Faith Chepkoech**, 26, night receptionist. Strangled with the lanyard of her own key ring (report language only; no image of the body). The electric wall clock behind the desk stopped at **23:10**.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paul Njeru | 44 | Suspect | Guest in room 12, checked in two nights before | **Culprit** |
| Kennedy Ouma | 36 | Suspect | Guest in room 7; had complained loudly about the hot water | Innocent: stuck in the lift |
| Zawadi Mwende | 39 | Suspect | Hotel cook; owed Faith money | Innocent: buying candles across the road |
| Amos Kibet | 58 | Witness | Hotel owner, at home when it happened | Innocent |
| Selina Waweru | 34 | Witness | Lift technician on night call | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Two years earlier Paul Njeru, using another name, took KSh 180,000 from Faith's family for a fake overseas job placement. On his second night at the hotel she recognised him and said she'd call the police in the morning. When the power went at 23:10 he came down the stairs with a candle, and in the dark at the desk he killed her. He went back up the stairs with the candle and left it outside his door while he locked it.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_clock | Physical | Reception wall | Electric clock stopped at 23:10 (blackout) |
| ev_body | Physical | Front desk | Report: lanyard; struggle at the desk; the reception candle still unlit in the drawer |
| ev_wax | Physical | Stairs | A trail of white candle-wax drips from the reception desk up the stairs to the 2nd-floor landing |
| ev_stub | Physical | Outside room 12 | A burned-down candle stub on the floor outside the door of **room 12** |
| ev_register | Physical (found paper) | Front desk | Guest register: room 12, **P. Njeru**; room 7, K. Ouma; rooms 3, 9 empty |
| ev_lift | Physical (found paper) | Lift technician's callout sheet | Lift stuck between floors 23:10; occupant **room 7 guest** freed 23:58 |
| ev_kiosk | Witness | Kiosk owner across the road (statement only) | Zawadi bought four candles at 23:12 and waited for change for twenty minutes because nobody had coins |
| ev_amos | Witness | Owner | Was at home in Kileleshwa; called at 23:58 by Selina |

**Proof**
1. `ev_clock` + `ev_body` → Faith died during the blackout, in the dark, and her own candle was never lit, so the killer brought light.
2. `ev_wax` + `ev_stub` + `ev_register` → the light went from the desk up to room 12, whose guest is Paul Njeru → **WHO = Paul Njeru**.

**Eliminations.** Kennedy Ouma: `ev_lift` (trapped 23:10–23:58). Zawadi Mwende: `ev_kiosk` (across the road 23:12 to about 23:35, and the candles she bought are still wrapped in her bag). Amos Kibet: `ev_amos` + Selina's call record. Selina Waweru: arrived 23:40 by the front door (register).

**Red herrings / twist.** None. The angry room-7 guest is suspicious but provably stuck.

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Faith Chepkoech at the Mapumziko Hotel.` Person words: Paul Njeru, Kennedy Ouma, Zawadi Mwende, Amos Kibet, Selina Waweru (5).

**New interface beat.** **The scene sketch.** A floor plan of the hotel drawn as a police sketch; tapping the stairs reveals the wax trail floor by floor. First case where *following* evidence across space matters.

**Kenyan texture.** "Stima imepotea" (the power's gone), a whole street buying candles from the kiosk, a budget hotel guest register, the overseas-job scam that every Kenyan family has heard of.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** stima (electricity), kibanda / kiosk (small roadside shop).

**Images (5).** Portraits: Faith, Paul, Kennedy, Zawadi. Location: hotel reception lit only by a candle.

**Audit tags.** Culprit M, 40s, Embu-origin name, motive fraud exposure. Victim F, 20s, Kalenjin-origin name.

### Case 5 — The Long Rains

`case-005` · Nairobi CBD · 7 min · suspects 3 · chain 2 · herrings 0 · liars 0 · groups WHO

**OB entry.** OB 12/09/04, 15:31. A county gardener reports a newspaper vendor found collapsed under his kiosk awning at Jeevanjee Gardens after the afternoon downpour.

**Setting.** Jeevanjee Gardens, a Thursday in April. Heavy rain from 14:50 to about 15:30. The vendor's kiosk has a small tin awning.

**Victim.** **Patrick Njoroge**, 47, newspaper and airtime vendor. Struck once. **The ground beneath him is dry** while everything around is soaked.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bernard Langat | 50 | Suspect | Runs a small money-lending business; Patrick owed him KSh 10,000 | **Culprit** |
| Tony Kariuki | 22 | Suspect | Patrick's nephew; worked the kiosk; they'd quarrelled about wages | Innocent: at the newspaper depot |
| Fredrick Ouko | 38 | Suspect | Rival vendor who wanted Patrick's pitch | Innocent: in a Huduma Centre queue |
| Esther Muthoni | 61 | Witness | Regular customer | Innocent |
| Bakari Mwamba | 45 | Witness | County gardener who found him | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Bernard came at about 14:30 to collect. Patrick paid KSh 2,000 and asked for more time. Bernard lost his temper and hit him with the handle of his umbrella stand, a heavy steel one he carries. When the first drops fell at 14:50 he ran for the bus, leaving his umbrella behind.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_dryground | Physical | Under the body | Ground beneath Patrick is dry; the rain started at 14:50 (`ev_bakari`) → he fell before it began |
| ev_umbrella | Physical | Beside the kiosk | A closed black umbrella with a sticker: **"Langat Credit — Mikopo Haraka"** and a phone number |
| ev_esther | Witness | Customer | Bought airtime at 14:35; Patrick was fine; a man in a grey coat with a black umbrella was waiting beside the kiosk "like a man waiting to be paid" |
| ev_bakari | Witness | Gardener | Rain began at ten to three; he sheltered in the toilet block until 15:25, then found Patrick |
| ev_depot | Witness | Taifa depot dispatcher (statement only) | Tony Kariuki collected the Taifa Jioni bundle at 14:30 and waited for the second van until 15:05 |
| ev_huduma | Physical (found paper) | Fredrick Ouko's wallet (he shows you) | Huduma Centre queue ticket, number C-114, issued 13:58, served 15:21 |
| ev_ledger | Physical (found paper) | Patrick's kiosk drawer | A school exercise book: "Langat 10,000 — paid 2,000 today" in Patrick's hand, dated today |

**Proof**
1. `ev_dryground` + `ev_bakari` + `ev_esther` → Patrick was attacked between 14:35 and 14:50.
2. `ev_esther` + `ev_umbrella` + `ev_ledger` → the man waiting at the kiosk in that window was Bernard Langat, there to collect a debt, and he left his umbrella → **WHO = Bernard Langat**.

**Eliminations.** Tony Kariuki: `ev_depot` (14:30–15:05). Fredrick Ouko: `ev_huduma` (inside Huduma Centre 13:58–15:21). Esther Muthoni: left at 14:35 on the matatu she shows a fare receipt for (14:38, Jeevanjee–Kangemi). Bakari Mwamba: in the toilet block shelter with two other gardeners.

**Red herrings / twist.** None.

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Patrick Njoroge at Jeevanjee Gardens.` Person words: Bernard Langat, Tony Kariuki, Fredrick Ouko, Esther Muthoni, Bakari Mwamba (5).

**New interface beat.** **Narrowing a time window.** The notebook's time view shows each witness's times as bars; the player sees the 14:35–14:50 gap appear. This is the seed of the region-5 timeline rail.

**Kenyan texture.** The April long rains, the Taifa Jioni afternoon edition, Huduma Centre queue tickets, informal lenders ("mikopo haraka"), airtime sold at the kiosk.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** mikopo (loans), haraka (quick), Huduma Centre (government service centre), mvua (rain).

**Images (5).** Portraits: Patrick, Bernard, Tony, Fredrick. Location: Jeevanjee Gardens in rain, the kiosk under its awning.

**Audit tags.** Culprit M, 50s, Kalenjin-origin name, motive money/debt. Victim M, 40s, Kikuyu-origin name.

### Case 6 — Job Number 318

`case-006` · Nairobi CBD · 8 min · suspects 3 · chain 2 · herrings 0 · liars 0 · groups WHO · **spine background detail**

**OB entry.** OB 05/16/04, 13:42. An apprentice reports the technician at Signal Point electronics repair, Luthuli Avenue, found dead in the back room.

**Setting.** **Signal Point**, a fictional phone and radio repair shop on Luthuli Avenue. Front counter, a back room with a shelf of repaired items, each tied with a numbered paper tag. Narrow street, shops shoulder to shoulder.

**Victim.** **Joel Mutiso**, 34, repair technician. Struck from behind with a heavy transformer from the workbench.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wycliffe Barasa | 29 | Suspect | Customer; left a red radio for repair | **Culprit** |
| Simon Gakuru | 55 | Suspect | Shop owner; he and Joel disputed Joel's share of profits | Innocent: in Mombasa |
| Kelvin Njagi | 19 | Suspect | Apprentice; Joel had threatened to dismiss him | Innocent: at lunch |
| Esther Njoki | 33 | Witness | Customer whose blue radio (job 317) is still on the shelf | Innocent |
| Aisha Noor | 42 | Witness | Runs the phone-accessory shop next door | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Wycliffe was hiding stolen phone SIM trays and IMEI-changing chips inside his radio and paying Joel to "fix" it so it looked legitimate. On the day, Joel opened the radio, realised what he'd been part of, and said he'd go to the police. At about 13:05 Wycliffe came for the radio, they argued in the back room, and Wycliffe hit him. He tore the radio off the shelf, ripping the tag, and walked out at 13:10.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Back room | Struck from behind with a bench transformer |
| ev_tagstub | Physical | Shelf | A torn tag stub, **#318**, still tied to the shelf rail; the item is gone |
| ev_jobbook | Physical (found paper) | Counter | Job book: **#318 — red Philips radio — Wycliffe Barasa — "check inside!!"** in Joel's hand. #317 blue radio, Esther Njoki, still on shelf |
| ev_aisha | Witness | Next-door shop | Saw Joel alive at 12:50; at about 13:10 saw a young man leave quickly carrying a **red radio** |
| ev_ticket | Physical (found paper) | Simon Gakuru shows it | Bus ticket Nairobi–Mombasa, departed 21:00 the night before; he's calling from Mombasa |
| ev_kibanda | Witness | Kibanda owner (statement only) | Kelvin ate githeri at her kibanda on Accra Road 12:45–13:35 |
| ev_tray | Physical | Under the workbench | A loose SIM tray from a phone, not from any job in the book |
| ev_calendar | Physical | Shop wall | A calendar from **Mvua Holdings — Quick Loans · Title Searches · Till 880 214** (spine; not needed for this case) |

**Proof**
1. `ev_tagstub` + `ev_jobbook` → the item torn off the shelf was job #318, a red radio belonging to Wycliffe Barasa.
2. `ev_aisha` → the man who left at 13:10 was carrying a red radio → **WHO = Wycliffe Barasa**.

**Eliminations.** Simon Gakuru: `ev_ticket`. Kelvin Njagi: `ev_kibanda`. Esther Njoki: her radio is still on the shelf, and Aisha served her at 12:30 before she left for work. Aisha Noor: served customers continuously (her shop's sales book, 13:00 and 13:08 entries).

**Red herrings / twist.** None.

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Joel Mutiso at Signal Point.` Person words: Wycliffe Barasa, Simon Gakuru, Kelvin Njagi, Esther Njoki, Aisha Noor (5).

**New interface beat.** **Inspecting objects closely.** The shelf opens in a zoom view; tags can be flipped to read the number on the back. Teaches that small writing matters.

**Kenyan texture.** Luthuli Avenue's repair trade, paper job tags, githeri at a kibanda, the overnight Mombasa bus.

**Spine.** `ev_calendar` carries thread `t_mvua` with **Till 880 214**. Nothing points the player at it. When the Pattern File unlocks after case 10, this calendar is already pinned there (auto-filed per §4.7), and players who noticed it feel clever.

**Glossary.** githeri (maize and bean stew), kibanda (food stall).

**Images (5).** Portraits: Joel, Wycliffe, Simon, Kelvin. Location: Luthuli Avenue repair shop back room.

**Audit tags.** Culprit M, 20s, Luhya-origin name, motive cover-up (stolen goods). Victim M, 30s, Kamba-origin name.

### Case 7 — Pollen

`case-007` · Nairobi CBD · 8 min · suspects 3 · chain 2 · **herrings 1** · liars 0 · groups WHO

**OB entry.** OB 22/24/04, 12:19. A customer reports a florist found behind the curtain of her stall's cold room at City Market.

**Setting.** City Market off Muindi Mbingu Street, late morning. Flower stalls along one aisle, curio sellers along the next, butchers at the far end. Each stall has a licence number on a painted board.

**Victim.** **Beatrice Kerubo**, 39, florist (roses and carnations). Struck once with a flower-bucket stand. **Bright orange pollen stains** on the shoulder of her white blouse, as if someone grabbed her.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lucy Kagendo | 33 | Suspect | Lily and gerbera seller two stalls down; Beatrice had started undercutting her with cheap imported lilies | **Culprit** |
| Josphat Kimani | 45 | Suspect | Rose seller; **hands covered in fresh scratches** | Innocent (red herring) |
| Naliaka Simiyu | 50 | Suspect | Curio seller; loud argument with Beatrice that morning over aisle space | Innocent: at City Hall paying stall fees |
| Ahmed Yusuf | 48 | Witness | Butcher across the aisle | Innocent |
| Grace Adhiambo | 29 | Witness | Customer who found her | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Beatrice had got a cheap supply of lilies and was selling them at half Lucy's price. At about 11:50 Lucy came to her stall with a bucket of lilies to "talk", grabbed her by the shoulder when Beatrice laughed at her, and hit her with the bucket stand. Lily pollen came off Lucy's hands onto the blouse. Lucy went back to her stall and kept selling.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_pollen | Physical | Victim's blouse | Orange pollen stain shaped like fingers on the shoulder. Florists' saying: lily pollen stains everything and won't wash out |
| ev_stalls | Physical (found paper) | Market master's licence board | Stall list by product. **Only one stall sells lilies: Stall 41, L. Kagendo — Lilies & Gerberas**. Beatrice's stall 39: roses, carnations |
| ev_beatrice_stock | Physical | Beatrice's stall | Her cold room holds a new box of lilies, but **still sealed**, pollen-free: her lilies hadn't been opened yet |
| ev_lucy_hands | Witness | Ahmed Yusuf | Saw Lucy walk back to stall 41 at about 11:55 wiping her hands on her apron; her apron is orange-stained (you can see it in her portrait and on visiting her stall) |
| ev_grace | Witness | Customer | Beatrice sold her roses at 11:45; found her at 12:10 |
| ev_scratches | Physical | Josphat Kimani's hands (red herring) | Fresh scratches |
| ev_rose_thorns | Witness | Josphat Kimani's apprentice (statement only) | They de-thorned forty dozen roses that morning for a wedding order; everyone on the rose stall has scratches today |
| ev_church | Witness | All Saints Cathedral verger (statement only) | Josphat delivered the wedding flowers there 11:30–12:15 |
| ev_fees | Physical (found paper) | Naliaka's receipt | City Hall stall-fee receipt timed 12:02, queue started 11:20 (her queue number slip) |

**Proof**
1. `ev_pollen` + `ev_beatrice_stock` → the pollen didn't come from Beatrice's own stock; her lilies were still sealed. The attacker had lily pollen on their hands.
2. `ev_stalls` + `ev_lucy_hands` → only Lucy Kagendo handles lilies in the market, and she was seen wiping orange-stained hands coming back from that direction just after the attack → **WHO = Lucy Kagendo**.

**Eliminations.** Josphat Kimani: `ev_church` (at the cathedral 11:30–12:15); his scratches are explained by `ev_rose_thorns`. Naliaka Simiyu: `ev_fees`. Ahmed Yusuf: serving at his counter (two customers' statements in Grace's notes). Grace Adhiambo: arrived 11:45 and left, returned 12:10 (her fare receipt).

**Red herrings / twist.** **First red herring of the campaign:** the scratched hands. Rule: every red herring has an innocent explanation the player can find. The verdict reconstruction explicitly shows the scratches being explained, so players learn the game plays fair.

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Beatrice Kerubo at City Market.` Person words: Lucy Kagendo, Josphat Kimani, Naliaka Simiyu, Ahmed Yusuf, Grace Adhiambo (5).

**New interface beat.** **The first hint call.** If the player submits a wrong name once, Mwalimu's number lights up on the desk phone for the first time, and the three hint tiers are explained by her in one sentence each. (Hints exist from case 1; this is the first time the game *offers* one.)

**Kenyan texture.** City Market's flower aisle, stall licences, a wedding order for a cathedral, imported cut flowers undercutting local sellers.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** soko (market), harusi (wedding).

**Images (6).** Portraits: Beatrice, Lucy, Josphat, Naliaka. Location: City Market flower aisle. Evidence photo: the pollen-stained blouse shoulder (no body in frame).

**Audit tags.** Culprit F, 30s, Meru-origin name, motive business rivalry. Victim F, 30s, Kisii-origin name.

### Case 8 — The 18:10 to Embakasi

`case-008` · Nairobi CBD · 9 min · suspects 3 · chain 2 · herrings 0 · liars 0 · groups WHO

**OB entry.** OB 30/02/05, 18:57. A platform porter reports the owner of a tea kiosk at Nairobi Railway Station found in the kiosk storeroom.

**Setting.** Nairobi Railway Station, evening commuter rush. Fictional **Stesheni Tea Kiosk** on platform 2, with a storeroom behind it. Commuter trains to Embakasi and Syokimau (times fictional, printed on a timetable board).

**Victim.** **Elijah Onyango**, 58, co-owner of the kiosk, retired railway clerk. Struck with a crate of empty soda bottles.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dorcas Moraa | 37 | Suspect | His business partner in the kiosk; he planned to buy her out cheaply | **Culprit** |
| Felix Wanyonyi | 40 | Suspect | Porter; Elijah had accused him of stealing stock | Innocent: in the parcels office |
| Kamal Shah | 50 | Suspect | Bread and milk supplier; Elijah owed him for three months | Innocent: left by the gate at 17:45 |
| Janet Achieng | 28 | Witness | Ticket window clerk | Innocent |
| Musa Ngala | 63 | Witness | Ticket inspector on the 18:10 train | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Elijah told Dorcas that afternoon that he'd found a buyer for his half and would sell hers too, since her name wasn't on the original licence. She bought her usual ticket home for the 18:10 at 17:52, then went back to the storeroom to argue. At about 18:05 she struck him with a bottle crate. In the struggle her ticket fell from her pocket. She missed the train and walked out to catch a matatu.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Storeroom | Struck with a crate of empties |
| ev_ticket | Physical | Storeroom floor | Commuter ticket: **18:10 Nairobi–Embakasi**, sold at **window 3, 17:52**, **unpunched** |
| ev_timetable | Physical | Platform board | The 18:10 Embakasi train left at 18:12. Inspectors punch every ticket on board between Nairobi and Makadara |
| ev_janet | Witness | Window 3 clerk | "Dorcas buys an 18:10 ticket every weekday. Today too, about ten to six." |
| ev_musa | Witness | Inspector | Didn't see Dorcas on the 18:10, though she rides it every day and always greets him |
| ev_parcels | Physical (found paper) | Parcels office logbook | Felix Wanyonyi signed parcels in at 17:58, 18:04, 18:15, 18:22 |
| ev_gate | Physical (found paper) | Station gate vehicle log | Shah's van out at 17:45 |
| ev_licence | Physical (found paper) | Kiosk drawer | Kiosk licence in Elijah's name only; a note: "Buyer Tuesday. Tell D." |

**Proof**
1. `ev_ticket` + `ev_janet` → the ticket in the storeroom was bought by Dorcas at 17:52.
2. `ev_timetable` + `ev_musa` → it was never punched, so Dorcas never boarded the 18:10; her ticket ended up on the storeroom floor instead → **WHO = Dorcas Moraa**. (`ev_licence` supports motive.)

**Eliminations.** Felix Wanyonyi: `ev_parcels`. Kamal Shah: `ev_gate` (gone 20 minutes before). Janet Achieng: at window 3 serving the queue the whole time (ticket sequence numbers). Musa Ngala: on the 18:10 train from 18:12.

**Red herrings / twist.** None.

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Elijah Onyango at the Railway Station.` Person words: Dorcas Moraa, Felix Wanyonyi, Kamal Shah, Janet Achieng, Musa Ngala (5).

**New interface beat.** **Reading a timetable.** First code-drawn schedule board; tapping a train row shows which facts it touches. Also first time an *absence* of something (no punch hole) is the clue, a small preview of region 8.

**Kenyan texture.** Commuter rail at rush hour, punched tickets, the inspector who knows every regular, a kiosk licence in one name only.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** stesheni (station), tiketi (ticket).

**Images (5).** Portraits: Elijah, Dorcas, Felix, Kamal. Location: Nairobi Railway Station platform at dusk.

**Audit tags.** Culprit F, 30s, Kisii-origin name, motive business partnership dispute (rivalry). Victim M, 50s, Luo-origin name.

### Case 9 — The Obvious Man

`case-009` · Nairobi CBD · 10 min · suspects 3 · **chain 3** · **herrings 1** · liars 0 · groups WHO · **twist: the obvious suspect is innocent**

**OB entry.** OB 16/11/05, 17:20. A rowing-boat attendant found dead in the boat shed at Uhuru Park. Witnesses report a public fight with his brother that morning.

**Setting.** Uhuru Park boating lake, a Sunday. Fictional **Ziwani Boat Hire**: a shed, a fee book, a cash tin, attendants in **blue** overalls, the manager in a **green** one. Park photographers sell instant prints to families.

**Victim.** **Charles Maina**, 44, senior attendant. Struck with an oar. Cash tin missing.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Daniel ole Sankale | 39 | Suspect | Boat-hire manager; has been skimming hire fees | **Culprit** |
| George Maina | 41 | Suspect | Charles's brother; screamed at him over their mother's plot that morning; **his cap was found in the shed** | Innocent (the obvious man) |
| Dennis Mbugua | 23 | Suspect | Junior attendant | Innocent: on the water |
| Mama Pendo (Pendo Atieno) | 55 | Witness | Ice-cream seller by the lake | Innocent |
| Victor Nyamweya | 31 | Witness | Park photographer | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Charles had been checking the fee book against the cash tin for three weeks and found it short every Sunday. He wrote "D — 3 Sundays short" in pencil on the back page and told the manager he'd report it to the owner on Monday. At about 16:10, while Dennis was out on the lake retrieving a boat, Daniel struck him with an oar in the shed and took the tin to make it look like a robbery. George's cap had been lying in the shed since the morning fight.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_cap | Physical | Shed | George Maina's cap (red herring) |
| ev_pendo | Witness | Ice-cream seller | Saw George storm out of the shed **bareheaded at 09:15** after shouting at Charles; never saw him come back. Saw Charles alive at 15:55 |
| ev_gikomba | Witness | Gikomba trader (statement only) | George was at his mitumba stall in Gikomba from 11:00 until 18:00; she watched his stall while he went to the toilet, five minutes |
| ev_feebook | Physical (found paper) | Shed | Day's hire tickets: 46. The back page in pencil: **"D — 3 Sundays short."** |
| ev_photo | Physical (found paper) | Bought from Victor | Instant print of a family, time-stamped on the back **16:12** by the photographer. In the background: the shed door open and **a man in a green overall** walking away carrying a grey box |
| ev_uniforms | Witness | Victor (who has photographed the park for years) | "Attendants wear blue. Only the manager wears green." |
| ev_dennis | Witness | Pendo | Dennis was rowing out to bring back a drifting boat from 16:00 to 16:25; she watched the whole thing because the children were cheering |
| ev_tin | Physical | Found later in the manager's office cupboard | The cash tin, empty |

**Proof**
1. `ev_pendo` + `ev_gikomba` → George left at 09:15 bareheaded and was in Gikomba all afternoon; the cap was left in the morning and means nothing.
2. `ev_feebook` → Charles suspected someone with the initial **D** of taking money: either Daniel ole Sankale or Dennis Mbugua.
3. `ev_photo` + `ev_uniforms` + `ev_dennis` → at 16:12 a man in the manager's green overall left the shed with a box; Dennis was on the water → **WHO = Daniel ole Sankale**. (`ev_tin` confirms.)

**Eliminations.** George Maina: step 1. Dennis Mbugua: `ev_dennis` (and he wears blue). Pendo Atieno: at her cart in full view of the lake. Victor Nyamweya: taking photographs of families 15:30–17:00 (his print numbers run in sequence).

**Red herrings / twist.** **First twist.** The OB entry, the cap and the morning fight all point at George. The reconstruction ends with George collecting his cap, a small moment that teaches the region-2 lesson: suspicion isn't evidence.

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Charles Maina at Uhuru Park.` Person words: Daniel ole Sankale, George Maina, Dennis Mbugua, Pendo Atieno, Victor Nyamweya (5).

**New interface beat.** **A three-step proof.** The notebook's "pinned facts" tray is introduced: the player can pin up to six facts at the top while working. Also the first **photograph** shown with the case-photo treatment at full size, with zoom.

**Kenyan texture.** Sunday at Uhuru Park, rowing boats and ice cream, park photographers with instant prints, a family land dispute (mentioned only, foreshadowing region 4), Gikomba mitumba trade.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** mitumba (second-hand clothes), shamba (plot of farmland), ziwa (lake), mama (respectful address for an older woman).

**Images (6).** Portraits: Charles, Daniel, George, Dennis. Location: Uhuru Park boating lake. Evidence photo: the instant print (a family in front of the lake, with the green-overall figure in the background, small and turned away).

**Audit tags.** Culprit M, 30s, Maasai-origin name, motive cover-up (theft). Victim M, 40s, Kikuyu-origin name. *Note: this is the only Maasai-named culprit allowed before region 6, where Maasai characters will be cast mainly as rangers, guides and witnesses.*

### Case 10 — BOSS: The Printer of River Road

`case-010` · Nairobi CBD · **boss** · 12 min · suspects 4 · chain 3 · herrings 1 · liars 0 · groups WHO (two blanks) · **twist: the killer is on no customer list** · **spine group: first**

**OB entry.** OB 08/23/05, 19:48. An apprentice reports his employer, owner of Omar Printers & Rubber Stamps on River Road, found dead in the shop, drawers ransacked.

**Setting.** River Road, Friday evening: printing shops, sign writers, rubber-stamp makers, wedding-card printers, all lit, all busy. Fictional **Omar Printers & Rubber Stamps**: front counter, a back room with a stamp-making bench, an order book, a carbon collection-slip book.

**Victim.** **Rashid Omar Bakari**, 56, printer and rubber-stamp maker for 30 years. Struck with a stamp press handle. Drawers pulled out. One drawer, labelled "Mvua — Friday", is empty.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tom Ochieng | 31 | Suspect (appears late) | Courier for fictional **Haraka Couriers**; came to collect an order | **Culprit** |
| Hillary Kosgei | 35 | Suspect | Customer; his wedding cards were misprinted; shouted at Rashid at 17:00 in front of the street | Innocent (red herring) |
| Elizabeth Achola | 49 | Suspect | Owner of the print shop next door; in a rent dispute with Rashid | Innocent: serving customers |
| Juma Mwakio | 19 | Suspect | Rashid's apprentice; found the body | Innocent: delivering cards in Ngara |
| Abdullahi Gure | 64 | Witness | River Road night askari for the row of shops | Innocent |
| Mama Juma (Zuhura Mwakio) | 46 | Witness | Juma's mother; the Ngara client | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Three weeks earlier, a client calling itself **Mvua Holdings** paid a deposit by till for a "replica" stamp: a seal reading **REGISTRAR OF TITLES**. Rashid made the blank, then looked closer at the proof and realised it was meant to forge land titles. He refused to finish it. At 19:00 a courier came to collect. Rashid, who insists on taking the ID number of anyone collecting an official-looking stamp, wrote down the courier's name and ID on the collection slip, then wrote "REFUSED" and the time, 19:02. The courier had orders not to leave without it. They argued in the back room; the courier struck Rashid, emptied the Mvua drawer (the half-finished stamp, the proof and the deposit receipt) and ransacked the other drawers to make it look like a robbery. He missed two things: the carbon copy of the collection slip, and the note from Mvua that Rashid had tucked into the order book.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Back room | Struck with a stamp-press handle; drawers ransacked; cash box **untouched** under the counter (KSh 18,400) |
| ev_drawer | Physical | Back room | Drawer labelled "Mvua — Friday", empty |
| ev_orderbook | Physical (found paper) | Counter | Order book, three weeks ago: **"Replica seal — REGISTRAR OF TITLES — client: Mvua Holdings — deposit by Till 880 214 — collect Fri 19:00 by messenger."** Other clients this month: Kilele House Management, St. Teresa's Church Ngara, Tana Express, a wedding (H. Kosgei) |
| ev_slip | Physical (found paper) | Carbon copy under the order book | Collection slip: **"Mvua order. Collector: Tom Ochieng, ID 2xxxxxxx (fictional), Haraka Couriers. 19:02 — REFUSED. Told him I won't finish it."** |
| ev_note | Physical (found paper) | Tucked inside the order book | Handwritten on a plain card: **"Kivuli wants it Friday. No excuses."** |
| ev_abdullahi | Witness | Night askari | At about 19:20 a man in a **yellow Haraka Couriers rain jacket** came out of Omar Printers with a brown A4 envelope and walked fast towards Tom Mboya Street |
| ev_achola_sales | Physical (found paper) | Elizabeth Achola's carbon receipt book (she shows you) | Sales at 19:00, 19:08, 19:14, 19:20; customers waiting the whole time |
| ev_delivery | Physical (found paper) | Juma's delivery note | Wedding cards delivered to Z. Mwakio, Ngara, **signed 19:15** |
| ev_kosgei_ticket | Physical (found paper) | Hillary Kosgei (cooperative, angry, but cooperative) | Coach ticket Nairobi–Eldoret, departed 17:45; he calls from Nakuru |
| ev_kosgei_scene | Witness | Abdullahi | Hillary shouted at Rashid at 17:00 and left; the whole street saw (red herring) |

**Proof**
1. `ev_body` + `ev_drawer` → the robbery was staged: the cash was left, and the only drawer that was emptied, not just pulled out, was the Mvua order.
2. `ev_orderbook` + `ev_slip` → the Mvua order was due for collection at 19:00, and the collector who came at 19:02 and was refused was **Tom Ochieng** of Haraka Couriers.
3. `ev_abdullahi` → a man in a Haraka Couriers jacket left the shop at 19:20 carrying an envelope, inside the window between the refusal and the body being found → **WHO = Tom Ochieng**; **for = Mvua Holdings** (from `ev_orderbook` + `ev_slip` + `ev_drawer`).

**Eliminations.**
- *Killer blank:* Hillary Kosgei: `ev_kosgei_ticket` (on the 17:45 coach). Elizabeth Achola: `ev_achola_sales`. Juma Mwakio: `ev_delivery` + his mother's statement. Abdullahi Gure: on his rounds, seen by Elizabeth's customers at 19:08 and 19:14.
- *Client blank:* Kilele House Management, St. Teresa's Church, Tana Express and H. Kosgei all had ordinary orders already collected or not due (`ev_orderbook`). Only the Mvua order was due at 19:00 and is missing.

**Red herrings / twist.**
- Red herring: Hillary Kosgei's public shouting at 17:00.
- Twist: the killer isn't anyone with a grudge. He's a courier the player only discovers from the carbon slip, and he was there on someone else's errand.
- Spine twist: the "client" isn't a person, it's a company, and behind it is a name in a handwritten note.

**Charge sheet.** One WHO group, two blanks, both must be right:

> `{who} killed Rashid Omar Bakari when he refused to finish a stamp ordered by {client}.`

- Person words (killer blank): Tom Ochieng, Hillary Kosgei, Elizabeth Achola, Juma Mwakio, Abdullahi Gure (5).
- Client words: Mvua Holdings, Kilele House Management, St. Teresa's Church Ngara, Tana Express (4). The callbacks to cases 2 and 3 are deliberate: the order book is full of the region's history.
- Combinations: 5 × 4 = 20 (above the region-1 minimum of 4).
- Halima's lines. Pass: *"Ochieng carried it out. But he didn't order it. Who is Mvua Holdings?"* Fail on either blank: *"A courier doesn't kill over a parcel unless someone is waiting for it. Look again."*

**Spine group.** This is the first spine group, so it stays gentle: the `{client}` blank *is* the spine group. It's solved from this case's evidence, not from the Pattern File yet. From case 20 onwards, spine groups need earlier cases.

**After the verdict.**
- Reconstruction: Tom Ochieng, arrested at the Haraka depot, says one word to Amani: *"Kivuli."* Then nothing.
- The **Pattern File unlocks** (§4.4). It opens with three pins already on it: the Mvua deposit till **880 214** from this case, the Mvua calendar from **case 6** with the same till, and the note "Kivuli wants it Friday". The first time the player opens it, the two till numbers are side by side. Mwalimu's voice-note: *"You've seen that number before. Write it down somewhere I can't see it."*
- **Collectible:** Rashid's own brass shop stamp, *Omar Printers — River Road*, given to Amani by Juma. It sits on the desk from now on and stamps the player's charge sheets in every later case.

**New interface beat.** **Two blanks in one group** (preparing for multi-group sheets), the **Pattern File**, and the **desk collectible** system.

**Kenyan texture.** River Road's printing trade on a Friday night, rubber-stamp culture and why every Kenyan office needs one, carbon collection slips, ID numbers written down at the counter, courier companies, the land-title forgery pattern the whole spine runs on.

**Spine.** Threads `t_mvua` (till 880 214), `t_stamp` (REGISTRAR OF TITLES seal), `t_kivuli` (the note). All three auto-file.

**Glossary.** kivuli (shadow), mvua (rain), haraka (fast), muhuri (rubber stamp / seal), fundi (craftsman; foreshadows the enforcer's nickname without naming him).

**Images (8).** Portraits: Rashid, Tom Ochieng (taken at arrest, later reused in case 50), Hillary, Elizabeth, Juma. Locations: River Road at night; the back room with the stamp bench. Evidence photo: the empty "Mvua — Friday" drawer.

**Audit tags.** Culprit M, 30s, Luo-origin name, motive commissioned (spine). Victim M, 50s, Coastal/Swahili-origin name.

## Open questions for the cultural reader (region 1)

1. The OB number format and how a Nairobi station actually writes OB entries.
2. Whether a stage marshal's tally book at Ngara would realistically record parked vehicles by plate.
3. Sacco jacket colours (maroon for drivers, green for conductors are invented for the game; check they don't belong to a real sacco).
4. Sheng register in case 1 and case 3 dialogue.
5. Whether "Mama Pendo" and "Mama Juma" are natural forms of address in those settings (they are common, but check tone).
6. Name-origin tags for all 50 named characters in this region.

## Part C — Region 2: Eastlands (cases 11–20)

**Region frame.** Late May through the cold months of June and July. Amani leaves the CBD for the estates east of the city: Kayole, Jericho, Eastleigh, Umoja, Gikomba, Mathare, Pipeline, Dandora, Kamukunji, Komarock. Close-knit places where everyone saw something and not everyone says so. People start lying to Amani here. Halima starts texting after verdicts ("Clean file. Again."). Mwalimu's voice-notes shift from instructions to questions.

### C1. Region 2 rules

- **Interrogation arrives (case 11).** Each person has a statement sheet of claims. The player can ask about topics for free, or **press** a claim by presenting one fact. A correct press stamps the claim BROKEN and the person reacts. A wrong press costs one credibility stamp.
- **Credibility stamps arrive (case 11).** 5 per case. Wrong press −1, wrong charge submission −1 (plus the star penalty, §2.9). At zero the case continues; the superior takes over and the case is capped at 1 star.
- **Search warrants arrive (case 12).** Cost 1 stamp. The warrant button only appears once the player holds a **probable-cause fact** (a witness saw the person with the item, a document links them to it). This teaches that warrants need grounds, as in real procedure.
- **Exactly one liar per case.** The liar can be the culprit (cases 11, 12, 13, 15, 18, 19, 20), an innocent hiding something else (case 14), a false confessor (case 16) or someone covering for a friend (case 17). Lying is never proof of guilt on its own. Mwalimu says this out loud the first time it happens.
- **Stances:** cooperative and guarded only. Guarded people give their claims only when shown a relevant piece of evidence. Lawyered-up suspects wait until region 7.
- **Evidence types:** still physical (including found paper) and witness. Phone and mobile-money records start in region 3. Paper receipts printed by a till are found paper, so the spine's till number can still appear.
- **Credibility path:** every card lists the stamps the cheapest correct route costs. Validator rule 3 caps this at 3; region 2 never needs more than 1.

**Rule 9 amendment (flagged for the design doc).** Rule 9 as written asks for at least 12 possible combinations per group in regions 2–5. A single-blank WHO group would need 12 names in the bank, which bloats every case with filler people. The amended rule: a **single-blank group needs at least 5 options** in every region; a **multi-blank group needs at least 12** (regions 2–5) or **30** (regions 6–10). From region 2, every wrong guess also costs a credibility stamp, so guessing through 5 names costs an expected 2 stamps and a star. That's enough to make reasoning the cheaper route. I've applied this to the design doc §3.5.

### Case 11 — Number Seven

`case-011` · Eastlands · 10 min · suspects 3 · chain 2 · herrings 0 · liars 1 (culprit) · groups WHO · stamps needed 0

**OB entry.** OB 27/26/05, 21:04. A roast-maize seller reports a boda-boda rider found face down in the new drainage trench beside the Kayole Spine Road stage.

**Setting.** Kayole Spine Road boda-boda stage, a Monday night in late May. A row of motorbikes, riders in numbered reflective vests, a phone-charging and mandazi kiosk, a roast-maize brazier. The county is digging a drainage trench along the road; the stage ground is red murram, the trench floor is **grey clay**.

**Victim.** **Erick Odongo**, 32, boda rider, vest **No. 7**. Struck on the head, fell or was pushed into the trench. His bike is still parked at the stage with the key in it.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sharon Nanjala | 26 | Suspect | Runs the phone-charging and mandazi kiosk; Erick's ex-girlfriend; she co-signed the loan on his motorbike and he stopped paying, so the lender has been taking her things | **Culprit** |
| Jackson Mutuku | 47 | Suspect | Stage chairman; fined Erick last week over unpaid stage fees | Innocent: at the chief's baraza |
| Abednego Kerich | 30 | Suspect | Rival rider; fought Erick over customers on Sunday | Innocent: on a trip to Fedha |
| Teresia Ndunge | 51 | Witness | Roast-maize seller; found him | Innocent |
| Peninah Chelimo | 23 | Witness (statement only) | Petrol-station attendant in Fedha | Innocent |

**What really happened.** The lender's agents took Sharon's fridge that morning. At 20:15 Erick came to her kiosk to charge his phone as if nothing had happened. They shouted about the loan; he laughed and walked off towards the trench to relieve himself. She followed him in her gumboots, hit him with the kiosk's iron charcoal-jiko poker, and he fell into the trench. She climbed out, closed the kiosk, put the poker back and went home. Her boots carried the trench clay with her.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Trench | Struck on the side of the head; lying in grey clay |
| ev_signboard | Physical | County board at the trench | "Drainage works. Grey clay subsoil exposed. Keep off." The stage and road are red murram; grey clay exists only inside the trench |
| ev_prints | Physical | Trench floor beside the body | Small gumboot prints, a chevron tread, about size 37, going in and climbing out |
| ev_chargelog | Physical (found paper) | Sharon's kiosk | Her exercise book of phone charges at KSh 20: entries at 19:40, 20:10 and **20:25** in her handwriting |
| ev_gumboots | Physical | Inside Sharon's kiosk | Yellow gumboots, size 37, chevron tread, **grey clay to the ankle** |
| ev_poker | Physical | Kiosk, by the jiko | Iron poker, recently wiped; a smear of grey clay on the handle |
| ev_teresia | Witness | Maize seller | Sold Erick a maize cob at 20:20; heard a shout and a thud from the trench about 20:35, thought it was a drunk; found him at 20:52 when she went to tip out her ash |
| ev_baraza | Physical (found paper) | Chief's office | Baraza attendance sheet on stage fees, 19:00–21:00; J. Mutuku signed in 18:55; the minutes record him speaking at 20:30 |
| ev_fuel | Physical (found paper) | Abednego Kerich shows it | Fuel receipt, Petro Mashariki Fedha, **20:28**, plate of his bike |
| ev_peninah | Witness | Attendant | Remembers Abednego because he paid in coins; he left Fedha with a passenger heading further out |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sharon Nanjala | Cooperative | "Erick owed me money. Everyone knows that." / **"I closed the kiosk at half past seven and went home to Kayole Junction."** | Second claim | `ev_chargelog` (she wrote entries at 20:10 and 20:25) | *"Fine. I stayed. He came at quarter past eight and we shouted about the loan. He walked off to the trench. I locked up and went home. That's all."* (new fact: she was at the kiosk with Erick after 20:15) |
| Jackson Mutuku | Cooperative | "I was at the chief's baraza all evening." | True | — | Topic "Erick": the stage-fee fine; topic "Sharon": "That boy ruined her. The loan people took her fridge today." |
| Abednego Kerich | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_body` or `ev_teresia`) | "I took a customer to Fedha at eight." | True | — | Shows `ev_fuel` |

**Proof**
1. Sharon's claim + `ev_chargelog` → she was at the stage after 20:25, inside the window `ev_teresia` sets (20:20–20:35), and admits Erick was with her at 20:15.
2. `ev_signboard` + `ev_prints` + `ev_gumboots` → the person who went into the trench wore size-37 chevron gumboots and came out with grey clay that exists only in the trench; Sharon's boots carry it → **WHO = Sharon Nanjala**. (`ev_poker` supports.)

**Eliminations.** Jackson Mutuku: `ev_baraza`. Abednego Kerich: `ev_fuel` + `ev_peninah` (Fedha at 20:28, about 25 minutes away at night). Teresia Ndunge: at her brazier serving customers (two regulars mentioned in her statement); her own shoes are open sandals with murram dust, no clay.

**Red herrings / twist.** None. The rival rider's Sunday fight is mentioned to give the player a second plausible target to press.

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Erick Odongo at the Kayole stage.` Person words: Sharon Nanjala, Jackson Mutuku, Abednego Kerich, Teresia Ndunge, Peninah Chelimo (5).

**Credibility path.** 0 stamps. A wrong press (for example, presenting `ev_fuel` against Sharon's claim) costs 1 and teaches the cost.

**New interface beat.** **Pressing a claim.** The statement sheet appears with claims as typed lines; the player drags a fact card onto a claim. Correct press: a red BROKEN stamp thumps down, a beat of silence, then the reaction. Wrong press: a stamp is torn off the folder. Mwalimu's voice-note before the case explains it in two sentences.

**Kenyan texture.** Boda-boda stages and numbered vests, motorbike loans with co-signers and repossession, phone-charging kiosks, mandazi and roast maize, a chief's baraza on stage fees, county road works.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** boda-boda (motorbike taxi), mandazi (fried dough), baraza (public meeting at the chief's office), jiko (charcoal stove), mahindi choma (roast maize).

**Images (5).** Portraits: Erick, Sharon (yellow gumboots visible), Jackson, Abednego. Location: Kayole stage at night with the trench and county signboard.

**Audit tags.** Culprit F, 20s, Luhya-origin name, motive money/debt. Victim M, 30s, Luo-origin name.

### Case 12 — Rent Day

`case-012` · Eastlands · 11 min · suspects 3 · chain 2 · herrings 0 · liars 1 (culprit) · groups WHO · stamps needed 1 (warrant)

**OB entry.** OB 14/05/06, 18:31. The night watchman of Baraka Flats, Jericho, reports the caretaker found in the ground-floor rent office.

**Setting.** **Baraka Flats**, a fictional five-storey walk-up in Jericho estate. One gate with a watchman's stool and gate book; a ground-floor rent office; 20 flats. The 5th of the month: rent day.

**Victim.** **Margaret Wangila**, 45, caretaker for 11 years. Struck with the office's heavy metal date stamp. The **rent book** (a blue hard-cover carbon receipt book with the tenant ledger in its front pages) is missing. The day's cash, KSh 64,000 in an envelope in the drawer, is **untouched**.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mwita Chacha | 64 | Suspect | Tenant, flat 4C; retired railway clerk; three months behind on rent; an auctioneer's distress notice on his door | **Culprit** |
| Lydia Anyango | 28 | Suspect | Tenant, flat 1B; screamed at Margaret on Monday about the water rationing | Innocent: at the salon |
| Wilson Kiprono | 39 | Suspect | Plumber fixing the tank; Margaret refused to pay his last invoice | Innocent: left at 17:41 |
| Bonface Mutinda | 58 | Witness | Night watchman | Innocent |
| Janeth Kwamboka | 34 | Witness (statement only) | Salon owner, Jericho market | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Margaret told Mwita on Saturday that the auctioneers would take his furniture on Monday. He'd been a tenant for 19 years. On rent day, at about 18:00, he went into the office to beg again. She refused. He hit her with the date stamp, panicked, took the rent book because his arrears were written in it, and carried it upstairs under his jacket. That night he tore a blank receipt from the back of the book and wrote himself a receipt for "Jan–Mar, paid in full".

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Rent office | Struck with the metal date stamp, which is on the floor; the rent book's shelf slot is empty |
| ev_cash | Physical | Drawer | Envelope "5th — rent cash", KSh 64,000, untouched → whoever did this came for the book, not the money |
| ev_lydia_receipt | Physical (found paper) | Lydia shows it | Receipt **No. 0471**, today, **17:20**, KSh 9,500, signed by Margaret |
| ev_gatebook | Physical (found paper) | Gate | "17:41 — plumber W. Kiprono out." Watchman's note: "Mama Margaret walked him to the gate." No other entries until 18:20 |
| ev_bonface | Witness | Watchman | Margaret walked the plumber out at 17:41 and went back to her office. Between 17:41 and 18:10 **nobody came through the gate in either direction**. The only tenant home that evening was Mzee Mwita; everyone else works late on the 5th. At **18:10** he saw Mzee Mwita go up the stairs "with a big blue book under his jacket" **(probable cause for a warrant)** |
| ev_notice | Physical (found paper) | Door of flat 4C | Auctioneer's notice of distress for rent: arrears January–March, KSh 27,000; goods to be attached in seven days |
| ev_mwita_receipt | Physical (found paper) | Mwita shows it when asked | Receipt **No. 0498**, dated last Saturday, "Jan–Mar paid in full, KSh 27,000", signed with a scrawl |
| ev_rentbook | Physical, **warrant** | Under the mattress in flat 4C | The missing rent book. Carbons run in order: Saturday's receipts are **0455–0462**; today's last receipt is **0471** (Lydia, 17:20). Carbons **0472–0500 are blank**, and the original of **0498 has been torn out of the back with no carbon behind it**. The ledger page for 4C reads "Jan, Feb, Mar — UNPAID — FINAL NOTICE" in Margaret's hand |
| ev_janeth | Witness | Salon owner | Lydia was in her chair for braids from 17:30 until after 19:00 |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mwita Chacha | Cooperative | **"I paid all my arrears on Saturday. Margaret gave me a receipt."** (shows `ev_mwita_receipt`) / "Nineteen years I have lived in 4C. I have never been late until this year." | First claim | `ev_rentbook` (on Saturday the book only reached 0462; 0498 was torn out blank and filled in by hand) | *"...I took the book. Nineteen years in that flat. But she was already lying there when I went in, I swear it."* (new fact: he was in the office at about 18:05) |
| Lydia Anyango | Cooperative | "I paid my rent at twenty past five and went to get my hair done." | True | — | Topic "Margaret": the water rationing fight. Shows `ev_lydia_receipt` |
| Wilson Kiprono | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_gatebook`) | "She walked me out herself." | True | — | Topic "invoice": she'd promised to pay on the 10th |

**Proof**
1. Mwita's receipt claim + `ev_rentbook` → his receipt is forged from the back of the stolen book; he had the book, and admits being in the office at about 18:05.
2. `ev_gatebook` + `ev_bonface` → Margaret was alive at 17:41, nobody entered or left the compound until 18:20, and the only person inside was Mwita, who was seen at 18:10 carrying the book → **WHO = Mwita Chacha**. His story that she was "already lying there" can't be true: nobody else was inside to have done it.

**Eliminations.** Wilson Kiprono: `ev_gatebook` + `ev_bonface` (Margaret was alive and walked him out). Lydia Anyango: `ev_janeth`. Bonface Mutinda: at the gate the whole time (two passing tenants' statements see him at 18:20 when they arrive). Janeth Kwamboka: at her salon.

**Red herrings / twist.** None. The cash left behind is a fair early pointer that the book was the target.

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Margaret Wangila at Baraka Flats.` Person words: Mwita Chacha, Lydia Anyango, Wilson Kiprono, Bonface Mutinda, Janeth Kwamboka (5).

**Credibility path.** 1 stamp: the warrant for flat 4C. Without it, the book never surfaces and Mwita's claim can't be broken.

**New interface beat.** **The search warrant.** Once `ev_bonface` is read, a warrant form slides onto the desk with Mwita's name, address and the grounds pre-typed from the fact. Spending a stamp: the duty magistrate's signature writes itself in, and a new location ("Flat 4C — search") opens on the map. Searching uses the same hotspot interface as a scene.

**Kenyan texture.** Rent day on the 5th, caretakers who've run a building for a decade, carbon rent books, auctioneers' distress notices, water rationing in Eastlands, braids at the estate salon.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** caretaker (building manager), madalali (agent/auctioneer's man), mzee.

**Images (5).** Portraits: Margaret, Mwita, Lydia, Wilson. Location: Baraka Flats courtyard and gate at dusk.

**Audit tags.** Culprit M, 60s, Kuria-origin name, motive land/property (eviction). Victim F, 40s, Luhya-origin name.

### Case 13 — Barwaqo Mall

`case-013` · Eastlands · 12 min · suspects 3 · chain 3 · herrings 0 · liars 1 (culprit) · groups WHO · stamps needed 0 · **spine background detail**

**OB entry.** OB 33/11/06, 19:12. A tea seller reports a fabric wholesaler found in her stall's storage cubicle at Barwaqo Mall, First Avenue, Eastleigh.

**Setting.** **Barwaqo Mall**, a fictional four-floor wholesale mall on First Avenue, Eastleigh: corridors of fabric and clothing stalls, porters with handcarts in the lanes outside, Somali tea sellers walking the floors with flasks. Closing time 19:00. A bank branch on the ground floor with its hours painted on the glass: **Mon–Fri 08:30–16:00**.

**Victim.** **Hodan Farah**, 34, wholesaler of printed fabric, stall 2-14. Struck with a steel bale hook in her storage cubicle.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Josephine Mueni | 52 | Suspect | Retailer from Machakos who buys on credit and pays by bank deposit slip | **Culprit** |
| Abdirahman Mohamed | 44 | Suspect | Hodan's cousin and co-owner of the stall; they were in a dispute over her late father's share | Innocent: at prayers |
| Rajesh Patel | 58 | Suspect | Fabric importer who supplies Hodan; they argued about prices | Innocent: at his godown |
| Fatuma Ali | 49 | Witness | Tea seller on the 2nd floor | Innocent |
| Lameck Onyancha | 33 | Witness | Handcart porter | Innocent |
| Sheikh Ibrahim Hassan | 66 | Witness (statement only) | Imam of the mosque on 6th Street | Innocent |

**What really happened.** For two months Josephine had paid Hodan with forged bank deposit slips. Hodan only noticed this week. At 18:20 Josephine came back for three more bales with another slip, stamped as deposited at 17:55. Hodan looked at it, said the bank closes at four, and said she'd check with the bank in the morning, then go to the police. They argued in the cubicle. Josephine hit her with the bale hook, shut the cubicle door, and at 18:40 had the porter carry the bales out, telling him "Mama Hodan is resting".

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Cubicle | Struck with the bale hook, which is on the floor |
| ev_invoice | Physical (found paper) | Hodan's carbon invoice book | **No. 3317 — J. Mueni — 3 bales printed cotton — 18:20 — paid: bank slip** |
| ev_slip | Physical (found paper) | Stapled to the invoice | "Umoja Bank, Eastleigh branch. Deposited **17:55**. KSh 96,000." In pencil, Hodan's hand: **"FAKE? Bank closed. Call in the morning."** |
| ev_bankhours | Physical | Bank glass at the mall entrance | Mon–Fri 08:30–16:00. The bank was shut at 17:55 |
| ev_fatuma | Witness | Tea seller | Brought Hodan tea at 18:25; she was arguing about "the bank" with a woman in a **purple headscarf**. Fatuma left the tea outside. At 19:05 the cup was still there, cold; she opened the cubicle and found Hodan |
| ev_lameck | Witness | Porter | A woman in a purple headscarf hired him at 18:30 to carry three bales to the Machakos matatus at 18:40. When he came, the bales were already outside the cubicle, the door was shut, and she came out alone and said, "Mama Hodan is resting, don't disturb her." She paid him KSh 300 |
| ev_mosque | Witness | Sheikh Ibrahim | Abdirahman came early for Maghrib, about 18:20, and stayed to talk to him until about 19:00 |
| ev_godown | Physical (found paper) | Gate log of Rajesh's godown, Industrial Area | R. Patel in 17:00, out 19:30 |
| ev_card | Physical | Josephine's handbag (she empties it on the counter when asked) | Business card: **"Mvua Holdings — Fast Loans · Title Searches · Document Services — Till 880 214"** (spine; not needed) |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Josephine Mueni | Cooperative | **"I left Eastleigh at four on the Machakos matatu. By six I was already home."** / "I've bought from Hodan for five years. Ask anyone." | First claim | `ev_invoice` (Hodan wrote her an invoice at 18:20) | *"I came back for the bales, yes. She was alive when I left. She was shouting at me, but she was alive."* (new fact: she was at stall 2-14 at 18:20) |
| Abdirahman Mohamed | Cooperative | "I was at the mosque from before Maghrib." | True | — | Topic "Hodan": the inheritance dispute "is with the elders, it's not a matter for the police". Topic "Josephine": "She always paid by slip. Hodan trusted her." |
| Rajesh Patel | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_invoice`) | "I haven't been to Eastleigh in a week." | True | — | Topic "prices": the dispute was about the shilling falling, nothing personal |

**Proof**
1. Josephine's claim + `ev_invoice` → she was at Hodan's stall at 18:20, and admits it.
2. `ev_slip` + `ev_bankhours` → the slip she paid with claims a deposit at 17:55 at a bank that shuts at 16:00; it's fake, and Hodan had noticed. This is why she was killed.
3. `ev_fatuma` + `ev_lameck` → at 18:25 Hodan was arguing with a woman in a purple headscarf about the bank; at 18:40 that same woman came out of the closed cubicle alone and kept people away → **WHO = Josephine Mueni** (her portrait shows the purple headscarf).

**Eliminations.** Abdirahman Mohamed: `ev_mosque`. Rajesh Patel: `ev_godown`. Fatuma Ali: walking the floor with her flask; two stallholders bought tea from her on the 3rd floor at 18:35 (her statement). Lameck Onyancha: hired at 18:30 and only arrived at 18:40, the cubicle already shut.

**Red herrings / twist.** None. The inheritance dispute with the cousin is the obvious line to press; it's real but unrelated, and it resolves itself in one topic.

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Hodan Farah at Barwaqo Mall.` Person words: Josephine Mueni, Abdirahman Mohamed, Rajesh Patel, Fatuma Ali, Lameck Onyancha (5).

**Credibility path.** 0 stamps.

**New interface beat.** **Signs and notices as evidence.** For the first time, something painted on a wall (the bank hours) is a collectible fact. Hotspots on the mall entrance include the glass door. Teaches the player to look at the environment, not just at people and papers.

**Kenyan texture.** Eastleigh's wholesale malls and First Avenue traffic, credit trading on trust, deposit slips, handcart porters, shaah sellers with flasks, elders settling inheritance before anyone goes to the police.

**Spine.** `ev_card` carries `t_mvua` (till 880 214, now advertising "document services"). Auto-filed to the Pattern File on solve. Mwalimu's post-case voice-note only: *"Document services. Interesting thing to sell next to loans."*

**Glossary.** shaah (spiced tea, Somali), mkokoteni (handcart), Maghrib (sunset prayer), wazee (elders).

**Images (5).** Portraits: Hodan, Josephine (purple headscarf, clearly visible), Abdirahman, Rajesh. Location: a Barwaqo Mall corridor at closing time.

**Audit tags.** Culprit F, 50s, Kamba-origin name, motive fraud exposure. Victim F, 30s, Somali-origin name. *Note: Eastleigh is cast with a Somali victim and Somali helpers (cousin, tea seller, imam), none as the culprit.*
