### Case 14 — Full Time

`case-014` · Eastlands · 12 min · suspects 3 · chain 2 · **herrings 1** · liars 1 (**innocent**) · groups WHO · stamps needed 0 · **twist: the liar is innocent**

**OB entry.** OB 08/15/06, 21:41. A waitress reports the owner of Goal Pub & Screen, Umoja Inner Core, found in the storeroom at the end of the Sunday match.

**Setting.** **Goal Pub & Screen**, a fictional bar with a projector screen, Umoja Inner Core. Sunday's big match (generic: no real teams or competition named): kick-off 19:30, half-time about 20:20–20:35, full time about 21:25. A plywood screen booth beside the storeroom door. Across the road: **Kamari Point**, a betting shop with live-bet counters.

**Victim.** **Josiah Mutai**, 56, owner. Struck with a crate of empty bottles in the storeroom.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ian Kamotho | 27 | Suspect | Screen operator and DJ; Josiah fired him that afternoon and refused to pay him two months' wages | **Culprit** |
| Tobias Okoth | 24 | Suspect | Regular; shouted at Josiah at half-time over a KSh 300 tab | Innocent; **the liar** |
| Purity Chepngetich | 49 | Suspect | Josiah's wife; inherits the pub; they'd been fighting about selling it | Innocent: at church |
| Monicah Njeri | 31 | Witness | Waitress; found him | Innocent |
| Cynthia Awino | 26 | Witness | Cashier at Kamari Point | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Ian had worked the booth for two years. Fired that afternoon, he still ran the evening's match because Josiah had nobody else. At 20:55 Josiah went into the storeroom to count crates. At 20:58 Ian left the booth, letting the stream freeze, went into the storeroom to demand his wages, and hit Josiah with a crate when he laughed. His headphones fell behind the crates. He was back in the booth by 21:04 and restarted the stream. Tobias, meanwhile, had slipped across the road at 20:48 to bet his mother's school-fees money on the second half.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Storeroom | Struck with a crate of empties |
| ev_monicah | Witness | Waitress | Saw Josiah go into the storeroom at 20:55 to count crates. **The screen froze from about 20:58 to 21:04**; the whole pub booed. She went to shout at Ian and **the booth was empty**. Found Josiah at 21:30 when she went for more crates |
| ev_freeze | Physical | Pinned to the bar: a regular's scrawled betting note | "FROZE 68'–74'!!! refund??" A customer kept track of match minutes against the freeze; the second half kicked off at 20:35 (45'), so 68'–74' is 20:58–21:04 |
| ev_headphones | Physical | Behind the crates in the storeroom | DJ headphones, sticker **"DJ KAMO"** |
| ev_tab | Witness | Monicah | Tobias and Josiah shouted about a KSh 300 tab at half-time (red herring) |
| ev_betslips | Physical (found paper) | Cynthia's counter copies | Three live-bet slips in Tobias Okoth's name at **20:48, 20:59 and 21:06**, the last one for KSh 1,500 |
| ev_cynthia | Witness | Cashier | Tobias stood at her counter from about 20:45 to 21:08, watching the odds on the screen |
| ev_church | Witness | Usher at fictional Neema Fellowship, Umoja (statement only) | Purity was in the choir from 18:00 until the service ended at 21:30 |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tobias Okoth | Cooperative | **"I watched the whole second half from my seat. I never left the pub."** / "Mzee and I shouted about a tab. That's football." | First claim | `ev_betslips` or `ev_cynthia` | *"Please don't tell my mother. That was her school-fees money for my sister. I was at Kamari Point the whole time, I swear, ask the cashier."* (new fact: he was across the road 20:45–21:08) |
| Ian Kamotho | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_monicah`) | "I had no problem with Mzee." (flat denial, not a checkable claim) | — | — | Topic "freeze": "The stream drops when the Wi-Fi drops." Topic "headphones" (once found): "Anyone could have put them there." |
| Purity Chepngetich | Cooperative | "I was at church until half past nine." | True | — | Topic "sale": she wanted to sell; he didn't |

**Proof**
1. `ev_monicah` + `ev_freeze` → Josiah went into the storeroom at 20:55, and from 20:58 to 21:04 the booth beside the storeroom was empty; the operator was away exactly when nobody was watching the storeroom door.
2. `ev_headphones` → the operator's headphones are in the storeroom behind the crates → **WHO = Ian Kamotho**.

**Eliminations.** Tobias Okoth: his broken claim + `ev_betslips` + `ev_cynthia` (across the road 20:45–21:08; the lie hid gambling, not murder). Purity Chepngetich: `ev_church`. Monicah Njeri: serving tables in full view of 60 customers. Cynthia Awino: at her counter.

**Red herrings / twist.**
- Red herring: Tobias's half-time shouting match.
- **Twist:** Tobias is the only person who lies, and the player will want to charge him. Lying isn't killing. When the claim breaks, the notebook greys the claim out instead of turning it red, and Mwalimu's voice-note plays: *"A man who lies to you isn't always a man who kills. Find out what he was hiding before you decide what it means."*

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Josiah Mutai at Goal Pub & Screen.` Person words: Ian Kamotho, Tobias Okoth, Purity Chepngetich, Monicah Njeri, Cynthia Awino (5).

**Credibility path.** 0 stamps.

**New interface beat.** **Broken isn't guilty.** Broken claims get one of two marks after the reaction: red (the reaction implicates) or grey (the reaction explains). Also the first **guarded** suspect: Ian's statement sheet is blank until the player shows him relevant evidence.

**Kenyan texture.** Football screening pubs on match night, live betting shops across the road, school-fees money, a church choir on Sunday evening.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** kamari (gambling), mechi (match), bob (shillings, slang), karo (school fees).

### Case 15 — Seal A-2291

`case-015` · Eastlands · 13 min · suspects 3 · chain 3 · herrings 0 · liars 1 (culprit) · groups WHO · stamps needed 1 (warrant)

**OB entry.** OB 41/19/06, 06:19. A business partner reports a mitumba bale wholesaler found dead in his godown, Gikomba riverside lane.

**Setting.** Gikomba market before dawn: 04:30–06:00 is bale-opening time. Fictional godown **Nyaberi & Mbithi Mitumba** on the riverside lane, stacked with pressed bales, each closed with a **numbered plastic seal**. Traders' stalls up the slope; handcart pushers moving bales through the dark.

**Victim.** **Hezron Nyaberi**, 61, bale wholesaler. Struck with an iron lever bar used for prising bales. His leather cash pouch, always on his belt, is gone.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Felistus Wakesho | 44 | Suspect | Children's-clothes trader, stall C-17; last week he sold her a "first grade" bale, seal **A-2291**, that turned out to be rags; she'd paid with a KSh 38,000 chama loan; he refused a refund | **Culprit** |
| Lucas Mbithi | 37 | Suspect | His business partner; they fought over the split | Innocent: on the overnight bus from Mombasa |
| Winnie Akello | 29 | Suspect | Rival trader; Hezron had cut her off | Innocent: opening her stall |
| Hamisi Baya | 50 | Witness | Handcart pusher | Innocent |

**What really happened.** At 04:40 Felistus came to the godown with the opened seal A-2291 as proof and begged for her money. Hezron laughed and told her to sell the rags as rags. When Hamisi wheeled out the last bales for another customer at 04:50, she was still there. She hit Hezron with the lever bar, took his cash pouch (KSh 41,000) as "her refund", left the seal on the floor where it had fallen, and was at her stall by 05:00, opening a bale as if she'd never left.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Godown | Struck with the lever bar; belt clip empty where the pouch was |
| ev_seal | Physical | Godown floor | An opened bale seal, **A-2291** |
| ev_dispatch | Physical (found paper) | Hezron's dispatch book | Last week: **"A-2291 — First grade kids — F. Wakesho, C-17 — KSh 38,000 cash."** Today, 04:40, Hezron's own hand: **"Wakesho came about A-2291. Rags she says. No refund."** |
| ev_hamisi | Witness | Handcart pusher | Loaded two bales for another trader at 04:45–04:50. Hezron was alive, laughing at a woman shouting about rags. As he pushed up the lane at about 04:55 he saw the same woman hurry past him **carrying a brown leather pouch like the one Hezron keeps on his belt** **(probable cause for a warrant)** |
| ev_stallbox | Physical, **warrant** | Felistus's locked stall box, C-17 | Hezron's leather pouch, stamped **H.N.**, KSh 41,000 inside; her chama loan card |
| ev_bus | Physical (found paper) | Lucas shows it | Overnight Mombasa–Nairobi bus ticket; arrived Nairobi 05:45; reached the godown 06:10 and found Hezron |
| ev_winnie | Witness | Stall neighbours (statement only) | Winnie opened her stall at 04:45 with a crowd of early buyers and never left |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Felistus Wakesho | Cooperative | "He cheated me. I won't pretend he didn't." / **"This morning I opened my bale at my own stall at five. I never went down to his godown."** | Second claim | `ev_dispatch` (today's 04:40 note) or `ev_seal` | *"I went to show him the seal. I begged him. He laughed at me. Then I left."* (new fact: she was at the godown at about 04:40) |
| Lucas Mbithi | Cooperative | "I was on the bus all night." | True | — | Topic "Hezron's pouch": "He never takes it off. He sleeps with it." |
| Winnie Akello | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_dispatch`) | "I don't go to his godown since he cut me off." | True | — | Topic "Felistus": "She lost everything on that bale. Everyone knew." |

**Proof**
1. Felistus's claim + `ev_dispatch` / `ev_seal` → she was at the godown at 04:40 and admits it.
2. `ev_hamisi` → Hezron was alive at 04:50 with her still there, and at 04:55 she was seen hurrying away with a pouch like his.
3. `ev_stallbox` (warrant) → Hezron's pouch, with his initials, is in her locked stall box → **WHO = Felistus Wakesho**.

**Eliminations.** Lucas Mbithi: `ev_bus` (in Nairobi from 05:45, at the godown 06:10, after Hamisi's sighting). Winnie Akello: `ev_winnie`. Hamisi Baya: pushing his cart up the lane with another trader's bales (the trader's statement confirms delivery at 05:00).

**Red herrings / twist.** None.

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Hezron Nyaberi at his Gikomba godown.` Person words: Felistus Wakesho, Lucas Mbithi, Winnie Akello, Hamisi Baya, Daudi Gichohi (the trader whose bales Hamisi was carrying; his statement confirms the 05:00 delivery) (5).

**Credibility path.** 1 stamp: the warrant for stall C-17. Without it the player can still reach a correct WHO from steps 1–2, but the proof is weaker and the validator marks the warrant fact as part of the minimal proof, so the hint system points to it.

**Spine.** None.

**Images (5).** Portraits: Hezron, Felistus, Lucas, Winnie. Location: Gikomba riverside godowns before dawn, lit by bulbs.

### Case 16 — Maji

`case-016` · Eastlands · 13 min · suspects 3 · chain 2 · herrings 0 · liars 1 (**false confessor**) · groups WHO · stamps needed 0 · **twist: the wrong person confesses**

**OB entry.** OB 19/24/06, 22:08. A resident reports a man found dead beside the community water kiosk, Mathare North. A young man has walked into the station and confessed.

**Setting.** **Maji Safi Kiosk No. 7 (MK-7)**, a fictional community water kiosk run under a residents' water committee, Mathare North, near the river. Blue water tank, a tap stand, a painted price board (KSh 5 per 20-litre jerrican). The main valve is opened with a long iron **valve key** (a T-bar about 1.2 m long). A committee notice: *"Valve key held by kiosk attendant only."*

**Victim.** **Stanley Mulwa**, 36. Collects "fees" from water points for a local water-vending gang. Struck with the valve key.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kadzo Kahindi | 67 | Suspect | Kiosk attendant for 14 years; refuses to pay the gang | **Culprit** |
| Baraka Kazungu | 19 | Suspect | Her grandson; confessed at the station | Innocent; **the liar (false confession)** |
| Nicholas Ruto | 42 | Suspect | Runs a rival water-vending crew; wanted Mulwa's patch | Innocent: at a funeral vigil |
| Zipporah Mutheu | 45 | Witness | Neighbour; found him | Innocent |
| Rhoda Jebet | 38 | Witness (statement only) | Nurse at the fictional Mathare Community Clinic | Innocent |

**What really happened.** On Monday, Mulwa broke Baraka's arm when Baraka refused to hand over the kiosk's takings. On Tuesday night at 21:10 Mulwa came back to the kiosk and told Kadzo that next time it would be the boy's head. At 21:15 she swung the valve key at him with both hands. He fell and didn't get up. She called Baraka, told him to go home and say nothing. Baraka, afraid for her, walked to the station at 22:00 and confessed.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Beside the tap stand | Struck with the valve key, which lies in the mud |
| ev_valvekey | Physical | Scene | Iron T-bar, about 1.2 m, painted **MK-7**. Swinging it needs **both hands** (any player lifting it in the 3D view sees two grip positions) |
| ev_notice | Physical | Kiosk wall | "Valve key held by kiosk attendant only" — Mathare North Water Committee |
| ev_salesbook | Physical (found paper) | Kiosk counter | Kadzo's sales book: jerricans and coins, line by line; the **last sale is 21:05**, then nothing for the night, though the kiosk normally sells until 22:00 |
| ev_clinic | Physical (found paper) | Baraka's pocket | Clinic card, Monday: "Fracture, **right** forearm. POP cast applied. Review in 6 weeks." His right arm is in a cast and sling |
| ev_zipporah | Witness | Neighbour | At 21:10 heard Mulwa at the kiosk shouting "next time it's the boy's head". At 21:15 heard a clang. At 21:20 saw Kadzo walk Baraka away from the kiosk by the elbow. At 21:50 went for water and found Mulwa |
| ev_baraka_where | Witness | Zipporah | Baraka arrived at the kiosk only at **about 21:18**, running from the football pitch; he was "still in his jersey" |
| ev_matanga | Witness | Host of a funeral vigil in Huruma (statement only) | Nicholas Ruto was at the matanga from 20:00 until after 01:00, leading the singing |
| ev_rhoda | Witness | Nurse | Treated Baraka on Monday; "he said a man did it over water money; he was too scared to say who" |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baraka Kazungu | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_body` or `ev_valvekey`) | **"I did it. I hit him with the valve key. Leave my grandmother out of this."** | Yes (false confession) | `ev_clinic` + `ev_valvekey` (a two-handed bar; his right arm is in a cast) **or** `ev_baraka_where` (he arrived after the clang) | *"...I wasn't there when it happened. Bibi called me after. She told me to go home and say nothing. I couldn't let them take her."* (new fact: Kadzo called him to the kiosk after the attack) |
| Kadzo Kahindi | Cooperative | "That man broke my grandson's arm on Monday." / "I sell water. That is all I do." | True / flat denial | — | Topic "valve key": "Nobody else touches it. The committee says so." Topic "Baraka": she goes quiet |
| Nicholas Ruto | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_zipporah`) | "I was at a matanga in Huruma all night." | True | — | Topic "Mulwa": "Everyone on this river had a reason. Not everyone had the stomach." |

**Proof**
1. Baraka's confession + `ev_clinic` + `ev_valvekey` → he physically couldn't swing a two-handed iron bar with his right arm in a cast, and `ev_baraka_where` puts him at the kiosk only after the clang. The confession is false, and protects someone.
2. `ev_notice` + `ev_salesbook` + `ev_zipporah` → the weapon is the valve key only the attendant holds; Kadzo's sales stop at 21:05; Mulwa threatened the boy at 21:10 and was struck at 21:15; the only other person at the kiosk was Kadzo → **WHO = Kadzo Kahindi**.

**Eliminations.** Baraka Kazungu: step 1. Nicholas Ruto: `ev_matanga`. Zipporah Mutheu: in her house next door (heard, didn't see, until 21:20). Rhoda Jebet: at the clinic.

**Red herrings / twist.** **Twist:** the person who confesses is innocent, and the player who charges him gets Halima's sharpest fail line: *"A confession is where you start, not where you stop. Look at his arm."*

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Stanley Mulwa at Kiosk MK-7.` Person words: Kadzo Kahindi, Baraka Kazungu, Nicholas Ruto, Zipporah Mutheu, Rhoda Jebet (5).

Halima's pass line, which matters for tone: *"The court will hear what he did to that boy. It still has to hear what she did."*

**Credibility path.** 0 stamps.

**New interface beat.** **Handling objects in 3D.** The valve key can be lifted and turned; the two grip positions show without any text. First time a physical property of an object (it needs two hands) is the deduction.

**Kenyan texture.** Community water kiosks and residents' water committees, KSh 5 jerricans, water-vending gangs who tax water points (a real, widespread pattern), a funeral vigil (matanga) with singing all night, a grandmother called bibi.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** maji (water), bibi (grandmother), matanga (funeral gathering/vigil), mtaa (neighbourhood), mtungi / jerrican.

**Images (5).** Portraits: Kadzo, Baraka (arm in a cast and sling), Nicholas, Stanley. Location: kiosk MK-7 at night, the blue tank lit by one bulb.

**Audit tags.** Culprit F, 60s, Mijikenda (Giriama)-origin name, motive protecting someone. Victim M, 30s, Kamba-origin name. *Tone note: the victim is the aggressor in this case; the reconstruction must not glamorise the killing or mock him. It stays quiet and sad.*

### Case 17 — Visitor Badge 14

`case-017` · Eastlands · 14 min · suspects 3 · chain 3 · herrings 0 · liars 1 (**alibi friend**) · groups WHO · stamps needed 0 · **spine background detail**

**OB entry.** OB 06/02/07, 22:41. A resident of Tumaini Towers, Pipeline, reports her neighbour found dead in flat C-11-04.

**Setting.** **Tumaini Towers**, a fictional block of three 12-storey towers (A, B, C) in Embakasi Pipeline estate. **No lift.** One compound gate where every visitor signs the gate book and takes a numbered laminated **visitor badge**, which they hand back on the way out.

**Victim.** **Pauline Kanana**, 43, primary-school teacher, flat C-11-04 (11th floor). Struck with her own heavy charcoal iron.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Evans Nyakundi | 55 | Suspect | "Land agent"; sold Pauline a plot in Kitengela for KSh 650,000 with a title that, her own search showed, belongs to someone else | **Culprit** |
| Philip Masinde | 52 | Suspect | Evans's friend, lives in A-3-02; gave Evans an alibi | Innocent of the killing; **the liar** |
| Martin Sang | 47 | Suspect | Pauline's ex-husband; in a dispute over their son's school fees | Innocent: at work |
| Saida Abdallah | 36 | Witness | Neighbour, C-11-03; found her | Innocent |
| Julius Mwaniki | 61 | Witness | Gate guard | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Pauline's own title search, done through a friend at the lands office, showed the Kitengela plot wasn't Evans's to sell. On Monday she wrote him a letter: refund by Friday or the police. On Wednesday at 20:10 he signed in at the gate as her visitor, climbed to the 11th floor, and tried to talk her round. She told him the police already had a copy. He hit her with the iron. On the way out at 20:55 he slipped past the guard while a delivery van was at the gate and didn't hand back his badge; it had fallen under her sofa. He asked Philip to say they'd been watching TV together.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Living room | Struck with a charcoal iron |
| ev_letter | Physical (found paper) | Copy on her table | "Mr Evans Nyakundi: refund KSh 650,000 by Friday or I report to police. P. Kanana" |
| ev_agreement | Physical (found paper) | Her document folder | Sale agreement for a Kitengela plot (fictional parcel number), signed by Evans as vendor. A rubber-stamp impression in the corner: **"Title search — certified — REGISTRAR OF TITLES"**, in the same oval design as the half-finished seal from case 10 (spine; not needed) |
| ev_search | Physical (found paper) | Her document folder | Her own official search result: the parcel is registered to a different person entirely |
| ev_gatebook | Physical (found paper) | Gate | **"20:10 — Evans N. — visiting C-11-04 — badge 14."** Return column for badge 14: blank. Julius's note at 22:00: "Badge 14 NOT RETURNED" |
| ev_badge | Physical | Under Pauline's sofa | Laminated visitor badge **No. 14** |
| ev_saida | Witness | Neighbour | Saw Pauline come up the stairs with shopping at 20:05. Heard voices through the wall from about 20:15, a crash about 20:45, then quiet. At 22:35 noticed the door ajar and found her |
| ev_julius | Witness | Gate guard | Signed Evans in at 20:10. A delivery van blocked the gate at about 20:55 and he didn't see who left then |
| ev_clockcard | Physical (found paper) | Martin shows it | Night-shift clock card, JKIA cargo terminal (a neutral real setting): in 18:52, out 07:04 |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Philip Masinde | Cooperative | **"Evans was with me in my flat, A-3-02, from seven until ten. We watched the news and the football."** | Yes | `ev_gatebook` (Evans signed in at 20:10 to visit C-11-04) | *"...I fell asleep after the seven o'clock news. When I woke up he was there. He asked me to say he'd been there the whole time. I didn't ask why."* (new fact: Evans asked him for an alibi) |
| Evans Nyakundi | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_letter`) | "I've never been to her flat." (flat denial) / "That plot is clean. She was confused." | Denial / opinion, not checkable | — | Topic "title": "Searches go wrong. Clerks make mistakes." |
| Martin Sang | Cooperative | "I was at work all night." | True | — | Topic "Pauline": the fees dispute, "but I'd never hurt her, she's my son's mother" |

**Proof**
1. Philip's claim + `ev_gatebook` → Evans wasn't in A-3-02 all evening; he signed in at 20:10 to visit Pauline's flat, and he asked Philip to lie for him.
2. `ev_saida` → Pauline was alive at 20:05, someone was with her from 20:15, and the crash came at 20:45, inside Evans's 20:10 visit.
3. `ev_badge` + `ev_gatebook` → Evans's badge, never returned, is under her sofa → **WHO = Evans Nyakundi**. (`ev_letter` + `ev_search` give the motive.)

**Eliminations.** Philip Masinde: his own revealed fact (asleep in A-3-02; the gate book shows he never signed in to Tower C, and residents of A can't reach C's stairwell without crossing the gate yard in Julius's view). Martin Sang: `ev_clockcard`. Saida Abdallah: in her flat; her timeline is the one that fixes the window, and her own door was locked (the chain was on when she first looked out at 22:35). Julius Mwaniki: at the gate.

**Red herrings / twist.** None. The ex-husband with a grievance is the lazy suspect; his clock card closes him in one step.

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Pauline Kanana at Tumaini Towers.` Person words: Evans Nyakundi, Philip Masinde, Martin Sang, Saida Abdallah, Julius Mwaniki (5).

**Credibility path.** 0 stamps.

**New interface beat.** **Linked claims.** When Philip's alibi breaks, Evans's own whereabouts (which depended on it) turn grey in the notebook automatically. The player sees one broken claim knock out another.

**Kenyan texture.** Pipeline's no-lift 12-storey blocks, gate books and laminated visitor badges, fake plot sales on the city's edge, title searches, a charcoal iron in a city flat.

**Spine.** `ev_agreement` carries `t_stamp`: the same REGISTRAR OF TITLES oval as the seal Rashid refused to finish in case 10. Not needed for this case. On solve it's pinned to the Pattern File next to case 10's proof, and the two impressions match. No narration points it out; the match is for the player to see.

**Glossary.** ploti (plot), title deed (hati), msako (search/raid, used loosely).

**Images (5).** Portraits: Pauline, Evans, Philip, Martin. Location: Tumaini Towers at night, three towers, a lit stairwell climbing all twelve floors.

**Audit tags.** Culprit M, 50s, Kisii-origin name, motive land (fraud). Victim F, 40s, Meru-origin name.

### Case 18 — Studio ya Mtaa

`case-018` · Eastlands · 14 min · suspects 3 · chain 3 · herrings 0 · liars 1 (culprit) · groups WHO · stamps needed 0

**OB entry.** OB 30/13/07, 00:22 (Sunday). A musician reports a music producer found dead in his studio, Dandora Phase 4.

**Setting.** **Mtaa Records**, a fictional one-room studio in a converted ground-floor flat, Dandora Phase 4: egg-tray soundproofing, a mixing desk, a vocal booth made from a wardrobe, a booking clipboard on the wall. On Saturday night there's a big concert at a stadium across town (venue named only as "the Kasarani show").

**Victim.** **Shadrack "Shaddy B" Wekulo**, 25, producer. Struck with a microphone stand.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mercyline Jepkosgei | 24 | Suspect | Singer; his girlfriend and co-writer. Last week he released *Moto wa Jioni*, the song she wrote, credited to another artist, with her listed as "backing vocals" | **Culprit** |
| Clinton Mbaabu | 27 | Suspect | Rival MC who books midnight sessions; Shaddy owed him studio time | Innocent: arrived at 00:05 |
| Rosemary Nyambura | 38 | Suspect | Mercyline's manager; Shaddy owed her a performance fee | Innocent: at the Kasarani show |
| Sophie Adongo | 41 | Witness | Lives upstairs | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Mercyline's slot at the Kasarani show ended at 21:20. She took a boda straight to Dandora and signed in for an 23:00 "vocal retake" so Shaddy would have to see her. In the studio she demanded her writing credit. He told her she was lucky to be on the song at all. At about 23:30 she hit him with the mic stand and ran. Her left earring came off in the struggle and rolled under the desk.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Studio | Struck with a mic stand |
| ev_booking | Physical (found paper) | Wall clipboard | **"23:00 — MERCY — vocal retake"**, initialled **"MJ"** with the small heart she always draws |
| ev_lineup | Physical (found paper) | Show poster (on the studio door) | Mercyline's slot: **21:00–21:20** |
| ev_earring | Physical | Under the mixing desk | A gold hoop earring |
| ev_portrait | Physical | Mercyline's portrait / her show photo | She's wearing **one** gold hoop, in her **right** ear (the zoom view makes this visible) |
| ev_sophie | Witness | Upstairs neighbour | Shouting from about 23:15; a crash about 23:30; from her window saw **a woman in a silver jacket** run to a boda at the corner |
| ev_jacket | Physical | The show poster photo | Mercyline performed in a **silver jacket** |
| ev_payments | Physical (found paper) | Rosemary shows it | Organiser's performer-payment sheet at Kasarani: Rosemary signed for payouts at 22:40, 23:25 and 00:10 |
| ev_boda | Witness | Erastus Mugo, Clinton's boda rider (statement only) | Picked Clinton up in Kariobangi at 23:50, dropped him at the studio at 00:05 |
| ev_lyrics | Physical (found paper) | Desk drawer | Draft lyrics of *Moto wa Jioni* in Mercyline's handwriting, with the same heart doodles |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mercyline Jepkosgei | Cooperative | **"I was at the Kasarani show until midnight. Ask anyone."** / "Shaddy stole my song. I wanted my name on it, not his blood." | First claim | `ev_booking` (her signature for 23:00) or `ev_lineup` (her set ended 21:20) | *"I went to the studio after my set. We fought about the song. I left before half eleven. He was alive."* (new fact: she was at the studio from about 23:00) |
| Clinton Mbaabu | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_booking`) | "I came for my midnight session and found him." | True | — | Topic "Shaddy": "He took everyone's money. Not everyone's songs." |
| Rosemary Nyambura | Cooperative | "I was paying performers at Kasarani until after midnight." | True | — | Topic "Mercy": "She left right after her set. She was crying." |

**Proof**
1. Mercyline's claim + `ev_booking` / `ev_lineup` → she wasn't at the show until midnight; she signed in at the studio for 23:00 and admits being there.
2. `ev_earring` + `ev_portrait`, and `ev_sophie` + `ev_jacket` → her missing earring is under the desk, and the woman seen running at 23:30 wore a silver jacket like her stage outfit → **WHO = Mercyline Jepkosgei**. (`ev_lyrics` confirms the motive.)

**Eliminations.** Clinton Mbaabu: `ev_boda` (arrived 00:05, after the 23:30 crash). Rosemary Nyambura: `ev_payments`. Sophie Adongo: upstairs, never came down until the police arrived.

**Red herrings / twist.** None.

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Shadrack Wekulo at Mtaa Records.` Person words: Mercyline Jepkosgei, Clinton Mbaabu, Rosemary Nyambura, Sophie Adongo, Erastus Mugo (Clinton's boda rider, the source of `ev_boda`) (5).

**Credibility path.** 0 stamps.

**New interface beat.** **Portraits are evidence.** First case where a detail in a generated image (one earring) is a fact. The portrait zoom view becomes a hotspot. **Image-generation requirement:** Mercyline's portrait prompt must specify "one gold hoop earring, in the right ear only, left ear bare"; this image is checked by hand before shipping, because the deduction depends on it.

**Kenyan texture.** Dandora's music scene and home studios, egg-tray soundproofing, gengetone and the fight over song credits, a big Kasarani concert, boda-boda as the city's night transport.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** gengetone (Kenyan street-music genre), mbogi (crew), manzi (young woman, Sheng), studio ya mtaa (neighbourhood studio).

**Images (6).** Portraits: Shadrack, Mercyline (one earring, silver jacket), Clinton, Rosemary. Location: the studio with egg-tray walls. Evidence photo: the gold hoop under the desk.

### Case 19 — Jua Kali

`case-019` · Eastlands · 15 min · suspects 3 · chain 3 · herrings 0 · liars 1 (culprit) · groups WHO · stamps needed 1 (warrant)

**OB entry.** OB 22/21/07, 15:24. A metalworker reports his employer, a cookstove maker, found dead in her shed, Kamukunji jua kali sheds.

**Setting.** The Kamukunji jua kali metalwork sheds beside Gikomba: rows of open tin-roofed sheds, hammering all day, offcuts of sheet metal everywhere. Fictional **Moto Safi Jikos**, Wanjiku's shed, with a half-finished stove on the anvil. Every fundi's hammer face wears differently, and the old hands can tell whose hammer made a dent.

**Victim.** **Wanjiku Ngugi**, 41, maker of energy-saving charcoal jikos; last month she won a county tender to supply 500 stoves to schools. Struck with a hammer.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Benson Okiror | 53 | Suspect | Rival jiko maker two sheds down; lost the tender to her and lodged an appeal | **Culprit** |
| Gitau Mwaura | 46 | Suspect | Her husband; borrowed against her tender advance without asking her | Innocent: at a clinic with their daughter |
| Fidel Okumu | 26 | Suspect | Her employee; she docked his pay for a spoiled batch | Innocent: delivering stoves |
| Simeon Wachira | 62 | Witness | Old fundi in the next shed | Innocent |
| Edwin Koech | 35 | Witness (statement only) | Clerk at the county procurement office | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Benson's appeal was thrown out at City Hall at 13:30. He was back at the sheds by 14:15. At about 14:20 he walked into Wanjiku's shed with his hammer, saying he'd come to show her where her stoves were badly made. They argued; he hit her. Before leaving he hammered dents into her half-finished stove "so it looks like a fight over work". He locked his hammer in his toolbox.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Shed | Struck with a hammer; no hammer at the scene (hers is on its hook, clean) |
| ev_stove | Physical | Anvil | The half-finished jiko has fresh dents, each with a small **X-shaped mark** in the middle |
| ev_simeon_marks | Witness | Old fundi | "Every hammer wears its own face. An X like that is a chipped face. **Okiror's hammer has an X**; he chipped it on a rivet last year and never ground it down." |
| ev_simeon_saw | Witness | Old fundi | At about 14:20 saw Benson go into Wanjiku's shed **with his hammer in his hand**, "like a man going to fix something". Heard them shouting. Didn't see him leave **(probable cause for a warrant)** |
| ev_customer | Witness | A school bursar's driver (statement only) | Collected a sample stove from Wanjiku at 14:00; she was fine |
| ev_cityhall | Physical (found paper) | County procurement visitor register (Edwin Koech shows it) | **B. Okiror — in 12:10 — out 13:40** |
| ev_appeal | Physical (found paper) | Benson's pocket (he hands it over with his ID) | Letter dismissing his tender appeal, dated today |
| ev_toolbox | Physical, **warrant** | Benson's locked toolbox | His hammer: a **chipped X on the face**, wiped but with fresh metal shavings in the chip |
| ev_clinic | Physical (found paper) | Gitau shows it | Clinic card for their daughter, fictional Umoja Health Centre, in 13:30, out 15:30 |
| ev_delivery | Physical (found paper) | Fidel's delivery note | 20 stoves delivered to a school in Kariobangi, **signed by the bursar 14:35** |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Benson Okiror | Cooperative | **"I was at City Hall all afternoon about my appeal. I didn't come back to Kamukunji until four."** / "She won with bribes. Everyone knows." | First claim | `ev_cityhall` (out at 13:40) | *"I left early, yes. I went to eat. I didn't go near her shed."* (new fact: he was free from 13:40) |
| Gitau Mwaura | Cooperative | "I was at the clinic with our daughter." | True | — | Topic "money": admits the loan, ashamed |
| Fidel Okumu | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_stove`) | "I was delivering to the school." | True | — | Topic "dents": "Mama never left dents like that. She'd have beaten them out." |

**Proof**
1. Benson's claim + `ev_cityhall` → he left City Hall at 13:40, so his alibi for the afternoon is false.
2. `ev_customer` + `ev_simeon_saw` → Wanjiku was alive at 14:00, and at 14:20 Benson walked into her shed with a hammer.
3. `ev_stove` + `ev_simeon_marks` + `ev_toolbox` (warrant) → the dents carry the X of a chipped hammer face, and Benson's hammer has exactly that chip → **WHO = Benson Okiror**.

**Eliminations.** Gitau Mwaura: `ev_clinic`. Fidel Okumu: `ev_delivery` (Kariobangi at 14:35; he left at 13:50 with the handcart, confirmed by Simeon). Simeon Wachira: hammering at his own anvil in full view of his two apprentices. Edwin Koech: at the county office.

**Red herrings / twist.** None. The husband's secret loan is a real betrayal and an obvious line to press, but his clinic card ends it.

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Wanjiku Ngugi at the Kamukunji sheds.` Person words: Benson Okiror, Gitau Mwaura, Fidel Okumu, Simeon Wachira, Edwin Koech (5).

**Credibility path.** 1 stamp: the warrant for Benson's toolbox.

**New interface beat.** **The comparison view.** Two pieces of evidence (the dented stove and the hammer face) can be laid side by side under a magnifier and turned to line up. A match snaps with a click. Used for tool marks, handwriting, stamps and footprints from here on.

**Kenyan texture.** The jua kali sector and its craft pride, energy-saving jikos, county tenders and appeals, metalworkers who read each other's hammer marks.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** jua kali (informal artisan sector; literally "fierce sun"), fundi (craftsman), jiko (stove), tenda (tender).

**Images (6).** Portraits: Wanjiku, Benson, Gitau, Fidel. Location: Kamukunji sheds at midday, sparks and tin roofs. Evidence photo: the dented stove with the X marks.

**Audit tags.** Culprit M, 50s, Teso-origin name, motive business rivalry. Victim F, 40s, Kikuyu-origin name.

### Case 20 — BOSS: Three Padlocks

`case-020` · Eastlands · **boss** · 18 min · suspects 4 · chain 3 · herrings 1 · liars 1 (culprit) · groups WHO + **SPINE** · stamps needed 1 (warrant) · **twist: the lockbox tells the story; first blank that needs the Pattern File**

**OB entry.** OB 03/26/07, 21:26. A man reports his wife, treasurer of a women's chama, found dead at home in Komarock Phase 1; the chama's lockbox broken open.

**Setting.** A family maisonette in Komarock Phase 1, Saturday evening. **Upendo Women's Chama**: 24 members, a blue-and-yellow kitenge uniform, a mid-year payout due on 31 July (the date the members chose in January). The chama's savings records and cash live in a **blue steel lockbox with three padlocks**: one key each for the **chair**, the **secretary** and the **treasurer**, so no one official can open it alone. Anne keeps the box at her house.

**Victim.** **Anne Mumbua**, 54, the chama's treasurer for six years. Struck with the steel lockbox's lid bar. The box is open on the dining table. The **ledger is gone**.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Millicent Akoth | 48 | Suspect | Chama chairlady; pushed the "Mvua land investment" | **Culprit** |
| Joyce Kemunto | 37 | Suspect | Chama secretary | Innocent: at a wedding committee |
| Musau Kilonzo | 57 | Suspect | Anne's husband; took a chama loan against her share and lost it; shouted at her that afternoon | Innocent (red herring): MC at a funeral harambee in Kangundo |
| Florence Nekesa | 35 | Suspect | Member who publicly demanded an early payout at the last meeting | Innocent: on a hospital night shift |
| Gladys Kawira | 60 | Witness | Next-door neighbour | Innocent |
| Mohamed Jillo | 45 | Witness | Shopkeeper at the corner | Innocent |

**What really happened.** In April, with Anne away at her son's graduation, Millicent got the members present to vote the chama's savings into a "land investment plan" sold by **Mvua Holdings**: KSh 1.14 million paid in six instalments to till **880 214** for "plot reservations" in Bahati, Nakuru. To make withdrawals easy she had the secretary hand her key over "for safekeeping during the investment", which the minutes record. Anne came home, checked the ledger against the bank and the till receipts, found the plots don't exist, and said she'd tell all 24 members at the payout. On Saturday at about 20:20 Millicent came to Anne's house with both keys and bolt cutters to take the ledger. Anne caught her at the box. Millicent struck her with the lid bar, cut the treasurer's padlock off (Anne's key was on a chain around her neck), and left at 20:40 with the ledger.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Dining room | Struck with the lockbox's steel lid bar |
| ev_box | Physical | Dining table (3D view) | Three padlocks. **Chair's padlock: opened with a key**, hanging open. **Secretary's padlock: opened with a key**, hanging open. **Treasurer's padlock: cut through with bolt cutters**. Ledger compartment empty |
| ev_annekey | Physical | On Anne's body | The treasurer's key on a chain around her neck, under her blouse |
| ev_minutes | Physical (found paper) | Joyce brings the minutes book | April meeting: *"Investment — Chair proposes the Mvua Holdings Land Investment Plan. Carried. **Secretary's key handed to Chair** for safekeeping during the investment period."* Under attendance: **"Apologies: A. Mumbua (son's graduation, Eldoret)."** **(Probable cause for a warrant: only the chair holds two keys)** |
| ev_joyce | Witness | Secretary | "I gave her my key in April. There's no copy. You can't copy those keys on River Road; they're the old kind." |
| ev_jillo | Witness | Shopkeeper | Anne bought milk at **20:05** and said she was "going home to count". |
| ev_gladys | Witness | Neighbour | Heard a shout at about 20:30. At about 20:40 saw **a woman in the Upendo kitenge** leave Anne's gate with a heavy bag. Couldn't see her face. (All 24 members own that uniform: a fair clue that narrows nothing by itself) |
| ev_millicent_house | Physical, **warrant** | Millicent's house, Komarock Phase 2 | The chama **ledger**; **bolt cutters**; six PesaPap receipts: **"Till 880 214 — Mvua Holdings — Plot reservation, Bahati block"**, total KSh 1,140,000; a typed letter on Mvua letterhead: *"Delay the payout. Members will be paid in plots. — K."* |
| ev_musau | Physical (found paper) | Funeral harambee programme | "MC: Mr Musau Kilonzo", 17:00–21:00, Kangundo, about 90 minutes' drive away; 40 mourners saw him at the microphone |
| ev_musau_quarrel | Witness | Gladys | Musau and Anne shouted about the loan at about 15:00 (red herring) |
| ev_wedding | Physical (found paper) | Joyce's wedding-committee minutes | Committee meeting in Kayole, 18:00–22:00, Joyce taking minutes throughout |
| ev_florence | Physical (found paper) | Florence shows it | Night-shift clock card, fictional Embakasi Mission Hospital, in 18:55 |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Millicent Akoth | Cooperative | **"Anne voted for the Mvua investment at the April meeting. She agreed to everything."** / "I was home all evening." (flat; not checkable without the warrant) | First claim | `ev_minutes` ("Apologies: A. Mumbua") | *"...She wasn't there. We needed the vote before the offer closed. It's a good investment. The plots are real."* (new fact: the investment was pushed through without the treasurer) |
| Musau Kilonzo | Cooperative | "I was the MC at my cousin's funeral in Kangundo." | True | — | Topic "loan": he lost the money betting; he's ashamed; he and Anne fought about it at 15:00 |
| Joyce Kemunto | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_box`) | "I don't have my key. The chair does." | True | — | Shows `ev_minutes` |
| Florence Nekesa | Cooperative | "I was at work." | True | — | Topic "payout": "Because Millicent kept saying the money was 'invested'. I wanted mine before it disappeared." |

**Proof**
1. `ev_box` + `ev_annekey` → whoever opened the box had the chair's and secretary's keys and had to cut the treasurer's lock because Anne's key was on her body.
2. `ev_minutes` + `ev_joyce` → since April, both of those keys have been held by one person, the chair, Millicent Akoth; there's no copy. Millicent's claim that Anne voted for the investment is false (Anne was absent).
3. `ev_jillo` + `ev_gladys` + `ev_millicent_house` (warrant) → Anne was alive at 20:05; a member in uniform left with a heavy bag at 20:40; the missing ledger and the bolt cutters are in Millicent's house → **WHO = Millicent Akoth**.

**Spine proof (Pattern File).** The receipts in `ev_millicent_house` show the savings went to **Till 880 214**. The Pattern File holds six pins at this point (five offered as SPINE words; the sixth, the emptied 'Mvua — Friday' drawer from case 10, is pinned but not offered); only one of them is a *payment* to that till: Rashid's deposit for the forged REGISTRAR OF TITLES seal (case 10). The others show the till without a payment (case 6 calendar, case 13 business card) or don't show it at all (case 17 stamp, case 10 note).

**Eliminations.**
- *WHO:* Musau Kilonzo: `ev_musau`. Joyce Kemunto: `ev_wedding` (and she has no key). Florence Nekesa: `ev_florence`. Gladys Kawira: at her gate; she's the one who saw the woman leave. Mohamed Jillo: at his counter.
- *Spine:* as above.

**Red herrings / twist.**
- Red herring: the husband's afternoon quarrel and lost loan.
- **Twist:** the lockbox, an everyday piece of chama trust, is the whole proof: two keys used, one lock cut, and the minutes say who held two keys.
- **Spine twist:** the chama's money and the forged seal were paid into the same till, so the people forging land titles are also selling the land.

**Charge sheet.** Two groups:

> **WHO:** `{who} killed Anne Mumbua to stop her telling the members where their savings had gone.`
> **SPINE:** `Upendo's savings were paid to Till 880 214, the same till that took the deposit for {pin}.`

- WHO words: Millicent Akoth, Joyce Kemunto, Musau Kilonzo, Florence Nekesa, Gladys Kawira (5).
- SPINE words (Pattern File pins): *the forged registrar seal (case 10)*, *the Mvua calendar (case 6)*, *the Mvua business card (case 13)*, *the stamped sale agreement (case 17)*, *the note "Kivuli wants it Friday" (case 10)* (5).
- Halima: WHO pass, SPINE fail: *"She did it. But you're telling me this is bigger than a chama. Show me how."* Both pass: *"The same till that ordered a fake seal is selling fake plots. Amani, who are these people?"*

**After the verdict.**
- Reconstruction ends with Millicent in the interview room: she never met anyone from Mvua. Letters came signed "K." Cash for the "plot fees" was collected by **"a man they call Fundi, with a bad leg"**. Hearsay only: Fundi isn't identified until case 50.
- Pattern File gains three pins: the six Mvua receipts (`t_mvua`), the "K." letter (`t_kivuli`), and Millicent's description of Fundi (`t_fundi`). The receipts say **"Bahati block, Nakuru"**, the first pointer towards region 4.
- Halima's first personal text: *"Drink something. That one was heavy."*
- **Collectible:** a photocopied page of the Upendo ledger, the members' names in Anne's handwriting, sent to Amani by the members after the payout is restored. It goes in a frame on the desk.

**New interface beat.** **The Pattern File as evidence.** First charge-sheet blank filled by dragging a pin from the Pattern File, not a word from this case. Also the **lockbox 3D inspection**: turn the box, look at each padlock in turn.

**Kenyan texture.** Women's chamas and their mid-year payouts, three-key lockboxes, minutes books, "investment" schemes selling plots far from Nairobi, matching kitenge uniforms, funeral harambees with an MC, a corner shop where everyone buys milk at 8 pm.

**Spine.** Threads `t_mvua`, `t_kivuli`, `t_fundi`. First spine group requiring earlier cases (§4.4).

**Glossary.** chama, kitenge (printed cloth), harambee (community fundraiser), ploti (plot), mweka hazina (treasurer), mwenyekiti (chairperson).

**Images (8).** Portraits: Anne, Millicent, Joyce, Musau, Florence. Location: Komarock maisonette dining room at night. Evidence photos: the lockbox with two padlocks open and one cut; the six Mvua receipts fanned on a table.

**Audit tags.** Culprit F, 40s, Luo-origin name, motive commissioned (spine). Victim F, 50s, Kamba-origin name.

## Open questions for the cultural reader (region 2)

1. **Eastleigh (case 13):** does the casting (Somali victim, cousin, tea seller and imam as helpers) read as respectful? Is "Barwaqo" a plausible mall name?
2. **Mathare water (case 16):** is the water-gang depiction accurate without stigmatising residents? Would a Giriama grandmother in Nairobi be called *bibi* by her grandson, or something else?
3. **Distress for rent (case 12):** is an auctioneer's seven-day notice on the door accurate to how Kenyan landlords proceed?
4. **Chama lockboxes (case 20):** is the three-padlock box a common practice, and are the officer titles in Swahili right?
5. **Dandora and gengetone (case 18):** does the studio and the song-credit dispute feel true to the scene? Any slang that dates badly?
6. **Kuria and Teso names (cases 12, 19):** check name-origin tags and that neither character leans on a stereotype.
7. **Pipeline (case 17):** are gate books and laminated visitor badges standard in those blocks?
8. Sheng in cases 11, 14 and 18.
9. **Umoja Bank (case 13)** is fictional. A web search found no Kenyan bank of that name, but a licensed digital lender called "Umoja Fanisi" exists; the reader should confirm the name won't be read as a real institution.

## Region 2: changes made while writing the case files (deliverable 6)

The case files in `kesi-repo/www/cases/case-011.json` … `case-020.json` are the source of truth. These changes were made to the cards above while writing them:

| Case | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 11 | Monday, not Tuesday. Peninah's statement now has Abednego at the Fedha pump from about 20:15 to 20:40 | 26 May falls on a Monday in the campaign calendar; the alibi must cover the whole window (rule 6) |
| 11 | Sharon's admission says she locked up at about 20:40 | Places her at the stage during the window (rule 6) |
| 12 | Mwita's second claim is now "Nineteen years in 4C, never late until this year" | "In my flat all evening" was a second checkable lie; region 2 allows one liar per case |
| 12 | New statement-only witness: Rehema Wanjiku, vegetable seller at the gate | Gives Bonface an independent alibi and unlocks Lydia |
| 13 | Hodan's pencil note: "Call in the morning" | The case is on a Wednesday |

| 17 | The guard's yard testimony covers Tower A until the van at 20:55 | The guard admits missing the yard at 20:55, so the alibi must stop there; the crash was at 20:45 |

**Curve check (rule 13, warning).** On the validator's difficulty score, cases 17 and 18 measure one point easier than cases 14 and 15 (case 14 has a red herring and a twist; case 15 needs a warrant). Both are reported, not hidden. Neither is easy in play: 17 adds linked claims and an alibi friend, 18 makes a portrait the evidence.

## Part D — Region 3: Mombasa Old Town (cases 21–30)

**Region frame.** August and September on the coast: heat, humidity, the call to prayer over Old Town, dhows in the old harbour, the Likoni ferry, Kongowea at dawn, container yards past Shimanzi. Amani is sent down on secondment to work with Mombasa's coastal detectives, so the SCU desk travels: the region-select drawer swaps its manila folders for coast-office folders with a different station stamp. People here talk on their phones, pay on their phones and lie on their phones, so the phone becomes the main witness.

### D1. Region 3 rules

- **Phone and mobile-money evidence arrives (case 21).** Two record types, both fictional services:
  - **Jamii Mobile subscriber record:** calls and SMS (time, other number, duration; *not* message content) and the **mast** the phone was connected to, in time blocks.
  - **PesaPap statement:** every transaction with time, amount, the counterparty's registered name, and agent withdrawals.
- **Records requests (case 21).** Cost 1 credibility stamp each (a court order). Like warrants, the request form only appears once the player holds a **probable-cause fact** that ties a specific number to a specific person *and* to the case (a confirmation SMS with a name in it, a call on the victim's phone from a saved contact). Records come back limited to the dates that matter, which reflects real proportionality rules for subscriber data.
- **Masts are areas, not points.** The map draws each fictional mast as a coverage zone about 1–2 km across (Old Town North, Biashara, Likoni Ferry, Kisauni, Kongowea, Nyali, Shimanzi, Mtwapa…). A phone on a mast means "somewhere in that zone". Several cases are designed so that mast data *narrows* but never pins, and the player has to combine it with something physical. Mwalimu says this in her case-21 voice-note: *"A mast tells you the neighbourhood, not the door."*
- **Found phones.** A victim's phone (unlocked by family) or a willing witness's phone can be read directly: SMS and chat content, call log, PesaPap confirmation messages. This is phone evidence, free to read.
- **The WHY group arrives (case 21).** Charge sheets now read `{who} killed X because {why}`. WHY is its own group, confirmed separately (§2.3 batch confirmation), so a player can get WHO right and WHY wrong. Motive words appear in the bank only when discovered. Every WHY has **at least 5 motive options**, and every wrong motive has an authored refutation (validator rule 5). Typical decoys: another suspect's motive, a rumour, a debt that turns out to be paid.
- **Exactly one liar per case** (still region-2 level). From here the liar is the culprit in 6 cases and someone else in 4.
- **One red herring per case.** Every herring has a findable innocent explanation.

**Region curve at a glance**

| # | Title | Setting | Suspects | Chain | Herring | Liar | Twist | Stamps | Est. min |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 21 | Kanga za Pwani | Biashara Street | 3 | 3 | 1 | Culprit | — | 1 | 14 |
| 22 | The 06:40 Ferry | Likoni | 3 | 3 | 1 | Culprit | — | 1 | 14 |

| 24 | Nahodha | Old Port dhow harbour | 3 | 4 | 1 | Culprit | The "drowning" was murder; the dead man's phone travelled without him | 2 | 16 |

### Case 21 — Kanga za Pwani

`case-021` · Mombasa · 14 min · suspects 3 · chain 3 · herrings 1 · liars 1 (culprit) · groups WHO, WHY · stamps needed 1 (records)

**OB entry.** OB 17/08/08, 13:41. A shopkeeper on Biashara Street reports his neighbour, a kanga seller, found in the back store of her shop during Friday prayers.

**Setting.** Biashara Street at the edge of Old Town, Friday. Kanga and kikoi shops with cloth hanging in the doorways. Between about 12:30 and 13:30, for Jumaa prayers, most men pull their shutters half down and walk to the mosques; the street empties. Fictional shop **Kanga za Pwani**, 31 years old, with a front counter, a back store stacked with kanga bales, and a long brass-tipped measuring rod.

**Victim.** **Mwanajuma Athman**, 58, owner, widow. Struck with the shop's brass-tipped measuring rod in the back store.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dancan Odhiambo | 34 | Suspect | Shop manager for six years | **Culprit** |
| Faiz Athman | 27 | Suspect | Her nephew; wants to run the shop; shouted at her on Tuesday about his late uncle's share | Innocent (red herring): at Jumaa |
| Rukia Hamisi | 33 | Suspect | Tenant of the flat above the shop; two months behind on rent | Innocent: at a maternity home |
| Abubakar Hassan | 66 | Witness | Shopkeeper next door; found her | Innocent |
| Pili Juma | 41 | Witness | Regular customer | Innocent |

**What really happened.** For eight months, on busy days, Dancan propped a cardboard sign on the counter: *"Till haifanyi kazi — lipa namba hii"* ("the till isn't working, pay this number"), with his own PesaPap number. Customers paid him; he withdrew the money at agents every evening. On Thursday Mwanajuma read the shop till's monthly statement and saw takings collapse on the days he ran the shop. She told him to come on Friday during Jumaa, when the street would be empty, to explain. She made two glasses of tea. At about 12:55 she showed him the statement and said she'd go to the police on Saturday. He hit her with the measuring rod, took the statement, left by the back alley and walked to Mwembe Tayari bus park so he'd be seen there at 13:30.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Back store | Struck with the brass-tipped measuring rod, on the floor beside her |
| ev_tea | Physical | Counter | Two glasses of spiced tea, one finished, one barely touched: she was expecting a visitor during prayers |
| ev_envelope | Physical (found paper) | Her drawer | An empty envelope: "PesaPap Business — July statement". The statement itself is gone |
| ev_sign | Physical | Under the counter | Cardboard sign: **"TILL HAIFANYI KAZI — LIPA NAMBA HII: 07xx xxx 418"** (fictional number) |
| ev_pili | Phone (witness's phone) + witness | Pili Juma | Twice this month Dancan told her the till was broken and to pay "his number". She shows the confirmation SMS on her phone: **"Confirmed. KSh 6,400 sent to DANCAN ODHIAMBO 07xx xxx 418"**. **(Probable cause for a records request on that number)** |
| ev_abubakar | Witness | Neighbour | Pulled his shutter at 12:30 and went to the mosque; Mwanajuma stayed in, as she always does on Fridays to do her books. At 13:35 he saw her shutter half down and the back light on, called out, went in and found her |
| ev_records | **Records request** (Dancan's line) | Jamii Mobile + PesaPap | PesaPap: **112 incoming customer payments since December, KSh 341,900**, mostly on Saturdays, each evening withdrawn at agents. Jamii Mobile masts Friday: **12:30–13:20 Biashara**, **13:28 onwards Mwembe Tayari** |
| ev_mwembe | Witness | A kanga supplier at Mwembe Tayari (statement only) | Dancan arrived at 13:30, sweating, and said three times that he'd "been waiting here an hour" |
| ev_faiz | Witness | Mosque committee member (statement only) | Faiz recited Qur'an before the sermon and stayed until the end of prayers, about 12:20–13:25, in front of several hundred people |
| ev_rukia | Physical (found paper) + witness | Pwani Maternity Home (fictional) | Rukia signed in at 11:40 as birth companion for her sister; the nurse says she didn't leave until after 15:00 |
| ev_will | Physical (found paper) | Drawer | Copy of Mwanajuma's will: the shop to her daughter and Faiz jointly |
| ev_wagebook | Physical (found paper) | Drawer | Dancan's wages paid in full to July |
| ev_stockbook | Physical (found paper) | Counter | One kanga bale marked "missing" last month; a supplier's note clipped behind it: "Bale found at our Malindi depot, sending back" |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dancan Odhiambo | Cooperative | **"I was at Mwembe Tayari from half past twelve, waiting for the Malindi bus with our stock."** / **"The till works fine. Mama handled all the money."** | Both | Claim 1: `ev_records` (Biashara mast 12:30–13:20). Claim 2: `ev_sign` or `ev_pili` | Claim 1: *"I passed the shop at one, for a minute. She was fine when I left."* Claim 2: *"Sometimes the till was slow. I was helping customers."* |
| Faiz Athman | Cooperative | "I was in the mosque." | True | — | Topic "inheritance": the will gives him half; "I wanted to run it now, not when she's dead. I'm ashamed of what I said on Tuesday." |
| Rukia Hamisi | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_body`) | "I was with my sister. She had a baby girl at two o'clock." | True | — | Topic "rent": "Mama Mwanajuma told me to pay when I can. She was like that." |

**Proof**
1. `ev_tea` + `ev_abubakar` → Mwanajuma was alone in the shop during prayers, 12:30–13:35, and expecting someone.
2. Dancan's claim 1 + `ev_records` (mast) → he was in the Biashara zone 12:30–13:20, not at Mwembe Tayari; he admits being at the shop "for a minute" at 13:00.
3. `ev_sign` + `ev_pili` + `ev_records` (PesaPap) + `ev_envelope` → he'd been diverting customer payments to his own number for eight months, and the statement that would have shown it is missing → **WHO = Dancan Odhiambo**, **WHY = she'd found out he was diverting the shop's payments to his own number**.

**Eliminations**
- *WHO:* Faiz Athman: `ev_faiz`. Rukia Hamisi: `ev_rukia`. Abubakar Hassan: at the mosque (the same committee statement lists the shopkeepers present). Pili Juma: shopping at Marikiti, her own PesaPap messages show market payments at 12:40 and 13:05.
- *WHY:*

| Motive word | Refuted by |
|---|---|
| "she was cutting him out of the inheritance" | `ev_will`: the inheritance concerns her daughter and Faiz; Dancan has no claim |
| "she was about to evict him" | Dancan doesn't live there; the rent dispute is Rukia's, and Rukia's statement shows Mwanajuma had forgiven it |
| "his wages were unpaid" | `ev_wagebook` |
| "she accused him of stealing a bale" | `ev_stockbook`: the bale was found in Malindi |
| ✔ "she found out he was diverting the shop's payments to his own number" | — |

**Red herrings / twist.** Red herring: Faiz's Tuesday shouting match over the inheritance. No twist.

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Mwanajuma Athman because {why}.`
- WHO: Dancan Odhiambo, Faiz Athman, Rukia Hamisi, Abubakar Hassan, Pili Juma (5).
- WHY: the five motive words above (5).
- Halima. WHO right, WHY wrong: *"He did it. Now tell me why, or his lawyer will tell the court a story."* Both right: *"Three hundred and forty thousand shillings, two glasses of tea. Clean."*

**Credibility path.** 1 stamp: records request on 07xx xxx 418.

**New interface beat.** **The records request** (form, probable cause, the court-order stamp), **the mast map** (coverage circles over Old Town) and **the WHY blank**. Mwalimu's voice-note before the case covers all three in under 30 seconds.

**Kenyan texture.** Biashara Street's kanga trade and the proverbs printed on every kanga, Friday prayers emptying the street, spiced tea in glasses, "till isn't working, pay this number", a widow who runs her own books.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** kanga (printed cloth wrap with a proverb), kikoi (woven cloth), Jumaa (Friday prayer), Bi (respectful title for an older woman), lipa namba hii (pay this number), wakala (mobile-money agent).

**Images (5).** Portraits: Mwanajuma, Dancan, Faiz, Rukia. Location: Biashara Street at midday with shutters half down and kangas in the doorways.

**Audit tags.** Culprit M, 30s, Luo-origin name, motive cover-up (theft). Victim F, 50s, Swahili-origin name.

### Case 22 — The 06:40 Ferry

`case-022` · Mombasa · 14 min · suspects 3 · chain 3 · herrings 1 · liars 1 (culprit) · groups WHO, WHY · stamps needed 1 (records)

**OB entry.** OB 08/14/08, 07:48. A cleaner reports a fish trader found in the back of the Samaki Bora cold store, Likoni ferry side.

**Setting.** The Likoni ferry crossing at dawn: thousands of commuters, handcarts and fish traders crossing from Likoni to Mombasa island on ferries every few minutes. Fictional **Samaki Bora cold store**, run by a fish traders' collective, on the Likoni side: insulated rooms, ice blocks, a collection book where traders sign out their crates.

**Victim.** **Agnes Auma**, 44, fish trader. Struck with an ice mallet in the back room.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mwanasiti Mwinyi | 31 | Suspect | Fish trader in the same collective | **Culprit** |
| Thomas Owino | 47 | Suspect | Agnes's ex-husband; they've fought for a year over their children's school fees | Innocent (red herring): at work |
| Mariamu Mbaraka | 39 | Suspect | Trader who shares the initials "M.M." in the collection book | Innocent: at Marikiti |
| Omari Mwinyi | 36 | Witness | Mwanasiti's husband | Innocent |
| Zaituni Omar | 50 | Witness | Cold-store cleaner; found her | Innocent |
| John Charo | 25 | Witness (statement only) | Boda rider at the ferry | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Mwanasiti found out last week that her husband Omari had been sending Agnes money every month and that they'd been seeing each other for a year. At 06:30 she called Agnes and said, "Come to the cold store, we need to talk." She signed out her crates at 06:52, waited until the cleaner left for ice, and at about 07:05 hit Agnes with an ice mallet. At 07:18 she paid a boda by PesaPap to take her to the ferry, and crossed on the 07:30. Later she told everyone she'd crossed at 06:40 as she does every day.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Back room | Struck with an ice mallet; Agnes's apron pocket still holds KSh 7,200 |
| ev_agnes_phone | Phone (victim's, unlocked by her sister) | Agnes's apron | Call log: incoming **06:30** from contact **"Mwanasiti"**, 48 seconds. Chat with Omari Mwinyi: months of messages; last week "Nimekutumia elfu tano" ("I've sent you five thousand"). **(Probable cause for a records request on Mwanasiti's number)** |
| ev_collection | Physical (found paper) | Cold-store collection book | "**M.M. — 2 crates kingfish — 06:52**". Two traders in the collective sign as M.M. |
| ev_zaituni | Witness | Cleaner | Agnes arrived 06:35. Zaituni left at 06:50 to fetch ice blocks from the factory up the road (`ev_icereceipt`), came back 07:35, found her at 07:40 |
| ev_icereceipt | Physical (found paper) | Zaituni | Ice factory receipt 07:20 |
| ev_records | **Records request** (Mwanasiti's line) | Jamii Mobile + PesaPap | Call to Agnes 06:30. Mast **Likoni Ferry** from 06:20 until **07:26**; Mombasa Island (Old Port) from 07:45. PesaPap: **07:18, KSh 100 to JOHN CHARO** |
| ev_charo | Witness | Boda rider | Picked up a woman with two fish crates outside Samaki Bora at 07:18, took her to the ferry; she paid by phone and was "shaking" |
| ev_mariamu | Physical (found paper) | Her Marikiti stall receipt | Market fee paid at Marikiti, Mombasa island, **06:35** |
| ev_ferry_timetable | Physical | Ferry board | Crossings every ~10–15 minutes at peak; the crossing takes about 10 minutes |
| ev_owino | Physical (found paper) | Thomas shows it | Security-company clock card: night shift at a Nyali hotel until 07:00, signed out 07:02; Nyali is on the far side of the island from Likoni |
| ev_omari | Witness | Husband | Admits the relationship with Agnes. Says Mwanasiti "found the messages last week and went silent" |
| ev_chama | Physical (found paper) | Collective's chama book | Agnes's loan from the collective fully repaid in June |
| ev_bays | Physical (found paper) | Cold-store bay allocation sheet | Agnes bay 3, Mwanasiti bay 7, unchanged for two years |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mwanasiti Mwinyi | Cooperative | **"I crossed on the 06:40 ferry like every morning. I was at the old port by seven."** / "I didn't speak to Agnes today." | Both (one liar) | Claim 1: `ev_records` (mast) or `ev_charo`. Claim 2: `ev_agnes_phone` (her call at 06:30) | *"I called her. I wanted her to stop. I went to the cold store and we shouted. Then I left for the ferry."* / *"Ask my husband who he sends money to every month."* |
| Thomas Owino | Cooperative | "I was on night shift in Nyali." | True | — | Topic "fees": the dispute is real and bitter, "but she's my children's mother" |
| Mariamu Mbaraka | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_collection`) | "That M.M. isn't me. I was in town by half six." | True | — | Shows `ev_mariamu` |

**Proof**
1. `ev_collection` + `ev_mariamu` → the M.M. who signed out crates at 06:52 can't be Mariamu, who was on the island at 06:35; it was Mwanasiti.
2. Mwanasiti's claims + `ev_agnes_phone` + `ev_records` → she called Agnes to the cold store, stayed in the Likoni zone until 07:26 (not the 06:40 ferry), and paid a boda from outside the cold store at 07:18.
3. `ev_zaituni` + `ev_charo` → Agnes was alone after 06:50; Mwanasiti left the cold store at 07:18 shaking → **WHO = Mwanasiti Mwinyi**. `ev_agnes_phone` + `ev_omari` → **WHY = she'd discovered Agnes was seeing her husband**.

**Eliminations**
- *WHO:* Mariamu Mbaraka: step 1. Thomas Owino: `ev_owino` (out at 07:02 in Nyali; he couldn't reach Likoni through the island and across the ferry by 07:18). Zaituni Omar: `ev_icereceipt`. Omari Mwinyi: at his own work at the old port from 06:00 (his employer's statement).
- *WHY:*

| Motive word | Refuted by |
|---|---|
| "a fight over cold-store space" | `ev_bays` |
| "an unpaid chama loan" | `ev_chama` |
| "to rob her" | `ev_body` (KSh 7,200 untouched) |
| "her ex-husband's school-fees fight" | That's Thomas's motive, and Thomas is eliminated |
| ✔ "she'd found out Agnes was seeing her husband" | — |

**Red herrings / twist.** Red herring: the bitter ex-husband. No twist.

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Agnes Auma because {why}.` WHO: Mwanasiti Mwinyi, Thomas Owino, Mariamu Mbaraka, Zaituni Omar, Omari Mwinyi (5). WHY: the five words above.

**Credibility path.** 1 stamp: records request on Mwanasiti's number.

**New interface beat.** **Geography across water.** The map shows the channel, the ferry crossing and mast zones on both shores; the time it takes to cross becomes part of an alibi. Also the **found phone** of a victim, read with the family's consent.

**Kenyan texture.** The Likoni ferry at dawn, fish traders and cold stores, ice-factory runs, boda riders paid by phone, a husband's secret sent in monthly mobile-money transfers.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** samaki (fish), kivuko (ferry), barafu (ice), boda.

**Images (5).** Portraits: Agnes, Mwanasiti, Thomas, Mariamu. Location: Likoni ferry ramp at sunrise, crowds and handcarts.

**Audit tags.** Culprit F, 30s, Digo-origin name, motive relationship/jealousy. Victim F, 40s, Luo-origin name.

### Case 23 — Turmeric

`case-023` · Mombasa · 15 min · suspects 3 · chain 3 · herrings 1 · liars 1 (**innocent assistant**) · groups WHO, WHY · stamps needed 1 (records) · **spine background detail**

**OB entry.** OB 22/20/08, 16:31. A shop assistant reports her employer, owner of a spice shop on Ndia Kuu, found dead in the shop.

**Setting.** Ndia Kuu, the old main street of Mombasa's Old Town: coral-stone houses with carved wooden doors and balconies. Fictional **Karimjee & Sons Spices**, a narrow shop in a heritage building, sacks of cumin, cardamom, cloves and turmeric open at the front. The building is worth a fortune to developers.

**Victim.** **Farida Karimjee**, 64, widow, owner of the shop and the building. Struck with a brass pestle. A sack of **turmeric** is split across the floor.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Yasmin Karimjee | 55 | Suspect | Her late husband's sister; co-heir to the building through the family trust; wants to sell it to a developer | **Culprit** |
| Ken Mutisya | 45 | Suspect | Developer's representative; told Farida last week "you'll sell, one way or another" | Innocent (red herring): at a planning meeting |
| Rahma Abeid | 22 | Suspect | Shop assistant | Innocent; **the liar** |
| Imran Karimjee | 38 | Witness (by phone) | Farida's son, in Nairobi on business | Innocent |
| Hussein Abdulkadir | 58 | Witness | Carved-door maker across the street | Innocent |

**What really happened.** A developer offered KSh 40 million for the building. Yasmin, short of money, wanted to sell; Farida refused and wrote "NEVER" across the offer letter. Yasmin went further: three days earlier she paid "document services" for a transfer that would let her sell without Farida's consent. On the day, she texted Farida at 14:58: "Nakuja saa tisa na nusu na karatasi" ("I'm coming at half past three with the papers"). Rahma, secretly job-hunting, had slipped out at 15:35 for an interview in Nyali and left a "back soon" sign on the door. Yasmin arrived at about 15:45. Farida tore up the papers. Yasmin hit her with the pestle; in the struggle the turmeric sack split, and the yellow powder went over Yasmin's white dupatta and her shoes. She left by tuk-tuk at 16:12.

| ev_turmeric | Physical | Floor | Turmeric powder: stains bright yellow, doesn't wash out of cotton; a smudged print of a woman's flat sandal in the powder, heading to the door |
| ev_farida_phone | Phone (victim's, unlocked by Imran) | Counter | SMS from **"Yasmin"** at **14:58**: *"Nakuja saa tisa na nusu na karatasi."* **(Probable cause for a records request on Yasmin's number)** |
| ev_offer | Physical (found paper) | Drawer | Developer's offer, KSh 40 million; Farida's handwriting across it: **"NEVER."** |

PesaPap: tuk-tuk fares **15:38** and **16:12**. Three days earlier: **KSh 15,000 to Till 880 214, MVUA HOLDINGS — "title & transfer documents"** (spine; not needed) |

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rahma Abeid | Cooperative | **"I was in the shop all afternoon. Nobody came."** | Yes | `ev_hussein` or `ev_rahma_sales` | *"I went for an interview. Mama didn't know. I left the sign. I'm so sorry."* Shows `ev_interview` (new fact: the shop was unattended 15:35–16:25) |
| Yasmin Karimjee | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_farida_phone`) | "I didn't go in the end. I was home." (a flat denial: she won't give times) | — | — | Topic "building": "That building is half mine. She was sentimental." Topic "turmeric" (after `ev_dupatta`): silence |
| Ken Mutisya | Cooperative | "I was presenting at the county planning office." | True | — | Topic "threat": "I meant the courts. Developers sue, they don't kill." |

**Proof**
1. Rahma's claim + `ev_hussein` / `ev_rahma_sales` → the shop was unattended 15:35–16:25; she was at an interview in Nyali. Her lie hid a job hunt, not a crime.
2. `ev_farida_phone` + `ev_records` → Yasmin said she was coming at 15:30 with papers, and her phone was in the Old Town zone 15:42–16:14, with tuk-tuk fares there and back.
3. `ev_turmeric` + `ev_dupatta` + `ev_torn` → turmeric from the split sack is on Yasmin's dupatta, and the transfer papers she brought are torn in the bin → **WHO = Yasmin Karimjee**; with `ev_offer` + `ev_trust`, **WHY = Farida refused to sell the family building**.

**Eliminations**
- *WHO:* Rahma Abeid: step 1 + `ev_interview`. Ken Mutisya: `ev_mutisya`. Imran Karimjee: in Nairobi (hotel bill). Hussein Abdulkadir: working at his door in the street the whole time.
- *WHY:*

| Motive word | Refuted by |
|---|---|
| "an old family debt" | `ev_ledger` (settled) |
| "she'd been cut out of the spice business" | The trust deed covers only the building; Yasmin never had a share of the shop (Imran) |
| "she caught her stealing from the till" | Cash box full |
| "the developer's threat" | That's Ken's pressure, not Yasmin's motive; and Ken is eliminated |
| ✔ "Farida refused to sell the family building" | — |

**Red herrings / twist.** Red herring: Ken Mutisya's threat. The innocent liar isn't counted as a twist here; players met that idea in case 14.

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Farida Karimjee because {why}.` WHO: Yasmin Karimjee, Ken Mutisya, Rahma Abeid, Imran Karimjee, Hussein Abdulkadir (5). WHY: five words above.

**Credibility path.** 1 stamp: records request on Yasmin's number.

**New interface beat.** **Language as evidence.** SMS in Swahili with a tap-to-translate toggle (the glossary inline). The time "saa tisa na nusu" is 15:30 in Swahili time-telling (saa tisa = the ninth hour after 06:00); the glossary explains it, and the translation toggle shows "3:30 pm". It's a small, very Kenyan detail that matters to the timeline.

**Kenyan texture.** Old Town's carved doors and heritage buildings under developer pressure, spice sacks, family trusts, Swahili time ("saa tisa" for 3 pm), "narudi sasa hivi" signs, tuk-tuks between Ganjoni and Old Town.

**Spine.** `ev_records` carries `t_mvua`: Yasmin paid Till 880 214 for "title & transfer documents". Not needed for this case. On solve it's pinned to the Pattern File: Mvua is now selling forged transfers, not just titles.

**Glossary.** saa tisa (3 pm in Swahili time; hours count from 6 am), narudi sasa hivi (back shortly), dupatta (long scarf), kinu (mortar).

**Images (5).** Portraits: Farida, Yasmin (white dupatta, faint yellow stain visible on zoom), Rahma, Ken. Location: Ndia Kuu with carved doors in late-afternoon light.

**Audit tags.** Culprit F, 50s, Kenyan-Asian-origin name, motive land/inheritance. Victim F, 60s, Kenyan-Asian-origin name. *Note: this is the first Kenyan-Asian culprit; Kenyan-Asian characters have appeared as innocent suppliers and witnesses in cases 8 and 13.*
