### Case 24 — Nahodha

`case-024` · Mombasa · 16 min · suspects 3 · **chain 4** · herrings 1 · liars 1 (culprit) · groups WHO, WHY · stamps needed 2 (two records requests) · **twist: the "drowning" was murder; the dead man's phone travelled without him**

**OB entry.** OB 05/27/08, 06:22. Fishermen report a dhow captain found in the water beside his moored dhow at the Old Port. **Recorded as suspected accidental drowning.** Amani is asked to "close it quickly".

**Setting.** The Old Port dhow harbour below Fort Jesus, before dawn. Wooden dhows moored to buoys, small rowing boats ferrying crews out, the smell of fish and diesel. Fictional dhow **Upepo Mwema** ("good wind").

**Victim.** **Khamis Bwanaheri**, 61, nahodha (captain) from Lamu, sailing Upepo Mwema for 30 years. Found in the water at 06:10. A head wound the harbour assumes he got falling against the hull.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| James Ireri | 45 | Suspect | Runs fictional **Sunset Dhow Cruises** for tourists; wanted Khamis's mooring and his dhow | **Culprit** |
| Swaleh Mbwana | 28 | Suspect | Khamis's crewman, sacked last week for siphoning fuel | Innocent (red herring): on night watch elsewhere |
| Abdalla Khamis | 30 | Suspect | Khamis's son, captain of the family's second boat in Lamu | Innocent: in Lamu |
| Fumo Shali | 70 | Witness | Old fisherman | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Ireri had offered twice to buy Upepo Mwema and its mooring; Khamis wrote "HAPANA" on the offer. At midnight Ireri rowed out to make a last offer. Khamis refused, they fought on deck, and Ireri hit him with a belaying pin. He rolled Khamis into the water, set his sandals neatly on the deck as if he'd gone in himself, took his phone and rowed back. At home in Kisauni at 02:14 he used Khamis's phone to text the son: *"Naenda kuvua peke yangu, usijali"* ("I'm going fishing alone, don't worry"), to make it look like an accident at sea. He then switched the phone off and threw it away. He didn't know that Khamis couldn't read or write SMS: he only ever made calls.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Harbour | Head wound; found beside the dhow |
| ev_sandals | Physical | Dhow deck | Khamis's sandals, side by side, neatly placed at the rail |
| ev_offer | Physical (found paper) | Dhow cabin | "Sunset Dhow Cruises — offer for vessel Upepo Mwema and mooring, KSh 2.8 million." Across it in Arabic-script Swahili and in Latin letters: **"HAPANA"** (written by his son, as Khamis dictated: "Baba can't write") |
| ev_son_phone | Phone (witness's phone) | Abdalla Khamis, by call from Lamu | SMS from his father's number at **02:14**: *"Naenda kuvua peke yangu, usijali."* **(Probable cause for a records request on the victim's line)** |
| ev_son | Witness | Son | "Baba never sent an SMS in his life. He can't read or write. He calls. He called me at 23:30 to say 'the cruise man' was coming at midnight about the mooring. **The cruise man is James Ireri.**" **(Probable cause for a records request on Ireri's number)** |
| ev_records_khamis | **Records request** (victim's line) | Jamii Mobile | Call to son 23:30. Mast **Old Town** until **01:40**; **Kisauni 01:55–02:20**; SMS sent **02:14 via Kisauni**; then off |
| ev_records_ireri | **Records request** (Ireri's line) | Jamii Mobile + PesaPap | Mast **Old Town 23:50–01:40**; **Kisauni from 01:55** (his home zone). PesaPap: last month **KSh 40,000 to KHAMIS BWANAHERI**, "charter Upepo Mwema", paid in full |
| ev_fumo | Witness | Old fisherman | Saw a small boat row out to Upepo Mwema around midnight, heard raised voices, then "the oars going back fast" |
| ev_dinghy | Physical | Sunset Dhow Cruises jetty | Ireri's rowing dinghy, oars still wet at 07:00, a smear of the dhow's blue hull paint on its bow |
| ev_swaleh | Physical (found paper) | Marikiti cold room | Night-watch clock card 20:00–06:00 |
| ev_lamu | Witness | Lamu harbour master's office (statement only) | Abdalla's boat moored in Lamu all night; he was seen at 05:00 prayers |
| ev_harbourlog | Physical (found paper) | Harbour master's office | No report against Ireri for smuggling or anything else; last year's capsized tourist trip was a different operator's boat |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| James Ireri | Cooperative | **"I haven't been to the old harbour since Sunday. I was home in Kisauni all night."** / "Khamis and I were friends. I chartered his dhow." | First claim | `ev_records_ireri` (Old Town mast 23:50–01:40) or `ev_fumo` + `ev_dinghy` | *"I rowed out at midnight. I made him a fair offer. He said no again. I rowed back. He was alive."* (new fact: he was on Upepo Mwema at midnight) |
| Swaleh Mbwana | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_offer`) | "I was on night watch at Marikiti." | True | — | Topic "fuel": admits it, ashamed; "Mzee gave me a second chance three times" |
| Abdalla Khamis | Cooperative (by phone) | "I was in Lamu." | True | — | `ev_son` |

**Proof**
1. `ev_son_phone` + `ev_son` → the 02:14 SMS can't have come from Khamis, who couldn't read or write. Someone else had his phone.
2. `ev_records_khamis` → his phone left the Old Town zone at 01:40 and was in **Kisauni** when the SMS was sent. Khamis was in the harbour; his phone had travelled without him. This is murder, not an accident (`ev_sandals` is staging).
3. `ev_records_ireri` + Ireri's broken claim → Ireri's phone made exactly the same move: Old Town until 01:40, Kisauni from 01:55. He admits being on the dhow at midnight.
4. `ev_fumo` + `ev_dinghy` → a boat rowed out at midnight, voices were raised, it rowed back fast; Ireri's dinghy has the dhow's paint on its bow → **WHO = James Ireri**; with `ev_offer`, **WHY = Khamis refused to sell him the dhow and its mooring**.

**Eliminations**
- *WHO:* Swaleh Mbwana: `ev_swaleh`. Abdalla Khamis: `ev_lamu`. Fumo Shali: on his own boat at the far mooring, where other fishermen saw him. Hamza Athumani: the harbour office's night log shows him at home off duty until 05:45, and he only logged the "drowning" from the fishermen's report at 06:20.
- *WHY:*

| Motive word | Refuted by |
|---|---|
| "an unpaid charter fee" | `ev_records_ireri` (paid in full) |
| "Khamis had reported him for smuggling" | `ev_harbourlog` (no report) |
| "the crewman's stolen fuel" | That's Swaleh's dispute; Swaleh is eliminated |
| "revenge for a capsized tourist trip" | `ev_harbourlog` (another operator) |
| ✔ "Khamis refused to sell him the dhow and its mooring" | — |

**Red herrings / twist.**
- Red herring: the sacked crewman.
- **Twist:** the case arrives as an accident. The player has to prove a murder happened at all, using the one thing the killer didn't know: the victim couldn't read. Mwalimu, after the verdict: *"You read the man before you read the phone. Good."*

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Khamis Bwanaheri because {why}.` WHO: James Ireri, Swaleh Mbwana, Abdalla Khamis, Fumo Shali, and the harbour master's clerk who logged the "drowning", Hamza Athumani (5). WHY: five words above.

**Credibility path.** 2 stamps: records on the victim's line and on Ireri's line.

**New interface beat.** **Overlaying two records.** Mast timelines from two phones can be stacked on one strip; matching moves line up. The first "two phones moved together" deduction, used often in later regions.

**Kenyan texture.** Dhow captains (nahodha) and the Lamu–Mombasa trade, sunset cruises for tourists squeezing out working boats, harbour moorings worth more than the boats, an elder who can't read texting being the giveaway, Arabic-script Swahili.

**Spine.** None. *(Mvua doesn't appear here, deliberately. Case 30 later reveals Mvua had also tried to hire Upepo Mwema to carry cartons to Lamu and Khamis refused; that's a separate reveal, not a link to Ireri, and case 30's card says so explicitly so players don't over-connect.)*

**Glossary.** nahodha (captain), jahazi (dhow), hapana (no), kuvua (to fish), Upepo Mwema (good wind).

**Images (6).** Portraits: Khamis, James Ireri, Swaleh, Abdalla. Location: Old Port dhow harbour at dawn under Fort Jesus. Evidence photo: the neatly placed sandals on deck.

**Audit tags.** Culprit M, 40s, Embu-origin name, motive business rivalry. Victim M, 60s, Bajuni-origin name.

### Case 25 — Wrong Number

`case-025` · Mombasa · 15 min · suspects 3 · chain 3 · herrings 1 · liars 1 (culprit) · groups WHO, WHY · stamps needed 1 (records)

**OB entry.** OB 33/02/09, 11:14. A porter reports a tomato wholesaler found behind the produce sheds at Kongowea market.

**Setting.** Kongowea market, one of the biggest open-air markets on the coast, a Tuesday morning. Lorries of tomatoes from Taveta, onions from upcountry, mangoes; porters, handcarts, weighing scales with cast-iron weights.

**Victim.** **Everlyne Nasimiyu**, 36, tomato wholesaler. Struck with a 5 kg cast-iron weight from a scale.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mwanaidi Mwatsahu | 23 | Suspect | Sells second-hand phones at Mwembe Tayari; received Everlyne's money by mistake | **Culprit** |
| Benard Mwakitele | 52 | Suspect | Lorry driver from Taveta; Everlyne owed him KSh 85,000 for the load and he threatened "no money, no more tomatoes" | Innocent (red herring): at the weighbridge |
| Linet Chepchumba | 41 | Suspect | Everlyne's business partner; arguing about splitting up | Innocent: in a bank queue |
| Saidi Mwero | 34 | Witness | Porter | Innocent |

**What really happened.** On Monday Everlyne sent **KSh 85,000** to pay Benard for the lorry, mistyped one digit, and the money went to Mwanaidi. Mwanaidi saw the confirmation, withdrew all of it at an agent three minutes later, and ignored Everlyne's calls. Everlyne's reversal request failed because the money was gone. The confirmation SMS had given Everlyne the recipient's registered name, and a cousin knew Mwanaidi. On Tuesday Mwanaidi came to Kongowea to "sort it out"; behind the sheds Everlyne grabbed her phone pouch to stop her leaving, and Mwanaidi hit her with a weight from a nearby scale.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Behind the produce sheds | Struck with a 5 kg scale weight |
| ev_everlyne_phone | Phone (victim's, unlocked by her sister) | Her apron | PesaPap confirmation, Monday 16:02: **"KSh 85,000 sent to MWANAIDI MWATSAHU 07xx xxx 309"**. Then: "Reversal request received" (16:10) and **"Reversal failed: recipient has insufficient balance"** (16:40). 11 unanswered calls to that number. Tuesday 10:05 incoming call from it, 2 minutes **(probable cause for a records request)** |
| ev_lorry_number | Physical (found paper) | Her apron | Benard's number on a scrap of paper: **07xx xxx 390**, one digit different (309 vs 390) |
| ev_records | **Records request** (Mwanaidi's line) | PesaPap + Jamii Mobile | Monday 16:02 received KSh 85,000; **16:05 agent withdrawal KSh 85,000**. Tuesday: call to Everlyne 10:05; mast **Kongowea 10:20–10:55**; PesaPap 10:52 tuk-tuk fare from Kongowea |
| ev_saidi | Witness | Porter | At about 10:40 saw Everlyne arguing behind the sheds with a young woman carrying a **pink phone pouch** on a strap; Everlyne grabbed at the pouch. He was called away; at 11:05 another porter found her |
| ev_pouch | Physical | Mwanaidi's stall at Mwembe Tayari | Her trade pouch: pink, a broken strap clip, tomato juice stain |
| ev_receipt_sale | Physical (found paper) | Everlyne's receipt book | Sold 12 crates to a hotel buyer at 10:35 |
| ev_weighbridge | Physical (found paper) | Benard shows it | Weighbridge ticket, **Mariakani, 10:30**, his lorry, outbound to Taveta (about an hour from Kongowea) |
| ev_bankqueue | Physical (found paper) | Linet shows it | Bank queue ticket, town branch, issued 10:10, served 11:02 |
| ev_ob_check | Physical (found paper) | Station OB search | No police report filed by Everlyne about the money |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mwanaidi Mwatsahu | Cooperative | **"That money came by mistake and I sent it straight back."** / **"I've never met her."** | Both | Claim 1: `ev_records` (withdrawn at 16:05) or `ev_everlyne_phone` (reversal failed). Claim 2: `ev_records` (call and mast) + `ev_saidi` | *"I needed it. My mother is in hospital. I went to tell her I'd pay it back slowly. She shouted, she grabbed my pouch, I pulled away and left."* |
| Benard Mwakitele | Cooperative | "I was on the road back to Taveta." | True | — | Shows `ev_weighbridge` and `ev_lorry_number`: "She told me on the phone she'd sent it to the wrong number. I didn't believe her." |
| Linet Chepchumba | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_receipt_sale`) | "I was at the bank." | True | — | Topic "partnership": they were splitting up "politely" |

**Proof**
1. `ev_everlyne_phone` + `ev_lorry_number` → Everlyne sent KSh 85,000 to Mwanaidi by mistake (one digit off) and couldn't get it back.
2. Mwanaidi's claims + `ev_records` → she withdrew it within three minutes, called Everlyne on Tuesday, and was in the Kongowea zone 10:20–10:55.
3. `ev_saidi` + `ev_pouch` → the woman fighting with Everlyne at 10:40 carried a pink pouch Everlyne grabbed; Mwanaidi's pouch has a broken clip and a tomato stain → **WHO = Mwanaidi Mwatsahu**, **WHY = she wouldn't return money sent to her by mistake**.

**Eliminations**
- *WHO:* Benard Mwakitele: `ev_weighbridge`. Linet Chepchumba: `ev_bankqueue`. Saidi Mwero: called to unload a lorry at 10:42 (the other porter's statement). Godfrey Mwangemi: he left in the hotel van with the van driver at 10:37 (the driver's statement) and the delivery note shows them unloading at the hotel kitchen in Nyali at 10:55.
- *WHY:*

| Motive word | Refuted by |
|---|---|
| "a fight over a stolen phone" | Everlyne's phone is still in her apron |
| "a tomato debt" | That's Benard's grievance; Mwanaidi doesn't trade tomatoes |
| "a quarrel over stall space" | Mwanaidi has no stall at Kongowea |
| "Everlyne had reported her to the police" | `ev_ob_check` (no report) |
| ✔ "she wouldn't return money sent to her by mistake" | — |

**Red herrings / twist.** Red herring: the unpaid lorry driver who threatened her. No twist.

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Everlyne Nasimiyu because {why}.` WHO: Mwanaidi Mwatsahu, Benard Mwakitele, Linet Chepchumba, Saidi Mwero, and the hotel buyer from `ev_receipt_sale`, Godfrey Mwangemi (5). WHY: five words above.

**Credibility path.** 1 stamp.

**New interface beat.** **Reading a mobile-money statement.** Agent withdrawals, reversal requests and failure messages are explained once, in-world, by Halima: *"A reversal fails when the money's already out. Whoever withdrew it in three minutes knew exactly what they had."*

**Kenyan texture.** Sending money to the wrong number, one of the most common everyday disasters in Kenya; reversal requests; agents; Kongowea's tomato trade from Taveta; weighbridge tickets on the Mombasa road.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** namba (number), kurudisha pesa (return money), wakala (agent), nyanya (tomatoes).

**Images (5).** Portraits: Everlyne, Mwanaidi (pink phone pouch visible), Benard, Linet. Location: Kongowea market at mid-morning.

**Audit tags.** Culprit F, 20s, Duruma-origin name, motive money/debt. Victim F, 30s, Luhya-origin name.

### Case 26 — Paid in Advance

`case-026` · Mombasa · 16 min · suspects 3 · chain 3 · herrings 1 · liars 1 (**bribed witness**) · groups WHO, WHY · stamps needed 1 (records)

**OB entry.** OB 46/09/09, 22:19. A police patrol reports a tuk-tuk driver found slumped in his parked vehicle on Mama Ngina Drive. A witness at the scene describes "a tall man in a cap" running away.

**Setting.** Mama Ngina Drive, the seafront promenade, at night: coconut-water sellers, cassava crisps fried on carts, families walking, tuk-tuks waiting for fares.

**Victim.** **Abdalla Swaleh**, 32, tuk-tuk driver. Struck with a tyre lever from his own tuk-tuk.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Felister Mghanga | 47 | Suspect | A mother whose son Jeremy, 19, was killed eight months ago on New Year's night by a hit-and-run tuk-tuk; the case was never solved | **Culprit** |
| Said Omar Mbarak | 55 | Suspect | Owns the tuk-tuk Abdalla rents; Abdalla was two weeks behind on daily payments | Innocent: at the Makadara grounds |
| Omari Kai | 30 | Suspect | Rival driver; fought Abdalla over the Mama Ngina stage | Innocent: on a fare to Bamburi |
| Rajab Mwaringa | 41 | Witness | Tuk-tuk driver who "saw a tall man in a cap" | **The liar (bribed)** |
| Mama Chiku (Chiku Rashidi) | 60 | Witness | Coconut-water seller | Innocent |

**What really happened.** In August a mechanic told Felister that on 2 January, the day after her son was killed, Abdalla's tuk-tuk came in with a smashed front fork and windscreen, paid cash, no questions. She watched Abdalla for weeks. On Tuesday she paid KSh 200 by PesaPap for a ride "along the drive", sat in the back, and when he stopped at 21:35 she asked him if he remembered New Year's night. He laughed. She hit him with the tyre lever from under the seat. Then she called Rajab, a driver she knew, and paid him KSh 3,000 to tell the police he'd seen a tall man in a cap run off.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Tuk-tuk | Struck with the tuk-tuk's tyre lever |
| ev_abdalla_phone | Phone (victim's, unlocked by his brother) | Dashboard holder | Last incoming PesaPap: **21:28, KSh 200 from FELISTER MGHANGA**, "fare". No calls after 21:20 |
| ev_chiku | Witness | Coconut seller | Saw **a woman in a red kanga** get into Abdalla's tuk-tuk "like a passenger" at about 21:30; it drove a little way up the drive and stopped. Didn't see her get out. **Didn't see any tall man in a cap.** Says Rajab only arrived after the police, "about ten past ten" **(probable cause for a records request on Rajab)** |
| ev_rajab_statement | Witness | Rajab | "At about 21:40 I saw a tall man in a cap hit him and run towards Likoni Road." |
| ev_records | **Records request** (Rajab's line) | Jamii Mobile + PesaPap | Mast **Bamburi until 22:02**, Mama Ngina zone from 22:10. Incoming call 21:44 from **FELISTER MGHANGA**'s number. PesaPap **22:40: KSh 3,000 from FELISTER MGHANGA** |
| ev_glovebox | Physical (found paper) | Tuk-tuk glovebox | Garage receipt, **2 January**: "Front fork straightened, windscreen replaced — cash" |
| ev_old_ob | Physical (found paper) | Station OB archive (free to search) | **OB 03/01/01**: hit-and-run, Nyali Road, 23:50, pedestrian Jeremy Mghanga, 19, died at scene; "three-wheeler, fled, no plate seen". File status: **pending, no suspect** |
| ev_kanga | Physical | Felister's home (cooperative; she hands it over) | A red kanga, washed that night, still damp the next morning |
| ev_makadara | Witness | Football club secretary (statement only) | Said Mbarak was at the evening match committee at Makadara grounds 19:00–22:30 |
| ev_kai | Phone (witness's phone) | Omari Kai shows it | Fare payment 21:15 from a passenger to Bamburi; mast Bamburi until 22:20 (he shows his own call log) |
| ev_handbag | Physical | Felister | Her handbag; nothing of Abdalla's in it |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rajab Mwaringa | Cooperative | **"I saw a tall man in a cap hit him at 21:40 and run."** | Yes | `ev_records` (he was in Bamburi until 22:02; she paid him 3,000 at 22:40) or `ev_chiku` | *"I didn't see anything. She called me crying and gave me three thousand to say it. She said he killed her boy."* |
| Felister Mghanga | Cooperative | "I went for a ride on the drive. He was alive when I got out." / She won't say more until shown `ev_old_ob` | — (only a vague denial) | — | After `ev_old_ob`: *"Eight months. Nobody came. Nobody looked. I looked."* |
| Said Omar Mbarak | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_glovebox`) | "I was at the football committee." | True | — | Topic "January": "He told me he hit a pothole. I believed him." |

**Proof**
1. `ev_abdalla_phone` + `ev_chiku` → at 21:28 Felister paid Abdalla a fare, and at 21:30 a woman in a red kanga got in his tuk-tuk; it stopped up the drive.
2. Rajab's claim + `ev_records` → the "tall man in a cap" was invented; Rajab wasn't there, and Felister called him at 21:44 and paid him KSh 3,000 at 22:40.
3. `ev_glovebox` + `ev_old_ob` + `ev_kanga` → Abdalla's tuk-tuk was repaired the day after Jeremy's hit-and-run; Felister is Jeremy's mother; her red kanga was washed that night → **WHO = Felister Mghanga**, **WHY = she believed his tuk-tuk had killed her son**.

**Eliminations**
- *WHO:* Said Omar Mbarak: `ev_makadara`. Omari Kai: `ev_kai`. Rajab Mwaringa: `ev_records` (Bamburi until 22:02). Chiku Rashidi: at her cart in full view of the drive.
- *WHY:*

| Motive word | Refuted by |
|---|---|
| "a dispute over the fare" | `ev_abdalla_phone` (paid in advance) |
| "to steal from him" | His takings pouch untouched; `ev_handbag` |
| "the owner's unpaid daily rent" | That's Said's grievance; Said is eliminated |
| "a road-rage fight with a stranger" | Rajab's invented story, broken |
| ✔ "she believed his tuk-tuk had killed her son" | — |

**Red herrings / twist.** Red herring: the "tall man in a cap", a phantom created by the bribed witness. No twist.

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Abdalla Swaleh because {why}.` WHO: Felister Mghanga, Said Omar Mbarak, Omari Kai, Rajab Mwaringa, Chiku Rashidi (5). WHY: five words above.

Halima, on a correct charge: *"Two files, then. His and her son's. Get me the garage."* After the verdict, the old hit-and-run file is reopened and closed by the garage receipt: a quiet echo of Amani's own unfinished file.

**Credibility path.** 1 stamp.

**New interface beat.** **The station's own archive.** The OB archive can be searched by name or date for free. First time an old, unsolved file is evidence. Mwalimu, after the case, without explanation: *"Old files don't close themselves."*

**Kenyan texture.** Mama Ngina Drive at night, coconut water and cassava crisps, tuk-tuks rented by the day from owners, hit-and-runs that never get solved, mobile-money fares paid in advance.

**Spine.** Thematic only (`t_joseph`-adjacent: an unsolved old file). No pin.

**Glossary.** tuk-tuk / bajaji (three-wheeler taxi), madafu (green coconuts), mihogo (cassava crisps), kanga.

**Images (5).** Portraits: Abdalla, Felister (red kanga), Said, Rajab. Location: Mama Ngina Drive at night, carts lit by lamps.

**Audit tags.** Culprit F, 40s, Taita-origin name, motive revenge. Victim M, 30s, Swahili-origin name. *Tone note: Felister is a grieving mother, not a monster. The reconstruction stays restrained, and Abdalla's guilt for the hit-and-run is stated as evidence, not as justification.*

### Case 27 — Staff Quarters

`case-027` · Mombasa · 16 min · suspects 3 · chain 3 · herrings 1 · liars 1 (culprit) · groups WHO, WHY · stamps needed 1 (records) · **spine background detail**

**OB entry.** OB 12/15/09, 00:04. The night security supervisor of Coral Tide Resort, Mtwapa, reports a housekeeper found dead in the staff-quarters laundry.

**Setting.** Fictional **Coral Tide Resort**, a beach hotel in Mtwapa, 25 km north of Mombasa. Guest side: pool, beach, lights. Staff side, behind a wall: the admin block, the staff gate with its clock book, and the staff quarters with a laundry room.

**Victim.** **Riziki Chai**, 29, housekeeper and the staff's elected welfare representative. Struck with an iron (steam press) in the laundry.

**Cast**

| Anthony Gikonyo | 44 | Suspect | Guest from Nairobi who accused Riziki of stealing his watch that morning and shouted at her at reception | Innocent (red herring): at the hotel bar |
| Kache Mwaro | 26 | Suspect | Riziki's roommate; they'd argued about money | Innocent: on kitchen night shift |
| Jumaa Tsuma | 48 | Witness | Staff-quarters gate guard | Innocent |
| Riziki's sister (Neema Chai) | 24 | Witness (by phone) | Received Riziki's last message | Innocent |

**What really happened.** For two years Catherine deducted staff pension contributions from every payslip and didn't remit them, and she ran a ghost employee, "Mwaka Kenga", on payroll whose salary went to her own PesaPap number. Riziki, as welfare rep, requested the staff's official pension statements and found two years of zero contributions. At 22:41 Catherine called her and said they should meet "privately, before you embarrass the hotel". Riziki texted her sister she was going, with the evidence. In the laundry at about 23:00 Catherine tried to take the statements; Riziki refused; Catherine hit her with the steam iron and took the statements. She signed out at the staff gate at 23:22.

WhatsApp to her sister **22:45**: *"Naenda kukutana na HR laundry. Nimeshika ushahidi wa pension."* ("Going to meet HR at the laundry. I've got the pension evidence.") **(Probable cause for a records request on the payroll account and Catherine's number)** |

### Case 28 — Seven Minutes of Taarab

`case-028` · Mombasa · 17 min · suspects 3 · chain 3 · herrings 1 · liars 1 (**covering grandson**) · groups WHO, WHY · stamps needed 0 · **twist: the beloved 74-year-old did it**

**OB entry.** OB 29/20/09, 23:52. The father of a bride reports the manager of the taarab band found dead in the hall's store room during the wedding.

**Setting.** A wedding night in Majengo: a community hall hung with lights, women's side and men's side, the bride on a decorated stage, a **taarab** band of oud, violin, keyboard and drum. Fictional band **Nyota ya Pwani** ("star of the coast"), 52 years old.

**Victim.** **Amina Shee**, 45, the band's manager and booker for 15 years. Struck with a heavy brass tray stand in the store room behind the stage.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mzee Abdulrahman Kibwana | 74 | Suspect | The band's oud player for 52 years; a legend; gentle; everyone's grandfather | **Culprit** |
| Mohamed "DJ Moha" Bwana | 33 | Suspect | Wedding DJ; fought publicly with the band over who'd play the night | Innocent (red herring): in the car park |
| Mwanaisha Fadhili | 56 | Suspect | The band's lead singer; wanted to take over as manager | Innocent: singing the whole set |
| Twaha Kibwana | 22 | Witness | The Mzee's grandson; the band's keyboard player | **The liar (covering)** |
| Bi Zainab Said | 50 | Witness | Mother of the bride | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Amina had signed a deal with DJ Moha for a "modern taarab package": a DJ, playback tracks and two young singers, cheaper than a live band. After this wedding, Nyota ya Pwani would get no more bookings; the Mzee's small share of each wedding fee was his only income. That evening she paid him his last fee and told him kindly that it was finished. During the second set, at 23:12, Twaha started the recorded oud track on his keyboard sampler, as he'd been doing for a year whenever his grandfather's hands tired. The Mzee went to the store room where Amina was counting the night's cash, pleaded once more, and when she said no, struck her. He was back on stage, his oud on his knee, at 23:19. His feather plectrum, broken in two, stayed on the store-room floor.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Store room | Struck with a brass tray stand; the night's cash still in its envelope |
| ev_risha | Physical | Store-room floor, under the stand | A broken **feather plectrum** (risha), the old kind cut from an eagle's quill |
| ev_risha_note | Witness | Mwanaisha | "Only the Mzee uses a feather risha. Everyone else uses plastic. He cuts his own." |
| ev_video | Phone (guest's phone, shared willingly) | Bi Zainab's niece | Video of the second set, timestamped **23:08–23:24**. From **23:12 to 23:19 the oud player's chair is empty** while the oud is still heard; Twaha's left hand is on the keyboard's sampler pads |
| ev_amina_phone | Phone (victim's, unlocked by her son) | Store room | WhatsApp to DJ Moha, 21:50: *"Baada ya leo, wazee wamekwisha. Contract yako inaanza Jumamosi."* ("After today, the old men are finished. Your contract starts Saturday.") PesaPap: **23:05, KSh 6,000 to ABDULRAHMAN KIBWANA**, "last fee, asante" |
| ev_contract | Physical (found paper) | Her bag | Signed agreement with DJ Moha: "Modern taarab package — all bookings from 1 October" |
| ev_dj_live | Phone (DJ Moha's live stream, public) | His social-media page | Live stream from the car park setting up his sound system 23:00–23:30, his face on camera throughout |
| ev_mwanaisha | Physical | `ev_video` | Mwanaisha singing centre stage throughout 23:08–23:24 |
| ev_family | Witness | Bi Zainab | The Kibwanas and the Shees are related by marriage and have played every family wedding for decades; "there's no feud, there's only love" |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Twaha Kibwana | Cooperative | **"Babu was on stage beside me the whole second set. I can see him from my keyboard."** | Yes | `ev_video` | *"Babu's hands get tired. For a year I've played his oud parts from a recording so he can rest. Nobody is supposed to know. He went out for a few minutes. That's all."* |
| Mzee Abdulrahman Kibwana | Cooperative, then silent | "Amina is my daughter's friend. I held her at her naming ceremony." (true) | — | — | Shown `ev_risha`: a long silence; then *"Fifty-two years."* Nothing more |
| Mohamed "DJ Moha" Bwana | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_contract`) | "I was setting up outside. I was live the whole time." | True | — | Shows `ev_dj_live` |

**Proof**
1. Twaha's claim + `ev_video` → the oud player's chair was empty 23:12–23:19 while a recording played; his grandfather left the stage.
2. `ev_amina_phone` + `ev_contract` → that evening Amina paid the Mzee his last fee and was ending the band's bookings.
3. `ev_risha` + `ev_risha_note` → the broken plectrum under the body is the kind only the Mzee uses → **WHO = Mzee Abdulrahman Kibwana**, **WHY = she was ending the band he'd played in for fifty years**.

**Eliminations**
- *WHO:* DJ Moha: `ev_dj_live`. Mwanaisha Fadhili: `ev_mwanaisha`. Twaha Kibwana: `ev_video` (his hands on the keyboard throughout). Bi Zainab Said: on the women's side with the bride, also in the video.
- *WHY:*

| Motive word | Refuted by |
|---|---|
| "she owed him his fee" | `ev_amina_phone` (paid at 23:05) |
| "a feud between the two families" | `ev_family` |
| "she stole the night's takings" | `ev_body` (cash still in its envelope) |
| "rivalry for the manager's job" | That's Mwanaisha's ambition; she's eliminated |
| ✔ "she was ending the band he'd played in for fifty years" | — |

**Red herrings / twist.**
- Red herring: the brash DJ who fought with the band.
- **Twist:** the culprit is the one person no one in the hall, or the player, wants it to be. The guarded suspect (DJ Moha) is the one the game's visual language has been setting up.

Halima, on a correct charge: *"Fifty years of music, and seven minutes. I'll ask the court to remember both."*

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Amina Shee because {why}.` WHO: Mzee Abdulrahman Kibwana, Mohamed Bwana, Mwanaisha Fadhili, Twaha Kibwana, Zainab Said (5). WHY: five words above.

**Credibility path.** 0 stamps.

**New interface beat.** **Video as evidence.** First time a video is scrubbed frame by frame with its timestamp. The audio waveform beside it shows the oud continuing while the chair is empty: picture and sound disagree, and that disagreement is the clue.

**Kenyan texture.** Mombasa taarab and its decades-old bands, weddings in Majengo, oud players and hand-cut feather plectrums, DJs replacing live bands, grandsons covering for grandfathers' tired hands.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** taarab (coastal sung poetry with orchestra), udi (oud), risha (plectrum), harusi (wedding), babu (grandfather), wazee (old men / elders).

**Images (6).** Portraits: Amina, Mzee Kibwana (with his oud), Twaha, DJ Moha. Location: the wedding hall with the band on stage. Evidence photo: the broken feather plectrum.

**Audit tags.** Culprit M, **70s**, Swahili-origin name, motive business rivalry (livelihood). Victim F, 40s, Swahili-origin name. *This case fulfils the "at least one culprit in their 70s" correction from the region 2 audit.*

### Case 29 — The 1503 Coin

`case-029` · Mombasa · 17 min · suspects 4 · chain 3 · herrings 1 · liars 1 (culprit) · groups WHO, WHY · stamps needed 1 (records)

**OB entry.** OB 14/26/09, 17:31. A tour guide is found dead in the courtyard of a ruined house used as a shortcut between Fort Jesus and the Leven Steps.

**Setting.** Old Town around Fort Jesus on a busy Friday: licensed tour guides in badges meeting groups outside the Fort, school trips, the narrow lanes down to the Leven Steps and the water. A fictional ruined coral-stone house with an open courtyard that guides use as a shortcut.

**Victim.** **Nuru Kombo**, 33, licensed guide, secretary of the Old Town guides' association. Struck with a loose coral stone.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bramwel Shikuku | 36 | Suspect | Licensed guide; sells fake "Portuguese coins" and "antique trade beads" to tourists | **Culprit** |
| Athumani Rashid | 48 | Suspect | Rival guide; lost a cruise-ship tour contract to Nuru's group | Innocent (red herring): at the port with cruise passengers |
| Pius Wanyama | 61 | Suspect | Curio dealer who supplies Bramwel's "antiques" | Innocent: at his shop |
| Leah Wawira | 40 | Witness | Teacher leading a school trip from Nakuru | Innocent |
| Swabri Hemed | 55 | Witness | Fort ticket-office clerk | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Nuru reported Bramwel to the guides' association: tourists had complained of buying "1503 Portuguese coins" that turned out to be cast in a mould. A hearing next Saturday would take his badge. On the day, Bramwel was assigned the Nakuru school group at 15:00, then at 15:55 asked Nuru to finish the tour for him, "something urgent". At 16:35 Nuru finished and texted him to meet "and sort this out like adults". They met in the ruined courtyard at about 16:45. He offered money to withdraw the complaint; she laughed. He hit her with a stone and left; one of his coins fell from his pocket. At 16:50, a few lanes away, he sold coins to a tourist for KSh 18,000.

**Evidence**

|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Courtyard | Struck with a coral stone |
| ev_coin | Physical | Courtyard floor | A "Portuguese coin" dated **1503**. Under the comparison view: a **mould seam** around the edge; a genuine struck coin has none |
| ev_register | Physical (found paper) | Fort ticket office | Group #14 (Nakuru school, 38 pupils), 15:00. Guide: **B. Shikuku**. A second entry in another hand at 15:55: "Guide changed: N. Kombo" |
| ev_leah | Witness + phone | Teacher | Bramwel left the group at the bastions at about 15:55 saying a colleague would finish. Nuru took them to 16:35, then said she had to "meet someone to sort something out". Leah's phone photo, **16:20**, shows Nuru with the group and no Bramwel |
| ev_nuru_phone | Phone (victim's, unlocked by her mother) | Her bag | SMS to **"Bramwel"** at **16:36**: *"Tukutane kwa nyumba bovu, tuongee kama watu wazima."* ("Let's meet at the ruined house and talk like adults.") Reply 16:37: "Sawa." **(Probable cause for a records request on Bramwel's number)** |
| ev_letter | Physical (found paper) | Nuru's bag | Guides' association: "Notice of disciplinary hearing — B. Shikuku — sale of counterfeit antiquities to tourists — Saturday 4 October" |
| ev_records | **Records request** (Bramwel's line) | Jamii Mobile + PesaPap | Mast **Leven / Old Town East** 16:05–16:58. PesaPap **16:50: KSh 18,000 received** from a tourist, reference "coins x3". Earlier this year: commission payments to and from Pius Wanyama |
| ev_bag | Physical | Bramwel's shoulder bag (he opens it when asked) | Six more "1503" coins with the same mould seam |
| ev_cruise | Physical (found paper) | Cruise tour manifest | Athumani Rashid leading 40 cruise passengers 14:30–18:00 at the port and Haller Park |
| ev_pius | Physical (found paper) | Pius's sales book | Sales at his shop 16:10, 16:32, 16:55 |
| ev_tips | Witness | Swabri, ticket clerk | Guides split tips through the association, recorded weekly; "nobody fights over tips here, it's all written" |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bramwel Shikuku | Cooperative | **"I guided the Nakuru group from three until five. I never left them."** / "Those coins are souvenirs. I tell people they're copies." | First claim (the second is a self-serving opinion, refuted by `ev_letter`) | `ev_register` or `ev_leah` | *"I had to meet a buyer. Nuru took over. I didn't see her after."* |
| Athumani Rashid | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_letter`) | "I was at the port with a cruise group." | True | — | Topic "contract": "I lost it fairly. She was better." |
| Pius Wanyama | Cooperative | "I sell to guides. What they say to tourists is their business." | True | — | Topic "coins": admits he sells them "as replicas"; shows `ev_pius` |

**Proof**
1. Bramwel's claim + `ev_register` + `ev_leah` → he left the group at 15:55; Nuru finished the tour and left at 16:35 to meet someone.
2. `ev_nuru_phone` + `ev_records` → Nuru arranged to meet Bramwel at the ruined house at 16:36; he agreed, and his phone was in that zone 16:05–16:58.
3. `ev_coin` + `ev_bag` + `ev_letter` → the mould-cast "1503" coin at the scene matches the coins in his bag; Nuru had reported him for exactly those coins → **WHO = Bramwel Shikuku**, **WHY = she'd reported him for selling fake antiques to tourists**.

- *WHY:*

| "a dispute over shared tips" | `ev_tips` |
| "she'd taken over his tour group" | `ev_register` + `ev_leah`: he asked her to |
| "an unpaid commission" | `ev_records` (commissions paid both ways) |
| ✔ "she'd reported him for selling fake antiques to tourists" | — |

**Red herrings / twist.** Red herring: the rival who lost the cruise contract.

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Nuru Kombo because {why}.` WHO: Bramwel Shikuku, Athumani Rashid, Pius Wanyama, Leah Wawira, Swabri Hemed (5). WHY: five words above.

**Credibility path.** 1 stamp.

**New interface beat.** **A fake as evidence.** The comparison view shows a mould seam on the coin: the first time the *falseness* of an object is the clue. Foreshadows region 7's forged documents.

**Kenyan texture.** Licensed guides and their association, school trips from upcountry to Fort Jesus, fake antiquities sold to tourists, the Leven Steps, Swahili text-speak between colleagues.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** nyumba bovu (ruined house), tukutane (let's meet), watu wazima (adults), sawa (okay).

**Images (6).** Portraits: Nuru, Bramwel, Athumani, Pius. Location: the ruined courtyard with Fort Jesus's walls beyond. Evidence photo: the 1503 coin under magnification, mould seam visible.

### Case 30 — BOSS: Printing Paper

`case-030` · Mombasa · **boss** · 22 min · suspects 4 · **chain 4** · herrings 2 · liars 1 (culprit) · groups WHO, WHY, **SPINE** · stamps needed 2 (records ×2) · **twist: the "fall" wasn't one, and the "printing paper" is title-deed paper**

**OB entry.** OB 02/30/09, 08:05. The security office of Bandari Freight Station, Shimanzi, reports a documentation clerk found at the foot of an external staircase; **recorded by the company as an accidental fall at about 06:00**.

**Setting.** Fictional **Bandari Freight Station**, a private container yard in Shimanzi near the port, and fictional **Pwani Clearing & Forwarding**, the clearing agency with offices on its upper floor. Container stacks, reach-stackers, a vehicle gate with a log, an office block with an outside steel staircase.

**Victim.** **Naomi Chepkemoi**, 38, documentation clerk at Pwani Clearing, from Eldoret, eight years at the coast. Head injury at the foot of the stairs. Her phone is missing.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Daniel Gichuru | 51 | Suspect | Operations manager, Pwani Clearing; secretly paid by Mvua Holdings | **Culprit** |
| Samson Odera | 33 | Suspect | Night reach-stacker operator; argued with Naomi over overtime sign-offs | Innocent (red herring 1): moving containers |
| Fatma Ruwa | 44 | Suspect | Rival clerk who wanted Naomi's senior post | Innocent: tallying on a ship at berth |
| Yusuf Mazrui | 58 | Suspect | Owner of Bandari Freight; ruled it "a fall" within an hour and didn't want police on site | Innocent (red herring 2): at home; his haste is about an unrelated tax audit |
| Ramadhan Kalume | 49 | Witness | Night gate guard | Innocent |
| Gladys Chepkemoi | 34 | Witness (by phone) | Naomi's sister in Eldoret | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Container **PCFU 418220-3** arrived declared as "printing paper, A3, 40 cartons", consignee **Mvua Holdings Ltd, Nairobi**. Preparing the customs entry, Naomi opened a carton for the sample check. The paper had a watermark, security fibres and a printed oval marked "Registrar's seal here": blank **title-deed paper**. She photographed a sheet, kept one, and refused to sign the entry as "printing paper". She was working a night shift for a vessel cut-off. At 23:05 Gichuru drove in, told her to sign, and offered her money. She texted her sister at 23:12. At about 23:35, on the outside staircase, he tried to take the sample and her phone; she fell or was pushed; he went down, struck her once more to be sure, took her phone and the sample sheet and drove out at 23:50. Next morning the company's security report, written by his man, said she'd fallen arriving for the 06:00 shift.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Foot of stairs | Head injuries; her ID lanyard and gate card on her |
| ev_security_report | Physical (found paper) | Company security office | "Clerk N. Chepkemoi fell from the external staircase on arrival for the 06:00 shift. Accident." Signed by the shift supervisor, approved by D. Gichuru |
| ev_gatelog | Physical (found paper) | Vehicle and staff gate log | **N. Chepkemoi — in 22:40 (night cut-off shift) — no exit.** **D. Gichuru, car KDB xxx — in 23:05 — out 23:50.** No other vehicle or staff movements 22:45–00:30 except the night operators already inside |
| ev_ramadhan | Witness | Gate guard | Heard a woman cry out from the office block at about 23:35. Gichuru drove out at 23:50 "fast, without greeting me" |
| ev_gladys_phone | Phone (witness's phone) | Naomi's sister | WhatsApp from Naomi **23:12**: *"Gichuru amekuja. Anataka nisaini PCFU kama printing paper. Si printing paper. Ona."* ("Gichuru's come. He wants me to sign PCFU as printing paper. It's not printing paper. Look.") Attached photo: a watermarked sheet with an empty oval box marked **"Registrar's seal here"**. **(Probable cause for records on Naomi's line)** |

| ev_tally_odera | Physical (found paper) | Yard tally sheet | Samson Odera's reach-stacker moves at 23:20, 23:34, 23:41, 23:58, all at the far end of the yard |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Daniel Gichuru | Cooperative | **"I was home in Nyali all night. I heard about Naomi this morning like everyone else."** / "That container is printing paper. I've seen the invoice." | Both (one liar) | Claim 1: `ev_gatelog` or `ev_records_gichuru`. Claim 2: `ev_container` / `ev_gladys_phone` | *"I came to collect a file. I didn't see her."* / *"I don't open cartons. I sign what I'm given."* |
| Samson Odera | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_overtime`) | "I was on the stacker all night." | True | — | Topic "Naomi": "She signed my overtime on Friday. She was fair." |
| Fatma Ruwa | Cooperative | "I was on the ship until three." | True | — | Topic "promotion": "I wanted her job. I didn't want her dead." |
| Yusuf Mazrui | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_security_report`) | "My security said she fell. I believed them." | True (he did) | — | Shown the tax notice: admits he wanted the police gone "for my own reasons, not hers" |

**Proof**
1. `ev_gatelog` + `ev_security_report` → Naomi came in at 22:40 and never left; the report's "06:00 on arrival" is false. The "accident" story is wrong from the start.
2. `ev_gladys_phone` + `ev_manifest` + `ev_container` → Naomi refused to sign PCFU 418220-3 as printing paper because it was title-deed security paper consigned to Mvua Holdings; Gichuru was pressuring her at 23:12.
3. Gichuru's claim + `ev_gatelog` + `ev_ramadhan` → he wasn't home; he drove in at 23:05 and out at 23:50, fifteen minutes after the cry.
4. `ev_records_naomi` + `ev_records_gichuru` → Naomi's phone left Shimanzi at 23:52 and went to Nyali, exactly as Gichuru's did; and Mvua Holdings has paid Gichuru every month for 14 months → **WHO = Daniel Gichuru**, **WHY = she refused to pass Mvua's title-deed paper as printing paper**.

**Spine proof (Pattern File).** The sheet in `ev_container` has an empty oval: *"Registrar's seal here"*. In the comparison view, the **proof impression of the REGISTRAR OF TITLES seal from case 10** fits the oval exactly. The seal Rashid refused to finish was made for this paper.

**Eliminations**
- *WHO:* Samson Odera: `ev_tally_odera`. Fatma Ruwa: `ev_ship_tally`. Yusuf Mazrui: `ev_mazrui`. Ramadhan Kalume: at the gate (log entries in his hand every 15 minutes).
- *WHY:*

| Motive word | Refuted by |
|---|---|
| "an overtime dispute" | `ev_overtime` (settled; and that was Odera) |
| "she wanted his job" | That's Fatma's ambition, and it was Gichuru's job neither wanted |
| "she'd found the owner's tax problem" | `ev_mazrui` (the audit concerns tax rates, not Naomi or Gichuru) |
| "a debt between them" | `ev_records_gichuru` (no transactions between them) |
| ✔ "she refused to pass Mvua's title-deed paper as printing paper" | — |

**Red herrings / twist.**
- Red herrings: the operator with the overtime grudge, and the owner who rushed to call it an accident.
- **Twist:** the case arrives closed as an accident (echoing case 24), and the "printing paper" is the raw material of the whole forgery operation.

**Charge sheet.** Three groups:

> **WHO / WHY:** `{who} killed Naomi Chepkemoi because {why}.`
> **SPINE:** `The empty seal box on this paper was made for the seal ordered from {pin}.`

- WHO: Daniel Gichuru, Samson Odera, Fatma Ruwa, Yusuf Mazrui, Ramadhan Kalume (5).
- WHY: five words above.
- SPINE (Pattern File pins): *the REGISTRAR OF TITLES seal proof, Omar Printers (case 10)* ✔, *the Mvua calendar, Signal Point (case 6)*, *the Mvua business card, Barwaqo Mall (case 13)*, *the Upendo receipts (case 20)*, *the beachfront plots flyer, Coral Tide (case 27)* (5).
- Halima. All three: *"Paper from the sea, a seal from River Road, buyers in Komarock and Kitengela. This isn't a gang, Amani. It's a factory."*

**After the verdict.**
- Gichuru, in interview: he was recruited by "a man with a bad leg they call Fundi", who brings the cash and never uses a phone. He's never heard the name Kivuli. He asks for a lawyer.
- `ev_gichuru_file` pins three things to the Pattern File: the container movement (`t_mvua`), the refused Lamu dhow run (connects quietly to case 24's Upepo Mwema; the card makes clear Ireri had nothing to do with Mvua, and Khamis refused Mvua separately), and **"Bahati — old matter — closed 12 yrs"** (`t_joseph`). Joseph Mwenda died outside Nakuru twelve years ago. Amani's desk lamp dims for a beat on the pin. Nothing else is said.
- The container is seized. Its paper goes to the evidence store in Nairobi.
- **Collectible:** a brass dhow compass, sent by Abdalla Khamis from Lamu with a note: *"Baba refused them too. Thank you for reading him right."* It sits on the desk from now on.

**New interface beat.** **Fitting one case's evidence into another's.** The comparison view takes a Pattern File pin (case 10's seal proof) and lays it over this case's paper. The click when the oval fits is the region's payoff moment.

**Kenyan texture.** Container freight stations in Shimanzi, clearing agents and customs entries, night cut-offs for vessels, security paper and watermarks, company "accident" reports, a clerk from Eldoret who wouldn't sign.

**Spine.** Threads `t_mvua`, `t_stamp`, `t_fundi`, `t_joseph`. The spine group needs case 10.

**Glossary.** bandari (port), makontena (containers), karatasi (paper), saini (sign), muhuri (seal).

**Images (9).** Portraits: Naomi, Gichuru, Odera, Fatma, Mazrui. Locations: Bandari Freight Station at night with the outside staircase; the opened container. Evidence photos: a watermarked sheet with the empty seal oval; the brass compass with Abdalla's note.

**Audit tags.** Culprit M, 50s, Kikuyu-origin name, motive commissioned (spine). Victim F, 30s, Kalenjin-origin name.

## Open questions for the cultural reader (region 3)

1. **Swahili time (case 23):** confirm "saa tisa na nusu" for 15:30 is how a Mombasa woman would text it, and that players unfamiliar with Swahili time will be fine with the glossary.
2. **Taarab (case 28):** are feather (quill) plectrums still used by older oud players in Mombasa? Is a keyboard sampler covering an elderly player plausible? Does a 74-year-old beloved musician as culprit risk offending the taarab community?
3. **Jumaa on Biashara Street (case 21):** do shopkeepers pull shutters half down for Friday prayers, and would a widowed shop owner stay inside doing accounts?
4. **Arabic-script Swahili (case 24):** would a Lamu family plausibly write "HAPANA" in Ajami script; is it respectful to show?
5. **Bajuni, Digo, Duruma, Giriama names:** check every name's origin tag and that none is a stereotype.
6. **Coast hotels (case 27):** is the staff-gate clock book used by managers too? Is the pension-deduction scam depicted accurately without implying the real fund is at fault?
7. **Kenyan-Asian family (case 23):** is the Karimjee family's depiction (spice trade, Old Town building, family trust) respectful and plausible?
8. **Likoni ferry timing (case 22):** crossing times and frequency at dawn.
9. **Mama Ngina Drive (case 26):** current state of the promenade and vendors (it was redeveloped; check what's there now).
10. Sheng and Swahili in all ten cases, particularly chat messages.

## Part E — Region 4: Rift Valley / Nakuru (cases 31–40)

**Region frame.** October and November, the short rains arriving over the Rift. Amani is posted to Nakuru for the region: Menengai crater, the flower farms of Naivasha, the flooded shore of Lake Nakuru, ranches near Elementaita, Njoro, the cold potato country around Molo, Ol Kalou's dairies, Eldama Ravine's sawmills, and Bahati. Land is everywhere in this region: who owns it, who surveyed it, who moved the beacon. Two new recurring characters arrive: **Dr. Ruth Chebii**, county pathologist, precise and dry, and **Eric Ndung'u**, analyst at the fictional Rift Valley Regional Forensic Lab, who answers the phone eating. Mwalimu's voice-notes get shorter as the region goes on. After case 30's "Bahati — old matter" pin, she knows where this is heading.

### E1. Region 4 rules

- **Forensics arrive (case 31).**
  - **Autopsy report**, from Dr. Chebii, in clinical report language only: cause of death, injuries and their likely sequence, a **time-of-death range** (rigor, body temperature, stomach contents), and notable marks. No images of bodies, ever; diagrams use a neutral outline figure.
  - **Lab tests** sent to Eric's lab: toxicology, fibre and hair comparison, fingerprints, soil, paint and glass, water chemistry, tool marks. Each has a lab time in **in-game hours** (prints 6 h, soil 8 h, fibres 12 h, toxicology 18 h, water chemistry 10 h).
- **Forensic rush (case 31).** 1 stamp: one test's result arrives in 1 h. Always optional: validator rule 17 (below) guarantees every case can be solved without it.
- **The in-game clock (case 31).** Each case now has a clock. Actions cost time: interview 2 h, visit a location 1–2 h, search 3 h, records request 4 h, lab submission 1 h.
- **The arrest clock (case 31).** Detaining a suspect starts a **24-hour** countdown (Article 49 of Kenya's constitution: a detained person must be brought before a court within 24 hours). While detained, the suspect can be **sampled without consent** (fingerprints, clothing, shoes, a mouth swab), and can be **re-interviewed with lab results**. When the clock runs out they're released: samples already taken stay in the lab, but the player can't press them again in this case. One detention at a time. Detaining the wrong person costs time, not the case.
- **The HOW group arrives (case 31).** Charge sheets read `{who} killed X by {how}, because {why}`. HOW is its own group with **at least 5 method options**, each wrong method refuted by evidence, usually forensic.
- **Liars: 1–2 per case.** Two liars in five cases (32, 34, 35, 36, 40).
- **Red herrings: 1 per case.**
- **Twists: 4** (cases 33, 34, 37, 40).

**Two new validator rules (added to the design doc §3.5):**
- **16. Clock solvability (error).** There is at least one order of actions in which every detention-gated sample is taken and every press that needs a lab result happens inside the 24-hour detention, **without** forensic rush.
- **17. Rush is optional (error).** The minimal proof never requires a forensic rush. The rush only buys convenience and protects stars for players who detain early.

### Case 31 — The Rim

`case-031` · Rift Valley · 18 min · suspects 3 · chain 3 · herrings 1 · liars 1 (culprit) · groups WHO, WHY, HOW · stamps needed 0

**OB entry.** OB 07/03/10, 18:40. Visitors report a woman found on a ledge below the viewpoint on the rim of Menengai crater.

**Setting.** Menengai crater, north of Nakuru town: a huge caldera, geothermal steam plumes rising from well pads on its floor, a viewpoint on the rim with a low stone wall, a gate with a visitors' book. Fictional **Rift Steam Energy** is laying a steam pipeline across farms on the crater's edge; landowners on the route get compensation for crops and trees.

**Victim.** **Beryl Adoyo**, 33, valuation surveyor assessing crops for pipeline compensation. Found 40 m below the viewpoint at 18:10.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kimaiyo Rotich | 62 | Suspect | Landowner on the pipeline route | **Culprit** |
| Duncan Kibe | 36 | Suspect | Beryl's colleague; sent her an angry email that morning about the project timeline | Innocent (red herring): on a drilling pad |
| Philemon Kiptoo | 40 | Suspect | Kimaiyo's farm manager | Innocent: with farm workers |
| Sammy Rono | 29 | Witness | Viewpoint gate attendant | Innocent |
| Ivy Njenga | 31 | Witness | Visitor from Nairobi who found her | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Two weeks before the compensation cut-off date, Kimaiyo planted 900 avocado seedlings and a row of eucalyptus on the strip the pipeline would cross, to claim they were mature crops. Beryl's valuation showed fresh planting rings and cut his claim from KSh 4.2 million to 0.6 million. He wrote her a letter: "You will regret this." On the day she drove up to the crater rim at 16:00 to photograph his strip from above, where the fresh rings show clearly. He saw her car pass his gate and followed. At about 16:30 at the viewpoint he grabbed her by both arms and pushed her over the wall. He drove away at 16:48.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_scene | Physical | Viewpoint | The stone wall is waist-high; her clipboard on the path |
| ev_camera | Physical | Strap still around her neck | Last photos 16:18–16:24: Kimaiyo's strip seen from above, rows of fresh planting rings. Last frame **16:24**: a small figure in a **green sweater** coming up the path behind her |
| ev_gatebook | Physical (found paper) | Gate | **"KCA 7xxX — K. Rotich — in 16:12, out 16:48."** Beryl's company car in 15:58 |
| ev_valuation | Physical (found paper) | Her car | Valuation: seedlings planted about 14 days before the cut-off; compensation cut from KSh 4.2 m to KSh 0.6 m |
| ev_letter | Physical (found paper) | Her car | Kimaiyo's handwritten letter: *"You will regret this."* |
| ev_route | Physical (found paper) | Her car | Wayleave agreement for the pipeline route, signed by Kimaiyo two years ago |
| ev_canteen | Physical (found paper) | Her pocket | Rift Steam canteen receipt, lunch at 12:45 |
| ev_sammy | Witness | Gate attendant | Saw an older man in a green sweater walk up towards the viewpoint at about 16:20, and the same man walk fast back to his car at about 16:45 |
| ev_ivy | Witness | Visitor | Arrived about 18:00, saw a clipboard on the path, looked over the wall, called the gate |
| ev_sweater | Physical, **detention** | Kimaiyo's own sweater (he refuses to hand it over voluntarily) | A hand-knitted green wool sweater |
| ev_shift | Physical (found paper) | Drilling-pad shift log | Duncan Kibe on the well pad on the crater floor 14:00–18:00, signing every hour |
| ev_workers | Witness | Two farm workers (statement only) | Philemon was supervising the evening milking with them 16:00–18:30 |
| ev_email | Physical (found paper) | Her phone | Duncan's email: angry about delays, nothing personal |

**Forensics**

| Test | Sample | Lab hours | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Autopsy (Dr. Chebii) | Body | Immediate | Injuries consistent with a fall from height. **Fingertip bruises on both upper arms, inflicted shortly before death**, as if gripped hard from the front. No blow to the head before the fall. Time of death **15:30–17:30**; stomach contents about three to four hours after a meal (`ev_canteen`, 12:45) narrow it to **about 16:00–17:00** |
| Fibre comparison | Fibres under her fingernails vs `ev_sweater` | 12 h | Green hand-spun wool under her nails **matches** Kimaiyo's sweater |
| Toxicology | Blood | 18 h | Clean |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kimaiyo Rotich | Cooperative, then refuses samples | **"I haven't been up to the crater in years. I was on my farm all afternoon."** / "That girl cheated me." | First claim | `ev_gatebook` or `ev_sammy` | *"I went up to talk to her. Only talk. I asked her to look again. She laughed. I came down. She was standing there when I left."* |
| Duncan Kibe | Cooperative | "I was on the pad all afternoon. The email was about drilling delays." | True | — | Topic "Beryl": "She was the only honest valuer we had." |
| Philemon Kiptoo | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_valuation`) | "I was milking with the workers." | True | — | Topic "seedlings": "Mzee told us to plant them at night. I said it was wrong." |

**Proof**
1. `ev_gatebook` + `ev_sammy` + Kimaiyo's broken claim → he drove up at 16:12, walked to the viewpoint at about 16:20 and left at 16:48; he admits confronting her.
2. Autopsy + `ev_camera` → she died about 16:00–17:00, gripped hard by both arms just before the fall; the last photo shows a man in a green sweater approaching at 16:24.
3. Fibre comparison (needs the detention to seize `ev_sweater`) → wool from his sweater is under her fingernails → **WHO = Kimaiyo Rotich**, **HOW = pushed from the crater rim**, **WHY = her valuation exposed the crops he'd planted just before the deadline**.

**Eliminations**
- *WHO:* Duncan Kibe: `ev_shift`. Philemon Kiptoo: `ev_workers`. Sammy Rono: at the gate (visitors' book entries in his hand throughout). Ivy Njenga: arrived at 18:00 (gate book).
- *HOW:*

| Method word | Refuted by |
|---|---|
| "struck on the head and thrown over" | Autopsy: no blow before the fall |
| "fell while taking photographs" | Autopsy grip bruises; the camera's last frame shows someone approaching |
| "hit by a reversing car" | Autopsy: no vehicle injuries; her car is parked 200 m away |
| "poisoned" | Toxicology clean |
| ✔ "pushed from the crater rim" | — |

- *WHY:*

| Motive word | Refuted by |
|---|---|
| "a dispute over the pipeline route through his farm" | `ev_route` (he signed the route two years ago) |
| "her colleague's anger about delays" | That's Duncan's email; Duncan is eliminated |
| "an old family feud" | No relation or past between them (Philemon, Duncan) |
| "a debt" | No money between them in any record |
| ✔ "her valuation exposed the crops he'd planted just before the deadline" | — |

**Red herrings / twist.** Red herring: Duncan's angry email. No twist.

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Beryl Adoyo by {how}, because {why}.` WHO: Kimaiyo Rotich, Duncan Kibe, Philemon Kiptoo, Sammy Rono, Ivy Njenga (5). HOW and WHY: five words each, above.

**Clock plan.** Interview Kimaiyo (2 h), read the gate book (1 h), interview Sammy (2 h): claim broken. **Detain Kimaiyo** (clock starts), seize the sweater, submit fibres (1 h). Visit the farm and Philemon (3 h), pull the shift log (1 h); the fibre result lands at hour 12 of the detention. Re-interview Kimaiyo with it. 13 h of the 24 used. Without the rush.

**Credibility path.** 0 stamps (a rush on fibres is optional, 1 stamp).

**New interface beat.** **The autopsy report, the lab queue and the arrest clock**, all at once. **Spine.** None.

### Case 32 — Greenhouse 7

`case-032` · Rift Valley · 18 min · suspects 3 · chain 3 · herrings 1 · liars 1 (**innocent**) · groups WHO, WHY, HOW · stamps needed 0

**OB entry.** OB 22/09/10, 13:20. A flower farm on the south shore of Lake Naivasha reports its new farm manager collapsed and died in greenhouse 7.

**Setting.** Fictional **Lakeview Roses**, an export rose farm on Lake Naivasha: rows of polythene greenhouses, a packhouse with a cold room and a tea urn, a locked chemical store whose key the sprayer keeps on his belt, a farm rule painted on the store door: *"Chemicals handled by trained sprayers only."*

**Victim.** **Caroline Jerop**, 41, appointed farm manager two weeks ago. Collapsed at 12:10 in greenhouse 7 after drinking tea from her green thermos; died before the ambulance arrived.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wambui Nderitu | 46 | Suspect | Packhouse manager for 20 years; expected the farm-manager post | **Culprit** |
| Samuel Kariithi | 55 | Suspect | The previous farm manager, demoted; bitter in public | Innocent (red herring): at a labour hearing |
| Hesbon Shitandi | 29 | Suspect | Sprayer; holds the chemical-store key | Innocent; **the liar** |
| Tabitha Wangui | 58 | Witness | Packhouse tea lady | Innocent |

**What really happened.** At 07:30 Hesbon left the chemical store unlocked while he went for breakfast. Wambui slipped in and poured about 80 ml from a bottle of an organophosphate insecticide into a small water bottle. At the 10:00 tea break she offered to fill the new manager's thermos herself "as a welcome", and added the poison at 10:15. Caroline drank in greenhouse 7 at about 11:30.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_thermos | Physical | Greenhouse 7 | Caroline's green thermos, half full of tea |
| ev_storeregister | Physical (found paper) | Chemical store | Stock card for "Rosetox 500 ml" (fictional brand, an organophosphate), **bottle #14**: opened last month; **420 ml** remaining at today's 13:00 count |
| ev_spraylog | Physical (found paper) | Sprayer's log | No Rosetox spraying recorded since the bottle was opened at 500 ml. **80 ml is unaccounted for** |
| ev_patrol | Physical (found paper) | Farm guard's patrol log | **"07:30 — chemical store door open, nobody present."** |
| ev_canteen | Physical (found paper) | Canteen | Hesbon's breakfast receipt, 07:22 |
| ev_tabitha | Witness | Tea lady | At 10:15 Wambui came to the urn and said, "Let me fill the new madam's flask myself, as a welcome." She'd never done that for anyone in 20 years |
| ev_doorrule | Physical | Store door | "Chemicals handled by trained sprayers only." Packhouse staff are never trained or allowed |
| ev_prints_bottle | Physical | Bottle #14 | Two sets of fingerprints |
| ev_hearing | Physical (found paper) | Naivasha labour office | Hearing minutes: Samuel Kariithi present 09:00–13:00 |
| ev_promotion | Physical (found paper) | Notice board | "Congratulations to Caroline Jerop, Farm Manager." Below it, someone has scrawled "20 YEARS" |
| ev_fumigation | Physical (found paper) | Fumigation log | Greenhouse 7 last fumigated eight days ago |
| ev_stock | Physical (found paper) | Packhouse | Export stock reconciles to the stem for the month |

**Forensics**

| Test | Sample | Lab hours | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Autopsy | Body | Immediate | No injuries. Signs consistent with **organophosphate poisoning** (pinpoint pupils, fluid on the lungs). Time of ingestion about 30–60 minutes before collapse |
| Toxicology | Stomach contents and thermos | 18 h | **Organophosphate present in both**, same compound as Rosetox |
| Fingerprints | Bottle #14 vs Hesbon (consents) and Wambui (**refuses → detention**) | 6 h | One set is Hesbon's (expected). The other **matches Wambui Nderitu** |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hesbon Shitandi | Cooperative | **"The store was locked all day. The key never left my belt."** | Yes | `ev_patrol` + `ev_canteen` | *"I left it open when I went for breakfast. Twenty minutes. If the farm finds out, I'm finished."* (new fact: the store was open 07:20–07:45) |
| Wambui Nderitu | Cooperative, then refuses prints | "I've never been inside the chemical store." / "I was happy for her." | First claim | Fingerprint result | *"I went in for gloves. Only gloves."* (the gloves are kept in the packhouse) |
| Samuel Kariithi | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_promotion`) | "I was at the labour office all morning." | True | — | Topic "Wambui": "She trained Caroline. Then Caroline got the job." |

**Proof**
1. `ev_storeregister` + `ev_spraylog` + Hesbon's broken claim → 80 ml of organophosphate is missing from bottle #14, and the store stood open and unattended at breakfast.
2. Autopsy + toxicology + `ev_tabitha` → the poison was in Caroline's thermos, filled at 10:15 by Wambui, who had never filled anyone's flask before.
3. Fingerprints (needs the detention) + `ev_doorrule` → Wambui's prints are on the bottle, though packhouse staff never handle chemicals → **WHO = Wambui Nderitu**, **HOW = organophosphate insecticide in her tea flask**, **WHY = Caroline got the farm-manager post Wambui had waited 20 years for**.

**Eliminations**
- *WHO:* Samuel Kariithi: `ev_hearing`. Hesbon Shitandi: at breakfast during the theft (`ev_canteen`), and his lie only hid a careless habit. Tabitha Wangui: she filled every flask for 20 years; her prints aren't on the bottle.
- *HOW:*

| Method word | Refuted by |
|---|---|
| "heatstroke in the greenhouse" | Toxicology |
| "fumigation gas in the greenhouse" | `ev_fumigation` |
| "a blow to the head" | Autopsy: no injuries |
| "an allergic reaction to a sting" | Autopsy: no sting or allergic signs |
| ✔ "organophosphate insecticide in her tea flask" | — |

- *WHY:*

| Motive word | Refuted by |
|---|---|
| "she'd caught her stealing export roses" | `ev_stock` |
| "the sprayer's careless habits" | That's Hesbon's problem, not a motive for Wambui |
| "the demoted manager's grudge" | That's Samuel's; Samuel is eliminated |
| "an unpaid loan between them" | No record of any loan (Tabitha: "they didn't even eat together") |
| ✔ "Caroline got the farm-manager post Wambui had waited 20 years for" | — |

**Red herrings / twist.** Red herrings: the bitter demoted manager, and the sprayer's lie about the store. No twist.

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Caroline Jerop by {how}, because {why}.` WHO: Wambui Nderitu, Samuel Kariithi, Hesbon Shitandi, Tabitha Wangui, and the guard who wrote `ev_patrol`, Daudi Lekalau (5).

**Clock plan.** Read the store register and spray log (1 h), interview Hesbon and break his claim (2 h), interview Tabitha (2 h). **Detain Wambui**, take prints, submit with the bottle (1 h). Pull the hearing minutes (1 h), visit Samuel (2 h). Prints back at hour 6. Re-interview Wambui. Toxicology (18 h) confirms the HOW but isn't needed to charge, because the autopsy already supports organophosphate; it arrives while the case continues and only adds a line to the verdict.

**Credibility path.** 0 stamps.

**New interface beat.** **Counting as evidence.** The stock card does arithmetic in the notebook: 500 − 0 sprayed = 500 expected; 420 found; 80 missing. Simple maths becomes a deduction the player can see.

**Kenyan texture.** Lake Naivasha's export flower industry, packhouse tea urns, chemical stores and spraying logs, 20 years of loyal service passed over for a newcomer.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** chai, madam (how farm staff address a woman manager), dawa (here: farm chemical).

**Images (5).** Portraits: Caroline, Wambui, Samuel, Hesbon. Location: greenhouse rows on the shore of Lake Naivasha.

**Audit tags.** Culprit F, 40s, Kikuyu-origin name, motive revenge (passed over). Victim F, 40s, Kalenjin-origin name.

### Case 33 — Brine

`case-033` · Rift Valley · 20 min · suspects 3 · **chain 4** · herrings 1 · liars 1 (culprit) · groups WHO, WHY, HOW · stamps needed 2 (records, warrant) · **twist: he drowned somewhere else** · **spine background detail**

**OB entry.** OB 31/15/10, 07:15. Fishermen report a man found floating among drowned fence posts at the flooded estate on Lake Nakuru's shore. **Recorded as drowning; suspected fall from a boat.**

**Setting.** The southern shore of Lake Nakuru, where years of rising water have swallowed roads, homes and a school. Fictional **Ziwani Gardens**, an estate of plots now half underwater: fence posts and gate pillars standing in green, alkaline water. Lake Nakuru's water is soda-alkaline and thick with blue-green algae (the flamingos' food).

**Victim.** **Hezekiah Onsongo**, 57, land broker who sold the Ziwani Gardens plots, and kept selling them as the water rose, promising "it will go back down".

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kyalo Mwanzia | 34 | Suspect | Mechanic in Lanet; paid KSh 900,000 (his savings plus a chama loan) for plot 47, now under a metre of water | **Culprit** |
| Nicodemus Kipkemboi | 47 | Suspect | Another buyer who protested loudly at Hezekiah's office last week | Innocent (red herring): at a church overnight prayer |
| Rael Nyaboke | 52 | Suspect | Hezekiah's widow; inherits his business | Innocent: at her sister's in Nakuru town |
| Barack Okeyo | 44 | Witness | Fisherman who found him | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Hezekiah agreed to meet Kyalo at Kyalo's garage in Lanet at 20:30 "to discuss a refund". He came to say there would be none. They fought in the yard; Kyalo forced his head into the open 5,000-litre water tank beside the garage, which holds clean, chlorinated county water. Hezekiah's watch strap snapped in the tank. At 23:00 Kyalo loaded the body into a customer's pickup that was in for repairs, drove to Ziwani Gardens and pushed it into the lake, then returned the pickup at 00:30.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Lake | No head injury; his left wrist bare, a pale band where a watch was |
| ev_rael | Witness | Widow | "He went to Lanet last night to tell a buyer there'd be no refund. He said the man was a mechanic." **(Probable cause for records on Hezekiah's line)** |
| ev_records_hez | **Records request** (victim's line) | Jamii Mobile | Call to and from **KYALO MWANZIA** 19:40. Mast **Lanet** 20:25–23:05; mast **Nakuru South (lake shore)** 23:20; then off |
| ev_plot47 | Physical (found paper) | Hezekiah's office | Sale agreement, plot 47, Ziwani Gardens, buyer **Kyalo Mwanzia**, KSh 900,000. A note from Kyalo pinned to it: "Refund or I'll see you in court." |
| ev_jobcard | Physical (found paper) | Kyalo's garage | Job card for a customer's pickup in for brake repair: **odometer in 48,210 km**, written at 08:00 yesterday. Odometer reading when the police see it this morning: **48,248 km**, though the job card says "brakes not yet road-tested" |
| ev_customer | Witness | Pickup owner (statement only) | Hasn't driven it since leaving it Monday |
| ev_lake_distance | Physical | Map | Garage in Lanet to Ziwani Gardens and back: about 38 km |
| ev_tank | Physical, **warrant** | Kyalo's yard (probable cause: `ev_records_hez` + `ev_plot47`) | 5,000-litre plastic water tank, clean county water. At the bottom: **a man's wristwatch with a snapped strap**, engraved "H.O. — 25 years" |
| ev_church | Witness | Pastor (statement only) | Nicodemus led the singing at an all-night prayer 20:00–05:00 |
| ev_sister | Witness | Rael's sister (statement only) | Rael stayed with her in Nakuru town from 19:00; they watched the news and slept |
| ev_chamabook | Physical (found paper) | Kyalo's chama | His loan from the chama is current; no debt to Hezekiah |
| ev_briefcase | Physical | Hezekiah's car at his office | Title deeds for Ziwani plots, each bearing a **REGISTRAR OF TITLES** oval seal in the familiar design, on watermarked paper; sale agreements printed "Title processing: Mvua Holdings" (spine; not needed) |

**Forensics**

| Test | Sample | Lab hours | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Autopsy | Body | Immediate | **Drowning** confirmed (water in lungs and airways). No head injury. Bruising on the back of the neck, as if held. Time of death **20:30–22:30** |
| Water chemistry | Lung fluid vs lake water vs `ev_tank` | 10 h | The lung fluid is **fresh, slightly chlorinated, with no algae**. Lake Nakuru water is **strongly alkaline and full of blue-green algae**. The lung fluid **matches the tank water** |
| Toxicology | Blood | 18 h | Clean |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kyalo Mwanzia | Cooperative | **"I haven't seen him since August. He won't even take my calls."** / "I was working late on a pickup's brakes." | Both | Claim 1: `ev_records_hez` (they spoke at 19:40; Hezekiah's phone was in Lanet 20:25–23:05). Claim 2: `ev_jobcard` (38 km driven on brakes "not yet tested") | *"He came here. He told me my money was in the lake with my plot. He laughed. Then he left."* / *"I took the pickup to test the brakes."* |
| Nicodemus Kipkemboi | Cooperative | "I was at church all night." | True | — | Topic "Hezekiah": "He sold me water too. I prayed for him. I didn't kill him." |
| Rael Nyaboke | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_body`) | "I was at my sister's." | True | — | Shows the business books: "He kept selling. I begged him to stop." |

**Proof**
1. Autopsy + water chemistry → Hezekiah drowned, but **not in the lake**: the water in his lungs is clean, chlorinated tank water with no algae. He was drowned elsewhere and dumped. **(Twist.)**
2. `ev_rael` + `ev_records_hez` + Kyalo's broken claim → Hezekiah went to Kyalo's garage in Lanet and his phone stayed there until 23:05, then moved to the lake shore by 23:20.
3. `ev_jobcard` + `ev_customer` + `ev_lake_distance` → the customer's pickup was driven 38 km that night: Lanet to Ziwani Gardens and back.
4. `ev_tank` (warrant) + water chemistry → the tank water matches the lungs, and Hezekiah's watch is at the bottom of the tank → **WHO = Kyalo Mwanzia**, **HOW = drowned in a water tank, then dumped in the lake**, **WHY = he'd sold him a plot that was under the lake and refused a refund**.

**Eliminations**
- *WHO:* Nicodemus Kipkemboi: `ev_church`. Rael Nyaboke: `ev_sister`. Barack Okeyo: fishing from 04:00 with two others.
- *HOW:*

| Method word | Refuted by |
|---|---|
| "drowned after falling from a boat" | Water chemistry: no lake water in the lungs |
| "struck and thrown into the lake" | Autopsy: no head injury; drowning confirmed |
| "a heart attack while wading" | Autopsy: drowning, held by the neck |
| "poisoned" | Toxicology clean |
| ✔ "drowned in a water tank, then dumped in the lake" | — |

- *WHY:*

| Motive word | Refuted by |
|---|---|
| "to inherit the business" | That's Rael's position; Rael is eliminated |
| "another buyer's refund" | That's Nicodemus's; eliminated |
| "a chama debt" | `ev_chamabook` |
| "a garage bill Hezekiah wouldn't pay" | Hezekiah was never a garage customer (job book) |
| ✔ "he'd sold him a plot under the lake and refused a refund" | — |

**Red herrings / twist.**
- Red herring: Nicodemus's loud protest.
- **Twist:** the lake killed nobody. Dr. Chebii's line on the water result: *"Your man drowned in drinking water, Detective. Somebody has a very clean tank."*

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Hezekiah Onsongo by {how}, because {why}.` WHO: Kyalo Mwanzia, Nicodemus Kipkemboi, Rael Nyaboke, Barack Okeyo, and the pickup's owner, Lawrence Gatimu (5).

**Clock plan.** No detention required. Autopsy (0 h) → water chemistry submitted with lake and lung samples (1 h) → Rael (2 h) → records on Hezekiah's line (4 h) → Kyalo's office agreement (1 h) → garage and job card (2 h) → warrant on the yard (3 h): the tank sample goes to the lab. The lung-vs-lake comparison is back at hour 10; the tank comparison 10 h after it's submitted. A player who detains Kyalo after the warrant still has 24 h for the final press.

**Credibility path.** 2 stamps: records on the victim's line, warrant on Kyalo's yard.

**New interface beat.** **Comparing three samples at once** (lung fluid, lake, tank) in the lab view: three test tubes, three readings, one mismatch, one match.

**Kenyan texture.** The rising Rift Valley lakes that have drowned homes and schools, brokers still selling flooded plots, plastic 5,000-litre water tanks in every compound, mechanics' job cards with odometer readings.

**Spine.** `ev_briefcase` carries `t_stamp` and `t_mvua`: the same seal design and Mvua "title processing" on the Ziwani deeds. Pinned on solve. Mwalimu, after: *"Every flooded plot in this country seems to have the same seal on it."*

**Glossary.** mafuriko (floods), tangi (tank), ploti, maji ya kunywa (drinking water).

**Images (5).** Portraits: Hezekiah, Kyalo, Nicodemus, Rael. Location: Ziwani Gardens half underwater, fence posts in green water, flamingos far off.

**Audit tags.** Culprit M, 30s, Kamba-origin name, motive land (fraud). Victim M, 50s, Kisii-origin name.
