### Case 34 — The Fence Line

`case-034` · Rift Valley · 22 min · suspects 4 · **chain 4** · herrings 1 · liars **2** · groups WHO, WHY, HOW · stamps needed 2 (records, warrant) · **twist: a staged riding accident, and the herders everyone blamed are innocent**

**OB entry.** OB 18/21/10, 09:05. The security head of Olkeri Ranch, near Lake Elementaita, reports the owner found dead beside the boundary fence; his horse grazing nearby. The ranch foreman reports herders cutting the fence at dawn. A local radio station is already blaming "herders".

**Setting.** Fictional **Olkeri Ranch**, 9,000 acres of acacia and grass beside Lake Elementaita: zebra, cattle, horses, a tack room with a farrier's kit, a long wire boundary fence. A drought has pushed pastoralist herds to the area looking for water. Tension in the area is real; the case is built so that the player, not the radio, decides.

**Victim.** **Robert Hollis**, 64, owner; third-generation Kenyan, born on the ranch. Rides the fence line alone every morning at 06:00.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Andrew Kerr | 43 | Suspect | Robert's son-in-law; wants to sell the ranch to a property developer | **Culprit** |
| Gerald Muriithi | 50 | Suspect | Ranch foreman; reported seeing herders cut the fence | Innocent of the killing; **liar 2** (paid to cut the fence and blame herders) |
| Kasaine ole Sopia | 38 | Suspect | Leader of the herding families camped near the ranch | Innocent: at the water point |
| Clare Kerr | 40 | Suspect | Robert's daughter, Andrew's wife; would inherit under the old will | Innocent: in Nairobi |
| Sankau Kipury | 45 | Witness | Ranch head of security, Maasai, 20 years on Olkeri | Innocent |
| Nelson Lekuta | 24 | Witness | Groom | Innocent |
| Bernard Oduor | 52 | Witness (statement only) | Night porter at a Nakuru hotel | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Robert had refused every offer for the ranch and was signing a new will on Monday leaving it to a conservation trust. Andrew paid Gerald KSh 20,000 at 05:10 to cut the boundary fence and say herders did it. Andrew left his Nakuru hotel at 04:50 and drove to the fence line. At 06:00 Robert rode out (the groom saw him go). At about 06:20 Robert stopped at the cut. Andrew, waiting, struck him twice with the farrier's hammer from the tack room, laid him by a rock as if thrown, and drove off. Gerald, at 07:00, told everyone he'd seen herders with wire cutters.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |

| ev_cutters | Physical | Ranch workshop | Bolt cutters, fresh wire marks on the jaws |
| ev_toolboard | Physical | Tack room | The farrier's kit board, each tool painted in outline: **the hammer outline is empty** |
| ev_lekuta | Witness | Groom | Saddled Robert's horse at 05:50; Robert rode out alone at 06:00; the farrier's hammer was on the board at 05:30 when he swept the tack room |
| ev_tracks | Physical | Fence track | Fresh tyre tracks of a vehicle with an aggressive all-terrain tread, coming from the public road and leaving the same way; no ranch vehicle uses that track |
| ev_waterpoint | Physical (found paper) + witness | Community water point 10 km away | Attendant's log: the ole Sopia families' herds watered **05:30–08:00**, Kasaine signing the log at 05:30 and 08:00; the attendant saw him throughout |
| ev_gerald_statement | Witness | Foreman | "At six I saw two herders cutting the fence with wire cutters and ran to report it." |
| ev_records_gerald | **Records request** (Gerald's line; probable cause: `ev_cut` + `ev_waterpoint` contradict his statement) | PesaPap + Jamii Mobile | **05:10: KSh 20,000 received from ANDREW KERR.** Mast: ranch workshop zone 05:15–05:40 |
| ev_porter | Physical (found paper) + witness | Nakuru hotel night log | "Room 14, Mr A. Kerr, went out **04:50** in his vehicle, back **07:40**" |
| ev_vehicle | Physical, **warrant** | Andrew's 4×4 (probable cause: `ev_porter` + `ev_records_gerald`) | All-terrain tyres matching `ev_tracks`; under the rear seat, the **farrier's hammer**, wiped |
| ev_will | Physical (found paper) | Robert's study | Draft new will leaving the ranch to "Olkeri Conservation Trust", signing appointment Monday |
| ev_offer | Physical (found paper) | Robert's study | Developer's offer for subdivision into plots; Robert's note: "No. Never. Tell Andrew again." |
| ev_clare | Witness | By phone from Nairobi | She knew about the new will and "was relieved"; she hadn't spoken to Andrew since Friday |
| ev_stockcount | Physical (found paper) | Ranch records | Cattle count reconciled last week |

**Forensics**

| Test | Sample | Lab hours | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Autopsy | Body | Immediate | **Two impacts to the head from a square-faced object about 2.5 cm across**, delivered from above by a standing attacker. **No injuries consistent with a fall from a horse** (no shoulder or wrist fractures, no hoof marks). Time of death **06:00–07:00** |
| Tool-mark comparison | Wounds vs the hammer in `ev_vehicle` | 8 h | The hammer's square face **matches** the wound dimensions; trace of blood on the face |
| Soil | Tyre-tread soil vs fence-track soil | 8 h | Match: white soda-dusted soil found only near the lake edge |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gerald Muriithi | Cooperative | **"At six I saw two herders cut the fence."** | Yes (liar 2) | `ev_cut` + `ev_waterpoint`, then `ev_records_gerald` | *"I cut it. Mr Andrew paid me twenty thousand to cut it and say the herders did. He said it was to make the old man sell. I didn't know anything else would happen."* |
| Andrew Kerr | Cooperative, polished | **"I was asleep at the hotel in Nakuru until Clare called me at eight."** / "Robert was a stubborn old man, but I loved him." | First claim (liar 1) | `ev_porter` | *"I went for a drive to clear my head. I never went near the ranch."* (then `ev_tracks` + `ev_vehicle`) |
| Kasaine ole Sopia | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_cut`) | "We were at the water point. Ask the attendant." | True | — | *"Every time something happens on a ranch, the radio says 'herders'. Bring your book. Our names are in it."* |

1. `ev_cut` + `ev_waterpoint` → the herders were 10 km away watering their cattle; the fence was cut with ranch bolt cutters, not "wire cutters" by passing herders. Gerald's statement is false.

3. Autopsy + `ev_toolboard` + `ev_lekuta` → Robert was struck twice with a square-faced hammer, not thrown; the farrier's hammer went missing from the tack room between 05:30 and the ride.
4. `ev_porter` + `ev_tracks` + `ev_vehicle` (warrant) + tool marks → Andrew left his hotel at 04:50, his tyres match the tracks to the cut, and the hammer is in his vehicle → **WHO = Andrew Kerr**, **HOW = struck with a farrier's hammer and staged as a fall from his horse**, **WHY = Robert refused to sell and was about to leave the ranch to a conservation trust**.

**Eliminations**
- *WHO:* Kasaine ole Sopia: `ev_waterpoint`. Gerald Muriithi: workshop zone 05:15–05:40, then seen by the groom at the stables 06:05 (Nelson's statement); he cut the fence before dawn, he didn't strike Robert. Clare Kerr: `ev_clare`. Sankau Kipury: on the main gate from 05:00 with two guards.
- *HOW:*

| Method word | Refuted by |
|---|---|
| "thrown from his horse onto a rock" | Autopsy (square wounds, no fall injuries) |
| "kicked by his horse" | Autopsy (no hoof marks) |
| "attacked by herders with sticks" | Autopsy (square-faced object) + `ev_waterpoint` |
| "a heart attack in the saddle" | Autopsy |
| ✔ "struck with a farrier's hammer and staged as a fall from his horse" | — |

- *WHY:*

| Motive word | Refuted by |

| "a grazing dispute with the herders" | Not Andrew's; and the herders are eliminated |
| "he'd caught Andrew stealing cattle" | `ev_stockcount` |
| "a quarrel over Clare's divorce" | `ev_clare` (no divorce) |
| "an unpaid debt" | No record of money between them |
| ✔ "Robert refused to sell and was about to leave the ranch to a conservation trust" | — |

**Red herrings / twist.**
- Red herring: the herders, and the radio.
- **Twist:** the accident was staged, and so was the blame. Sankau's line to Amani when the herders are cleared: *"Thank you for opening the book before the mouth."*

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Robert Hollis by {how}, because {why}.` WHO: Andrew Kerr, Gerald Muriithi, Kasaine ole Sopia, Clare Kerr, Sankau Kipury (5).

**Clock plan.** Scene and toolboard (2 h), groom (2 h), Sankau and the cut (2 h), the water point (2 h), Gerald broken (2 h), records on Gerald (4 h): payment from Andrew. Hotel night log (2 h). Warrant on the vehicle (3 h, 1 stamp): hammer to the lab, soil to the lab. **Detain Andrew** at this point: tool marks back at hour 8, soil at hour 8. Press him. 9 h of the detention used.

**Credibility path.** 2 stamps: records on Gerald, warrant on the vehicle.

**New interface beat.** **Two liars in one case**, one covering for the other, and the outline board (an empty silhouette where a tool should be) as a hotspot type used again later.

**Kenyan texture.** Rift Valley ranches beside soda lakes, drought pushing herds onto ranch land, the reflex to blame pastoralists (shown and then dismantled), a water point attendant's log as the herders' alibi, high-tensile fencing, ranch staff of many communities.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** ole (Maa: "son of", used in names), boma (homestead), shamba, wafugaji (herders).

Victim M, 60s, Kenyan-European. *Audit note: this case deliberately puts a pastoralist community under suspicion and clears it on the evidence. ### Case 35 — Earth Wire

`case-035` · Rift Valley · 20 min · suspects 3 · chain 3 · herrings 1 · liars **2** · groups WHO, WHY, HOW · stamps needed 1 (warrant)

**OB entry.** OB 05/28/10, 19:05. The fictional Njoro Agricultural College reports a lecturer found dead in the soil-science laboratory. **Recorded as a suspected electrical accident.**

**Setting.** Fictional **Njoro Agricultural College** near Njoro town: old stone buildings, a soil-science lab with metal drying ovens, a library with card-swipe turnstiles, student hostels, a robotics club with a numbered tool register.

**Victim.** **Dr. Damaris Wanjohi**, 44, soil-science lecturer and the college's exams officer. Electrocuted at about 16:30 when she opened a soil-drying oven, as she did every day.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ronald Omwenga | 23 | Suspect | Final-year student, robotics club member | **Culprit** (liar 1) |
| Elkanah Kiprop | 39 | Suspect | Lab technician | Innocent of the killing; **liar 2** (faked the safety checks) |
| Dr. Kenneth Mugambi | 50 | Suspect | Colleague; quarrelled with her over the moderation of exam marks | Innocent (red herring): at a senate meeting |
| Nelly Chepkurui | 46 | Witness | Librarian | Innocent |
| Brenda Cherono | 19 | Witness | First-year student | Innocent |
| Joshua Ndolo | 52 | Witness | College electrician | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Ronald ran a paid WhatsApp group selling leaked exam papers. A student sent Damaris a screenshot showing his number. On Monday she told him she'd take it to the disciplinary committee on Thursday: expulsion and a criminal report. Ronald knew from the robotics club how the lab's old ovens were wired, and knew the technician had removed the lab's tripping safety switch months ago because it "kept going off". At about 15:50, while the technician was at tea, Ronald went into the lab, opened the back panel of Damaris's oven, cut the earth wire with his club side-cutters and pressed the live conductor against the metal chassis. At 16:30 she touched the door handle.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_oven | Physical | Lab | Soil-drying oven; back panel screws loosened; Dr. Wanjohi's sample trays beside it |
| ev_joshua | Witness + physical | Electrician's inspection | **The earth wire is freshly cut**: bright copper ends, no corrosion. The live wire's insulation has been **stripped with a tool** and bent to touch the chassis. **The lab's safety cut-out switch (RCD) has been removed** from the board, "months ago by the look of the dust" |
| ev_checklist | Physical (found paper) | Lab wall | Weekly safety checklist, every box ticked "earth OK, RCD OK" through to today, **all in the same pen and the same pressure**, as if filled in at one sitting |
| ev_canteen | Physical (found paper) | Elkanah | Canteen receipt 15:45; the canteen lady says he stayed until about 16:20 |
| ev_brenda | Witness | First-year | Saw Ronald go into the soil lab at about 15:50 "with his robotics bag", and come out about ten minutes later |
| ev_turnstile | Physical (found paper) | Library swipe log | R. Omwenga: **in 14:02, out 15:40, in 17:10** |
| ev_damaris_phone | Phone (victim's, unlocked by her husband) | Her office | Screenshot from a student: group "Njoro Leaks: CAT papers KSh 500, send to 07xx xxx 562". Her draft email to the disciplinary committee naming **Ronald Omwenga**, saved Monday |
| ev_toolregister | Physical (found paper) | Robotics club | Toolkit **#7** (including side-cutters) issued to **R. Omwenga** this term |
| ev_cutters | Physical, **warrant** | Ronald's hostel room (probable cause: `ev_brenda` + `ev_toolregister`) | Side-cutters from toolkit #7, with a **small notch in one jaw** |
| ev_senate | Physical (found paper) | Senate minutes | Dr. Mugambi present 15:00–17:30 |
| ev_transcript | Physical (found paper) | Exams office | Ronald's grades: B+ average; nothing failed |

**Forensics**

| Test | Sample | Lab hours | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Autopsy | Body | Immediate | **Electrocution**: entry burn on the right palm, exit on the left foot. No other injury. Time of death **about 16:30** |
| Tool-mark comparison | Cut earth wire vs `ev_cutters` | 8 h | The wire ends carry the impression of a **notched jaw**: match |
| Toxicology | Blood | 18 h | Clean |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ronald Omwenga | Cooperative | **"I was in the library from two until six."** / "I've never touched those ovens." | Both (liar 1) | Claim 1: `ev_turnstile`. Claim 2: `ev_brenda` + tool marks | *"I went to the lab to ask her to give me a chance. She wasn't there. I left."* |
| Elkanah Kiprop | Cooperative | **"I checked that oven this morning. It was earthed. The RCD was working."** | Yes (liar 2) | `ev_joshua` + `ev_checklist` | *"The RCD kept tripping. I took it out in June so the ovens would run. I filled the checklist every Friday without checking. I've been afraid every day."* (new fact: the lab had no safety cut-out, which anyone who used the lab often knew) |
| Dr. Kenneth Mugambi | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_checklist`) | "I was in senate." | True | — | Topic "moderation": a professional disagreement, "she was usually right" |

**Proof**
1. `ev_joshua` → this was no accident of old wiring: the earth wire was freshly cut and the live wire deliberately bent to the chassis. Elkanah's broken claim explains why nothing tripped: there was no safety switch.
2. `ev_turnstile` + `ev_brenda` + Ronald's broken claim → he left the library at 15:40 and was in the lab at about 15:50, alone, while Elkanah was at tea.
3. `ev_toolregister` + `ev_cutters` (warrant) + tool marks + `ev_damaris_phone` → his club side-cutters cut the wire, and Damaris was about to report him → **WHO = Ronald Omwenga**, **HOW = electrocuted by an oven he deliberately made live**, **WHY = she was about to report him for selling leaked exam papers**.

**Eliminations**
- *WHO:* Elkanah Kiprop: `ev_canteen` (at tea 15:45–16:20); his lie hid negligence, not murder. Dr. Mugambi: `ev_senate`. Nelly Chepkurui: at the library desk. Brenda Cherono: in her practical class from 16:00 (class register).
- *HOW:*

| Method word | Refuted by |
|---|---|
| "an accident caused by old, faulty wiring" | `ev_joshua` (fresh cut, tool-stripped insulation) + tool marks |
| "a heart attack" | Autopsy (electrical burns) |
| "poisoned by lab chemicals" | Toxicology clean |
| "a blow to the head" | Autopsy |
| ✔ "electrocuted by an oven he deliberately made live" | — |

- *WHY:*

| Motive word | Refuted by |
|---|---|
| "she had failed him" | `ev_transcript` |
| "the technician's faked safety checks" | That's Elkanah's failing, not a motive |
| "a dispute over exam moderation" | Dr. Mugambi's quarrel; he's eliminated |
| "a robotics competition result" | She had no role in the robotics club (club register) |
| ✔ "she was about to report him for selling leaked exam papers" | — |

**Red herrings / twist.** Red herrings: the colleague's moderation quarrel, and the technician's frightened lie. Halima, after: *"Charge the boy. And send the college a letter about that switch."*

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Damaris Wanjohi by {how}, because {why}.` WHO: Ronald Omwenga, Elkanah Kiprop, Kenneth Mugambi, Nelly Chepkurui, Brenda Cherono (5).

**Clock plan.** No detention needed. Electrician (2 h), checklist and Elkanah (2 h), turnstile log (1 h), Brenda (2 h), tool register (1 h), warrant on the hostel room (3 h, 1 stamp) → tool marks (8 h).

**Credibility path.** 1 stamp.

**New interface beat.** **Two liars where only one is the killer.** The notebook's red/grey marking (from case 14) now does real work: the player has to sort which broken claim implicates and which only embarrasses.

**Kenyan texture.** Agricultural colleges, exam leaks sold on WhatsApp groups ("CATs" are continuous assessment tests), safety equipment bypassed to keep old machines running, robotics clubs with numbered tool kits.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** CAT (continuous assessment test), leak (leaked exam), stima, fundi wa stima (electrician).

**Images (5).** Portraits: Damaris, Ronald, Elkanah, Kenneth. Location: the soil lab with its row of old metal ovens.

**Audit tags.** Culprit M, 20s, Kisii-origin name, motive cover-up. Victim F, 40s, Kikuyu-origin name.

### Case 36 — Extended Bags

`case-036` · Rift Valley · 21 min · suspects 3 · chain 3 · herrings 1 · liars **2** · groups WHO, WHY, HOW · stamps needed 2 (records, warrant) · **spine background detail**

**OB entry.** OB 09/04/11, 07:20. A co-operative clerk reports the co-op's chairlady found dead inside the potato store at the Molo co-op yard; the store's door was barred and padlocked from outside.

**Setting.** Molo, high and cold: potato fields to the horizon, frost some mornings, nights near 3 °C. Fictional **Molo Highland Potato Co-op**: a yard, an office, and a thick-walled stone potato store with vents, a heavy wooden door and an iron outside bar. The co-op's own padlock is a brass one with a numbered key. A long-running fight in the potato trade: brokers using oversized "extended" bags of 120–130 kg while farmers are paid as if for 50 kg.

**Victim.** **Susan Chelangat**, 52, co-op chairlady, who led the campaign for the legal 50 kg bag.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vivian Chepngeno | 36 | Suspect | Potato broker; two of her lorries impounded last week for extended bags after Susan's complaint | **Culprit** (liar 1) |
| Hosea Kahiga | 61 | Suspect | Lost the co-op chair election to Susan; bitter | Innocent (red herring): at a funeral wake |
| Benjamin Kirwa | 33 | Suspect | Co-op night guard | Innocent of the killing; **liar 2** (left his post) |
| Agnetta Rutto | 28 | Witness | Co-op clerk; found her | Innocent |
| Jared Kimutai | 41 | Witness | County produce-enforcement officer | Innocent |

**What really happened.** The impounding cost Vivian KSh 200,000 in fines and her Nairobi buyer's contract. At about 18:30 on Monday she drove to the co-op yard, where Susan stayed late counting bags in the store. The night guard had gone to watch a football match. They argued inside the store; Susan turned back to her count; Vivian stepped out, swung the heavy door shut, dropped the outside bar and locked it with a steel padlock from her lorry's toolbox. She drove away at 18:55. The stone walls block phone signal. Susan died of cold in the early hours.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_door | Physical | Potato store | Door barred and locked with a **steel padlock**. The co-op's own **brass padlock** (key No. 12) is hanging open on its nail in the office |
| ev_agnetta | Witness | Clerk | Found the store locked at 07:00 with "a padlock that isn't ours"; had the lock cut and found Susan |
| ev_susan_phone | Phone (victim's) | Inside the store | Several outgoing calls after 18:50, all failed: **"No network"** |
| ev_ventlog | Physical (found paper) | Store wall | Ventilation and CO₂ readings logged by Susan at 18:00: vents open, CO₂ normal |
| ev_enforcement | Physical (found paper) | County officer | Impound notice: two lorries, owner **V. Chepngeno**, "extended bags, 128–131 kg"; complaint lodged by **Molo Highland Potato Co-op, chairlady S. Chelangat** |
| ev_jared | Witness | County officer | Vivian told him at the impound: "That woman will regret this." |
| ev_gatebook | Physical (found paper) | Guard's gate book | Entries signed by Benjamin every hour from 18:00 to 06:00, "all quiet", all in the same ink |
| ev_bar | Witness + physical | Bar owner in Molo town (statement only); bar receipt | Benjamin watched the match at the bar **18:10–23:00**; receipt timed 22:41 |
| ev_records | **Records request** (Vivian's line; probable cause: `ev_door` + `ev_enforcement` + `ev_jared`) | Jamii Mobile | Mast **Molo co-op zone 18:22–18:56**; then Molo town |
| ev_lorry | Physical, **warrant** | Vivian's lorry (probable cause: `ev_records`) | In the cab: a key ring with a **steel padlock key that opens the lock** from the store door; the toolbox's padlock hasp is empty. Also in the cab: a loan agreement, "Lorry financed by **Mvua Holdings**, repayments to **Till 880 214**" (spine; not needed) |
| ev_wake | Witness | Host (statement only) | Hosea Kahiga sat at a funeral wake in Elburgon from 17:00 until morning |
| ev_ledger | Physical (found paper) | Co-op | Vivian's purchases from the co-op paid in full; no seed-potato debts either way |

**Forensics**

| Test | Sample | Lab hours | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Autopsy | Body | Immediate | **Hypothermia.** No injuries, no alcohol. Time of death **01:00–04:00**: she was alive for hours after the door was locked |
| Toxicology | Blood | 18 h | Clean |
| Fingerprints | Steel padlock vs Vivian (**refuses → detention**) | 6 h | Match |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vivian Chepngeno | Cooperative | **"I was in Nakuru town all evening."** / "I have nothing against that woman." | First claim (liar 1) | `ev_records` | *"I went to the co-op to talk to her. She wouldn't listen. I left. I never touched that door."* |
| Benjamin Kirwa | Cooperative | **"I was at the gate all night. I signed every hour."** | Yes (liar 2) | `ev_bar` (and `ev_gatebook`'s identical ink) | *"I was at the bar. I signed the whole night's book when I came back at eleven. The gate was empty."* (new fact: anyone could have entered 18:10–23:00) |
| Hosea Kahiga | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_enforcement`) | "I was at a wake in Elburgon." | True | — | Topic "Susan": "We fought for years about the chair. Not about this." |

**Proof**
1. Benjamin's broken claim + `ev_bar` → the yard was unguarded 18:10–23:00; anyone could have come.
2. `ev_door` + autopsy + `ev_susan_phone` → Susan was locked in with a padlock that isn't the co-op's, couldn't call out, and died of cold hours later.
3. `ev_records` + Vivian's broken claim + `ev_lorry` (warrant) + fingerprints → Vivian was at the yard 18:22–18:56, the key to the steel padlock is on her ring, and her prints are on the lock → **WHO = Vivian Chepngeno**, **HOW = locked her in the potato store overnight, where she died of cold**, **WHY = Susan's complaint got Vivian's lorries impounded for oversized bags**.

| "a heart attack while working" | Autopsy: hypothermia |
| "gas from rotting potatoes" | `ev_ventlog` |
| "poisoned" | Toxicology |
| ✔ "locked her in the potato store overnight, where she died of cold" | — |

- *WHY:*

| Motive word | Refuted by |

| "unpaid potato money" | `ev_ledger` |
| "a seed-potato debt" | `ev_ledger` |
| "a quarrel over the guard's absence" | Benjamin's problem, not a motive |
| ✔ "Susan's complaint got her lorries impounded for oversized bags" | — |

**Red herrings / twist.** Red herrings: the bitter election rival, and the guard's false gate book. *Tone note: this is the darkest method in region 4. The reconstruction ends at the door closing; it does not show the night.*

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Susan Chelangat by {how}, because {why}.` WHO: Vivian Chepngeno, Hosea Kahiga, Benjamin Kirwa, Agnetta Rutto, Jared Kimutai (5).

**Clock plan.** Scene (2 h), Agnetta (2 h), enforcement officer (2 h), Benjamin broken via the bar (3 h), records on Vivian (4 h, 1 stamp), warrant on her lorry (3 h, 1 stamp). **Detain Vivian**, take prints (1 h): result at hour 6 of the detention. Press her with the key and the prints.

**Credibility path.** 2 stamps.

**New interface beat.** **Absence of signal as evidence.** The mast map shows the stone store as a dead zone; the failed-call log becomes a fact about the room, not just about the phone.

**Kenyan texture.** Molo's cold potato country, the "extended bag" fight between farmers and brokers, county produce enforcement, co-op chairladies, a funeral wake that runs all night.

**Spine.** `ev_lorry` carries `t_mvua` (Mvua finances brokers' lorries). Pinned on solve.

**Glossary.** viazi (potatoes), gunia (sack), chama / co-op, matanga (wake).

**Images (5).** Portraits: Susan, Vivian, Hosea, Benjamin. Location: the Molo co-op yard at dawn, frost on the ground, the stone store with its iron bar.

### Case 37 — The Camel Coat

`case-037` · Rift Valley · 22 min · suspects 3 · **chain 4** · herrings 1 · liars 1 (culprit) · groups WHO, WHY, HOW · stamps needed 1 (records) · **twist: the man seen alive at 21:00 was already dead**

**OB entry.** OB 21/11/11, 07:42 (Tuesday 11 November). A cleaner reports the chief executive of a teachers' sacco found dead in the strong room of the sacco's office on Kenyatta Avenue, Nakuru. The night askari says the CEO left the building at 21:00 the previous night.

**Setting.** Fictional **Rift Walimu Sacco**, a teachers' savings and loans co-operative in an office block on Kenyatta Avenue, Nakuru town: a banking hall, offices, a strong room for loan files and cash, a front door watched by an askari and a back door that board members have keys to. Coats hang on hooks behind each office door.

**Victim.** **Ezra Kamande**, 45, chief executive. Struck with the sacco's heavy brass commemorative paperweight. Everyone in town knows his long **camel-coloured coat** and **grey felt hat**.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kirimi Muthuri | 64 | Suspect | Board treasurer and loan signatory for 15 years | **Culprit** |
| Wilfred Cheruiyot | 41 | Suspect | Deputy CEO, wanted the top job | Innocent (red herring): at a club dinner |
| Jemimah Mumbi | 50 | Suspect | Member with a defaulted loan; threatened Ezra at the counter last week | Innocent: at her shop, then home |
| Lemaron Leteipa | 35 | Witness | Night askari | Innocent (honestly mistaken) |
| Eunice Kamande | 43 | Witness | Ezra's wife | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Ezra found 41 loans worth KSh 18 million issued to members who didn't exist, or were dead, all approved by Kirimi. At 18:00 on Monday he called Kirimi into the strong room where the loan files are kept and told him he'd report to the board and the regulator in the morning. Kirimi hit him with the paperweight. He locked the strong room and waited in his office. At 21:00, in the dim front lobby, he walked out past the askari wearing Ezra's coat and hat, giving a wave. He crossed to the chemist on the corner (his blood-pressure tablets) and paid with his sacco member discount at 21:05, then came back in through the back door with his own key, hung the coat and hat on Ezra's hook, and left again at about 21:20. The chemist's receipt stayed in the coat pocket.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_lemaron | Witness | Askari | "Mr Kamande came out at nine in his coat and hat and waved." Asked again: he didn't see the face under the hat brim; "he walked a bit bent; Mr Kamande walks very straight, but it was late" |
| ev_coat | Physical | Hook behind Ezra's office door | The camel coat and grey hat, hanging. In the coat pocket: a **chemist's receipt, 21:05**, blood-pressure tablets, member discount, **"Member 0114 — K. Muthuri"** **(Probable cause for a records request)** |
| ev_eunice | Witness | Wife | Ezra ate supper at home at eight every night of their marriage. He called at 17:50 to say "I'll be late, I have to deal with Kirimi." He never came home |
| ev_loanfiles | Physical (found paper) | Strong room | 41 loan files, members' ID copies; signatures for approval: **K. Muthuri** |
| ev_deceased | Physical (found paper) | Sacco's own register | 17 of the 41 "members" are on the sacco's deceased-members list; the rest have ID numbers that belong to nobody on the register |
| ev_ezra_note | Physical (found paper) | His desk | Draft letter to the board and the co-operatives regulator: "41 irregular loans approved by the treasurer" |
| ev_records | **Records request** (Kirimi's line) | Jamii Mobile + PesaPap | Mast **Nakuru CBD 17:40–21:30**, then Milimani (his home). PesaPap: chemist **21:05** |
| ev_backdoor | Physical | Back door | Board members' keys only (five people); the door bolt shows it was opened and closed after the cleaner locked it at 18:30 (cleaner's routine statement: she always shoots the bolt and the bolt was drawn in the morning) |
| ev_club | Physical (found paper) | Nakuru club dinner bill | Wilfred Cheruiyot 18:00–22:30, signed by him at 22:28; 30 diners |
| ev_jemimah | Witness | Neighbour (statement only) | Jemimah closed her shop at 20:00 and was home by 20:20; they watched TV together |
| ev_minutes | Physical (found paper) | Board minutes | The sacco's land purchase approved unanimously last year |

**Forensics**

| Test | Sample | Lab hours | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Autopsy | Body | Immediate | Struck once on the head with a heavy object with a rounded edge. **Time of death 17:30–19:30**: rigor and body temperature; stomach contents show lunch partly digested and **no supper** |
| Comparison | Wound vs the brass paperweight | Immediate (Dr. Chebii checks on site) | Consistent |
| Fingerprints | Paperweight vs Kirimi (consents, confident) | 6 h | His prints are on it, but he's on the board and handles it often: **not decisive** on its own (the card says so plainly, to teach that prints can be innocent) |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kirimi Muthuri | Cooperative | **"I left the office at five and was home in Milimani by half past."** / "Ezra left at nine. The askari saw him." | First claim (and the second is an assumption, not his own observation) | `ev_records` or `ev_coat` | *"I stayed late on some files. I went to the chemist and went home. I didn't see Ezra after five."* |
| Wilfred Cheruiyot | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_ezra_note`) | "I was at the club dinner." | True | — | Topic "Kirimi": "Nobody questions the treasurer. He was here before any of us." |
| Jemimah Mumbi | Cooperative | "I was at my shop, then home." | True | — | Topic "threat": "I shouted. I owe them money. I don't kill people." |

**Proof**
1. Autopsy + `ev_eunice` → Ezra died between 17:30 and 19:30, before his unbroken eight o'clock supper; he couldn't have walked out at 21:00. **The man the askari saw was someone in his coat. (Twist.)**
2. `ev_coat` → whoever wore the coat at 21:00 bought blood-pressure tablets at 21:05 on Kirimi Muthuri's member number.
3. `ev_records` + Kirimi's broken claim + `ev_backdoor` → Kirimi was in the CBD until 21:30, not home at 17:30, and the back door, which only board members can open, was used after 18:30.
4. `ev_loanfiles` + `ev_deceased` + `ev_ezra_note` → Ezra had found 41 ghost loans approved by Kirimi and was reporting them in the morning → **WHO = Kirimi Muthuri**, **HOW = struck with the brass paperweight in the strong room**, **WHY = Ezra had found the ghost-member loans he'd approved**.

**Eliminations**
- *WHO:* Wilfred Cheruiyot: `ev_club`. Jemimah Mumbi: `ev_jemimah` (and she has no back-door key). Lemaron Leteipa: at the front door all night; honest but mistaken. Eunice Kamande: at home waiting (children's statements).
- *HOW:*

| Method word | Refuted by |
|---|---|
| "attacked after he came back to the office late at night" | Autopsy time of death (before 19:30) |
| "locked in the strong room until he suffocated" | Autopsy: blunt injury, not suffocation |
| "a heart attack" | Autopsy |
| "poisoned" | Autopsy: no signs; tox not needed |
| ✔ "struck with the brass paperweight in the strong room" | — |

- *WHY:*

| Motive word | Refuted by |
|---|---|
| "the CEO post" | Wilfred's ambition; eliminated |
| "a defaulted loan" | Jemimah's; eliminated |
| "the sacco's land purchase" | `ev_minutes` (unanimous, no dispute) |
| "a salary dispute" | Board minutes and payroll: no dispute |
| ✔ "Ezra had found the ghost-member loans he'd approved" | — |

**Red herrings / twist.**
- Red herring: the ambitious deputy.
- **Twist:** the last sighting is false. The askari didn't lie; he saw a coat and a hat and filled in the rest, like everyone does. Mwalimu, after: *"People see the coat. Detectives see who's inside it."*

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Ezra Kamande by {how}, because {why}.` WHO: Kirimi Muthuri, Wilfred Cheruiyot, Jemimah Mumbi, Lemaron Leteipa, Eunice Kamande (5).

**Clock plan.** No detention required. Autopsy (0 h) → Eunice (2 h) → askari re-questioned (2 h) → the coat on the hook (1 h) → records on Kirimi (4 h, 1 stamp) → loan files and deceased register (2 h).

**Credibility path.** 1 stamp.

**New interface beat.** **A witness who isn't lying but is wrong.** Lemaron's statement gets a third mark, neither red nor grey: an amber "mistaken" mark once the coat is found. The notebook now distinguishes lies, innocent lies and honest mistakes.

**Kenyan texture.** Teachers' saccos and their loans, ghost members on the books (a recurring real scandal), a sacco treasurer no one questions, a chemist that gives sacco member discounts, a man known in town by his coat and hat.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** walimu (teachers), sacco, mkopo (loan), mlinzi / askari (guard), kofia (hat).

**Images (6).** Portraits: Ezra (in the camel coat and grey hat), Kirimi, Wilfred, Jemimah, Lemaron. Location: Kenyatta Avenue, Nakuru, at night, the sacco's lit lobby.

**Audit tags.** Culprit M, 60s, Meru-origin name, motive cover-up. Victim M, 40s, Kikuyu-origin name.

### Case 38 — Lactometer

`case-038` · Rift Valley · 20 min · suspects 3 · chain 3 · herrings 1 · liars 1 (culprit) · groups WHO, WHY, HOW · stamps needed 1 (records)

**OB entry.** OB 13/17/11, 11:30 (Monday 17 November). A dairy co-operative in Ol Kalou reports its milk grader found dead in the collection centre after morning collection.

**Setting.** Ol Kalou, Nyandarua: cool highlands, small dairy farms, farmers carrying milk in numbered steel cans to fictional **Kinangop Highland Dairy Co-op**'s collection centre each morning, 06:00–09:00. The grader tests every can with a **lactometer** (a floating gauge that shows milk density) and an alcohol test; milk that fails is rejected and poured away. A laminated chart on the wall: *"Normal whole milk reads 1.026–1.032. Below 1.026: water added."*

**Victim.** **Dorothy Wangechi**, 33, milk grader for five years. Struck with a 10-litre steel milk can.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mary Amoit | 44 | Suspect | Dairy farmer with three cows; her milk was rejected three days running | **Culprit** |
| Hudson Karanja | 58 | Suspect | Co-op chairman; shouted at Dorothy last week about "missing litres" | Innocent (red herring): at a dairy board meeting |
| Zakayo Ndegwa | 60 | Suspect | Farmer; paid Dorothy to pass his watered milk | Innocent of the killing: milking at home |
| Peris Wanjugu | 37 | Witness | Co-op clerk | Innocent |
| Ezekiel Njuguna | 26 | Witness (statement only) | Boda rider | Innocent |

**What really happened.** For a year Dorothy had taken KSh 200 a day from some farmers to pass their watered milk. To keep the centre's overall readings looking normal she rejected honest milk from farmers who wouldn't pay. Mary refused to pay. Three days running her good milk was marked "rejected" and poured out: KSh 4,500 lost, and she fell below the co-op's delivery minimum for a loan she needed for school fees. At 10:05 she called Dorothy to say she was coming. A boda dropped her at 10:20. Alone after the clerk left at 10:00, they argued at the grading table; Dorothy laughed and said "pay like everyone else". Mary hit her with a steel can from the rack and left on foot at about 10:35.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Grading table | Struck with a steel milk can, which lies dented on the floor |
| ev_gradingbook | Physical (found paper) | Grading table | This week's readings by farmer. **Mary Amoit: 1.029, 1.028, 1.030, all marked "REJECTED".** Zakayo Ndegwa: 1.022, 1.023, 1.021, all marked "ACCEPTED" |
| ev_chart | Physical | Wall | "Normal whole milk reads 1.026–1.032. Below 1.026: water added." |
| ev_notebook | Physical (found paper) | Dorothy's handbag | A small notebook with a column headed "B": names and daily ticks of 200. **Zakayo: ticks.** **"Amoit — REFUSED"** three days running |
| ev_dorothy_phone | Phone (victim's, unlocked by her mother) | Handbag | Incoming call **10:05** from **"Mama Amoit"**, 1 min 10 s **(probable cause for records)** |
| ev_records | **Records request** (Mary's line) | Jamii Mobile + PesaPap | Call to Dorothy 10:05. PesaPap **10:16: KSh 100 to EZEKIEL NJUGUNA** (boda). Mast **collection-centre zone 10:20–10:40** |
| ev_ezekiel | Witness | Boda rider | Took Mary from her farm to the centre, dropped her at 10:20; "she was angry, she said she'd been robbed for three days" |
| ev_peris | Witness | Clerk | Left at 10:00 to bank the collection; Dorothy was fine and alone; found her at 11:20 |
| ev_dairyboard | Physical (found paper) | County dairy board minutes, Nyahururu | Hudson Karanja present 09:00–13:00 |
| ev_zakayo | Witness | His son (statement only) | Zakayo was milking and then cutting fodder at home 09:30–12:00 |
| ev_shrinkage | Physical (found paper) | Co-op office | The "missing litres" were a cooling-tank meter fault, fixed and logged on Friday |

**Forensics**

| Test | Sample | Lab hours | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Autopsy | Body | Immediate | **Two blows** with a heavy rounded-rim object matching a milk can; no fall injury; no fluid in the lungs. Time of death **10:15–11:00** |
| Fingerprints | The dented can vs Mary (**refuses → detention**) | 6 h | Her prints on the can's **base**, gripped upside down as if swung, not carried by the handle |
| Toxicology | Blood | 18 h | Clean |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mary Amoit | Cooperative, then refuses prints | **"I delivered at half past six and went home. I didn't go back."** / "That girl stole from me." | First claim | `ev_records` or `ev_ezekiel` | *"I went back to show her my milk was good. She laughed. She said pay like everyone else. I left her standing there."* |
| Zakayo Ndegwa | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_notebook`) | "I was at home milking." | True | — | *"Yes, I paid her. Two hundred a day. Everyone who waters pays. I'm ashamed. I didn't hurt her."* |
| Hudson Karanja | Cooperative | "I was in Nyahururu at the dairy board." | True | — | Topic "missing litres": shows `ev_shrinkage` |

**Proof**
1. `ev_gradingbook` + `ev_chart` + `ev_notebook` → the numbers expose the scheme: Mary's milk was normal (1.028–1.030) but rejected; Zakayo's was watered (1.021–1.023) but accepted, and he's ticked as paying "B". Mary refused to pay and lost three days' milk.
2. Mary's claim + `ev_dorothy_phone` + `ev_records` + `ev_ezekiel` → she called Dorothy at 10:05 and was dropped at the centre at 10:20, inside the window `ev_peris` and the autopsy set.
3. Fingerprints (needs the detention) → her prints are on the can's base, as if swung → **WHO = Mary Amoit**, **HOW = struck with a steel milk can**, **WHY = Dorothy rejected her honest milk because she refused to pay bribes**.

**Eliminations**
- *WHO:* Hudson Karanja: `ev_dairyboard`. Zakayo Ndegwa: `ev_zakayo`. Peris Wanjugu: at the bank (deposit slip 10:25). Ezekiel Njuguna: rode off at 10:21 to another fare (his PesaPap at 10:34 from a passenger in Ol Kalou town).
- *HOW:*

| Method word | Refuted by |
|---|---|
| "fell and hit her head on the cooling tank" | Autopsy (two blows, can-rim shape) |
| "drowned in the cooling tank" | Autopsy (no fluid in lungs) |
| "poisoned with milk preservative" | Toxicology |
| "strangled" | Autopsy |
| ✔ "struck with a steel milk can" | — |

- *WHY:*

| Motive word | Refuted by |
|---|---|
| "the missing-litres dispute" | `ev_shrinkage` (and that's Hudson's) |
| "fear of being exposed as a briber" | That's Zakayo's position; Zakayo is eliminated |
| "a land boundary dispute" | Neither owns land next to the other (co-op member map) |
| "an unpaid loan between them" | No record of money between them |
| ✔ "Dorothy rejected her honest milk because she refused to pay bribes" | — |

**Red herrings / twist.** Red herring: the chairman's shouting about missing litres.

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Dorothy Wangechi by {how}, because {why}.` WHO: Mary Amoit, Hudson Karanja, Zakayo Ndegwa, Peris Wanjugu, Ezekiel Njuguna (5).

**Clock plan.** Grading book and chart (1 h), notebook (1 h), Peris (2 h), Dorothy's phone (1 h), records on Mary (4 h, 1 stamp), boda rider (2 h). **Detain Mary**, take prints (1 h); result at hour 6. Press.

**Credibility path.** 1 stamp.

**New interface beat.** **Reading a scale against a reference.** The grading book's numbers can be dragged onto the wall chart; each reading snaps into "normal" or "watered". Small domain knowledge, given in-world, decides the case.

**Kenyan texture.** Smallholder dairy in Nyandarua, morning milk collection with numbered cans, lactometer readings, the everyday corruption of a grader who decides whose milk is "good", school fees riding on three cows.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** maziwa (milk), mkebe / mtungi (can), lactometer, karo (school fees).

**Images (5).** Portraits: Dorothy, Mary, Hudson, Zakayo. Location: a milk collection centre at 07:00, farmers queuing with steel cans in the mist.

**Audit tags.** Culprit F, 40s, Teso-origin name, motive revenge (for the bribery rejections). Victim F, 30s, Kikuyu-origin name.

### Case 39 — Asali

`case-039` · Rift Valley · 22 min · suspects 3 · **chain 4** · herrings 1 · liars 1 (culprit) · groups WHO, WHY, HOW · stamps needed 1 (records)

**OB entry.** OB 30/23/11, 09:10 (Sunday 23 November). A hospital in Nakuru reports the death of a sawmill owner from Eldama Ravine after four days of unexplained bleeding; doctors suspect poisoning.

**Setting.** Eldama Ravine in Baringo county, on the edge of the forests: fictional **Mukhwana Timber Works**, a sawmill with a yard of logs, a canteen and an office; the owner's house up the hill. Baringo is famous for its honey; a jar of "Asali ya Baringo" is a common gift. The case starts at the fictional **Rift General Hospital**, Nakuru.

**Victim.** **Jacob Mukhwana**, 58, sawmill owner, 30 years in Eldama Ravine. Began bleeding from the gums on Wednesday, admitted Thursday, died Sunday.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cecilia Njiru | 54 | Suspect | His business partner (40% of the sawmill) | **Culprit** |
| Barnabas Kimeli | 37 | Suspect | Workers' representative; led a strike last month and threatened Jacob publicly | Innocent (red herring) |
| Allan Mukhwana | 27 | Suspect | Jacob's son; deep in debt | Innocent: in Nairobi until Saturday |
| Pamela Mukhwana | 52 | Witness | Jacob's wife | Innocent |
| Dr. Ibrahim Gedi | 45 | Witness | Physician at Rift General | Innocent |
| Rebecca Lokwang | 40 | Witness (statement only) | Honey seller at Marigat market | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Jacob found that Cecilia had been buying logs from a supplier on the forest service's published blacklist for illegally felled trees from a protected forest block, and passing them through the sawmill's books. On Friday he told her he'd report it and dissolve the partnership. On Saturday she brought him a jar of Baringo honey "for your chest, for the cold", with a card: *"For J. — get well — C."* She'd mixed crushed pellets of a long-acting rat poison into it. He took a spoonful in his tea every morning. Long-acting rat poisons stop the blood clotting over days.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_hospital | Physical (found paper) + witness | Dr. Gedi | Admission notes: bleeding gums, bruising, blood that wouldn't clot. "This is what we see with long-acting rat poison. Exposure would have started three to six days before the symptoms." |
| ev_honey | Physical | Jacob's kitchen (Pamela hands it over) | A jar of honey, half eaten, handwritten label **"Asali ya Baringo"**, and a card: **"For J. — get well — C."** |
| ev_pamela | Witness | Wife | Cecilia brought the honey **on Saturday**. Jacob took a spoonful in his tea every morning from Sunday. Nobody else in the house eats honey; Pamela is diabetic and the children are away |
| ev_blacklist | Physical (found paper) | Jacob's office | The forest service's published list of blacklisted timber suppliers, with one name circled: "Mau Hardwoods" (fictional) |
| ev_invoices | Physical (found paper) | Sawmill accounts | Eleven invoices from **Mau Hardwoods**, all approved by **C. Njiru** |
| ev_jacob_letter | Physical (found paper) | His desk | Draft letter, dated Friday: "Dissolution of partnership; report to the forest service attached" |
| ev_cecilia_jar | Physical | Cecilia's house (she offers it, confidently) | Her own jar of honey "from the same batch" |
| ev_rebecca | Witness | Honey seller | Sold Cecilia **two** jars last Thursday, ordinary honey |
| ev_records | **Records request** (Cecilia's line; probable cause: `ev_honey` + `ev_pamela` + `ev_jacob_letter`) | PesaPap | **Last Friday, 16:40: KSh 960 to an agrovet till in Eldama Ravine, reference "Rat Kill Max x4"** (fictional brand) |
| ev_canteen | Physical | Sawmill canteen | Food samples kept from the past week (a hygiene rule) |
| ev_bus | Physical (found paper) | Allan shows it | Bus ticket Nairobi–Eldama Ravine, arrived Saturday 18:00 |
| ev_strike | Physical (found paper) | Strike meeting minutes | Barnabas's threat was "we will take you to the labour office" |
| ev_accounts | Physical (found paper) | Partnership accounts | Profit shares paid to both partners in full every quarter |

**Forensics**

| Test | Sample | Lab hours | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hospital bloods | Victim | Immediate | Clotting severely impaired |
| Toxicology | Victim's blood | 18 h | **A long-acting anticoagulant rat poison** |
| Toxicology | `ev_honey` | 18 h | **The same poison**, at a high concentration. Under the magnifier: tiny **blue-green granules** in the honey, the dye used in rat-poison pellets |
| Toxicology | `ev_cecilia_jar` | 18 h | Clean |
| Toxicology | `ev_canteen` samples | 18 h | Clean |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cecilia Njiru | Cooperative, sympathetic | **"I've never bought rat poison in my life. We use traps at the mill."** / "I ate from the same honey myself." (true about her own jar) | First claim | `ev_records` | *"The mill has rats. I bought pellets for the store. That proves nothing."* |
| Barnabas Kimeli | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_strike`) | "I never went to his house." | True | — | Topic "strike": "We wanted fair pay. A dead boss doesn't pay anyone." |
| Allan Mukhwana | Cooperative | "I came home on Saturday evening." | True | — | Topic "debt": he'd asked his father for money; his father said yes |

**Proof**
1. `ev_hospital` + toxicology (victim) → Jacob was poisoned with a long-acting rat poison, taken in the days before Wednesday, so alibis on the day of death don't matter. *This is the first case where the time of the crime is days before the death.*
2. `ev_pamela` + `ev_honey` + toxicology (honey) → the poison was in the honey Cecilia gave him on Saturday, which only he ate; the blue-green granules are pellet dye.
3. Cecilia's claims + `ev_rebecca` + `ev_cecilia_jar` + `ev_records` → she bought two ordinary jars (hers is clean), and the day before the gift she bought four packs of rat poison, though she says she never has.
4. `ev_blacklist` + `ev_invoices` + `ev_jacob_letter` → Jacob was about to report her purchases of illegally felled timber → **WHO = Cecilia Njiru**, **HOW = long-acting rat poison mixed into a gift of honey**, **WHY = he was about to report her for buying timber felled illegally from a protected forest**.

**Eliminations**
- *WHO:* Barnabas Kimeli: never in the house (Pamela) and the canteen food is clean. Allan Mukhwana: `ev_bus` (he arrived after the honey was given, and doesn't eat honey: Pamela). Pamela Mukhwana: doesn't eat honey; she's the one who handed the jar over and pointed at Cecilia's card. Dr. Gedi: first saw Jacob Thursday.
- *HOW:*

| Method word | Refuted by |
|---|---|
| "poisoned in hospital" | `ev_hospital` (symptoms began before admission) |
| "a natural bleeding disorder" | Toxicology |
| "food poisoning from the sawmill canteen" | Canteen samples clean |
| "a fall causing internal bleeding" | No trauma (hospital notes) |
| ✔ "long-acting rat poison mixed into a gift of honey" | — |

- *WHY:*

| Motive word | Refuted by |
|---|---|
| "a dispute over profit shares" | `ev_accounts` |
| "the workers' strike" | Barnabas's cause; eliminated |
| "the son's debts" | Allan's; eliminated, and his father had agreed to help |
| "a dispute over the mill's land" | Title in Jacob's sole name, undisputed (title copy in the office) |
| ✔ "he was about to report her for buying timber felled illegally from a protected forest" | — |

**Red herrings / twist.** Red herring: the strike leader's public threat. Not counted as a twist: the slow poison is clear from the hospital notes at the start; the challenge is working backwards to Saturday.

**Charge sheet.** `{who} killed Jacob Mukhwana by {how}, because {why}.` WHO: Cecilia Njiru, Barnabas Kimeli, Allan Mukhwana, Pamela Mukhwana, Rebecca Lokwang (5).

**Clock plan.** No detention required. Hospital and Dr. Gedi (2 h), submit victim's blood (1 h), Pamela and the honey (2 h, submit 1 h), Cecilia and her jar (2 h, submit 1 h), Rebecca (2 h), records on Cecilia (4 h, 1 stamp), sawmill accounts and blacklist (2 h). Toxicology results arrive at hours 18–21; the player keeps investigating while they wait.

**Credibility path.** 1 stamp.

**New interface beat.** **The timeline before the timeline.** The notebook's time view stretches from hours to days for the first time; the player drags the window of poisoning back from Sunday's death to Saturday's gift. It prepares the WHEN group in region 5.

**Kenyan texture.** Baringo honey as a gift, sawmills on the forest edge, the published blacklists of illegal timber suppliers, agrovet shops, a business partnership signed on a handshake 20 years ago.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** asali (honey), msitu (forest), mbao (timber), sumu (poison), dawa ya panya (rat poison).

**Images (5).** Portraits: Jacob, Cecilia, Barnabas, Allan. Location: the Eldama Ravine sawmill yard with logs and a forest ridge behind. *(No image of the hospital patient.)*

**Audit tags.** Culprit F, 50s, Embu-origin name, motive cover-up. Victim M, 50s, Luhya-origin name.

### Case 40 — BOSS: Beacon BH9/14

`case-040` · Rift Valley · **boss** · 30 min · suspects 4 · **chain 5** · herrings 1 · liars **2** · groups WHO, WHY, HOW, **SPINE** · stamps needed 3 (records ×2, warrant) · **twist: the "robbery" is a copy of Joseph Mwenda's death**

**OB entry.** OB 04/29/11, 06:50. A milk transporter reports a man found dead on the roadside of the Bahati–Nakuru road; wallet and phone missing. **Recorded as robbery with violence.**

*(Twelve years ago, the OB entry for Joseph Mwenda read almost word for word the same. The game shows both entries side by side the moment the player opens this case's OB page, without comment.)*

**Setting.** Bahati, north-east of Nakuru town: green highland farms, red volcanic soil, hedges of cypress, survey beacons (iron pins set in concrete, painted red) marking plot corners. **Bahati Block 9**: land long farmed by old families, now being sold as 60 new plots by fictional **Bahati Highlands Land Ltd**. The fictional **Nakuru Survey Records Office** holds old field books and maps, some on microfilm.

**Victim.** **Titus Kibiwott**, 56, licensed land surveyor for 30 years.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Calvin Wamalwa | 44 | Suspect | Director, Bahati Highlands Land Ltd | **Culprit** (liar 1) |
| Elias Kipkoech | 38 | Suspect | Calvin's driver | Present, not the killer; **liar 2** |
| Simon Gacheru | 49 | Suspect | Farmer; threatened Titus at Bahati market last week over a fence Titus had moved on another job | Innocent (red herring): at a dowry negotiation |
| Nicholas Kemboi | 50 | Suspect | Rival surveyor; hired first by Bahati Highlands, then dropped | Innocent: with a client |
| Priscilla Kibiwott | 53 | Witness | Titus's widow | Innocent |
| Hannah Chesang | 35 | Witness | Clerk, Nakuru Survey Records Office | Innocent |
| Wesley Koros | 40 | Witness | Milk transporter who found him | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Bahati Highlands hired Titus to "re-establish" the plot boundaries of Block 9 according to an amended survey map registered eleven years ago. Titus compared that amendment with the **original survey of Block 9**, done twelve years ago by **Joseph Mwenda**, field book **FB 4471**. The original field book had been "withdrawn by the registry" and was missing, but Titus found it on the records office's old microfilm. The amendment had moved the beacons to carve 60 plots out of the old families' land. Titus refused to sign the re-establishment certificate and told his wife, "Mwenda was right." On Friday at 18:20 he went to beacon **BH9/14** to photograph the moved beacon. Calvin and his driver Elias met him there. Calvin pulled the beacon bar out of the ground and struck him with it. They laid him in the bed of Calvin's double-cab pickup and drove 7 km to the Bahati road, where they left him on the verge, took his wallet and phone to look like a robbery, and threw them, with the beacon bar, into a flooded quarry. It is exactly how Joseph Mwenda was found twelve years ago.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_ob_pair | Physical (found paper) | OB, today, beside Joseph's old OB from the drawer | Two near-identical entries: surveyor, roadside, Bahati road, wallet and phone gone, "robbery with violence" |
| ev_priscilla | Witness | Widow | Titus refused to sign the Block 9 re-establishment. On Thursday night he kept saying "Mwenda was right. They moved Mwenda's beacons." On Friday at 18:00 he said he was going to "photograph fourteen" and would be back for supper **(probable cause for records on Titus's line; spine link)** |
| ev_titus_car | Physical | His car, parked at the edge of Block 9 | In the glovebox: a **photocopy from microfilm of field book FB 4471**, Bahati Block 9, surveyed by **J. Mwenda**, with the original beacon positions; and the amended map with Titus's pencil arrows showing each moved beacon |
| ev_hannah | Witness + physical | Records clerk | The original FB 4471 is listed as **"withdrawn — Registry — 11 years ago"** and has never come back. Titus spent two days last week at the microfilm reader |
| ev_beacon_hole | Physical | Beacon BH9/14 | The beacon pulled out of the ground, the hole fresh, red-painted concrete crumbs around it. Titus's camera lens cap in the grass |
| ev_records_titus | **Records request** (victim's line) | Jamii Mobile | Mast **Bahati North (Block 9)** 18:20–19:10, then **Bahati Road** 19:25, then off |
| ev_contract | Physical (found paper) | Titus's office | Contract with Bahati Highlands Land Ltd; deposit paid by PesaPap from **BAHATI HIGHLANDS LAND LTD**, signed for by **C. Wamalwa**; Titus's handwritten note: "Will not sign. Amendment is false." |
| ev_records_calvin | **Records request** (Calvin's line; probable cause: `ev_contract` + `ev_priscilla`) | Jamii Mobile + PesaPap | Mast **Bahati North 18:10–19:12**, **Bahati Road 19:25**, Nakuru town from 19:50. PesaPap: monthly receipts from **"MVUA HOLDINGS LTD"** |
| ev_vehicle | Physical, **warrant** | Calvin's double-cab pickup | A ribbed load-bed liner, **ribs 4 cm apart**, washed but with traces in the grooves; red-painted concrete crumbs in the corner |
| ev_ruracio | Witness | Elders at a dowry negotiation in Subukia (statement only) | Simon Gacheru negotiated for his nephew from 16:00 to 22:00 in front of twenty people |
| ev_kemboi | Physical (found paper) | Client's receipt | Nicholas Kemboi at a client's farm in Rongai 17:00–20:30, with the client |
| ev_quarry | Physical | Flooded quarry at Kiamaina (located from Elias's reveal) | The **beacon bar**, red concrete still attached, Titus's wallet and phone |

**Forensics**

| Test | Sample | Lab hours | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Autopsy | Body | Immediate | Struck by a **cylindrical iron bar about 2.5 cm across**, with fragments of **concrete and red paint** in the wounds. Time of death **18:30–20:00**. **Lividity is fixed on his right side in parallel stripes about 4 cm apart**: he lay on his side on a ribbed surface for over an hour after death, and was then moved onto his back on the verge |
| Soil | Clothes vs roadside vs Block 9 | 8 h | His clothes carry **red volcanic soil and red paint flecks from Block 9**; the roadside where he was found is grey murram |
| Trace | `ev_vehicle` bed grooves | 12 h | Human blood; red survey paint |
| Comparison | `ev_quarry` bar vs wounds | Immediate once found | Match |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Calvin Wamalwa | Cooperative, smooth | **"I was in Nairobi from Friday morning until Sunday."** / "Titus was paid well. I'm sorry for his family." | First claim (liar 1) | `ev_records_calvin` | *"I came back early. I drove past the farm. I didn't see him."* (then silence until `ev_vehicle` and the quarry) |
| Elias Kipkoech | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_records_calvin`) | **"I drove Mr Calvin to Nairobi on Friday afternoon. We stayed until Sunday."** | Yes (liar 2) | `ev_records_calvin` (Calvin's phone was in Bahati, and Elias drives him everywhere) | *"We were at the farm. Mr Calvin hit him with the beacon. I only drove. I helped lift him. I've not slept. The bar is in the quarry at Kiamaina, with the wallet."* (new location: `ev_quarry`) |
| Simon Gacheru | Cooperative, angry | "I was at my nephew's ruracio." | True | — | Topic "fence": "I shouted at him. He was right about my fence and I was wrong." |
| Nicholas Kemboi | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_contract`) | "I was with a client in Rongai." | True | — | Topic "Bahati Highlands": *"They dropped me because I asked for more money to sign. Titus wouldn't sign for any money. That's the difference between us."* |

**Proof**
1. `ev_ob_pair` + autopsy + soil → the roadside isn't where Titus died: Block 9 soil and paint are on his clothes; striped lividity shows he lay on a ribbed surface for over an hour before being moved. The robbery is staged. **(Twist.)**
2. `ev_priscilla` + `ev_titus_car` + `ev_contract` + `ev_hannah` → Titus refused to sign a re-survey that moved the beacons of Joseph Mwenda's original survey; he went to beacon 14 on Friday evening to photograph it.
3. `ev_records_titus` + `ev_records_calvin` + Calvin's broken claim → both phones were at Block 9 18:20–19:10 and on the Bahati road at 19:25. Calvin wasn't in Nairobi.
4. `ev_vehicle` (warrant) + trace → Calvin's pickup bed has ribs 4 cm apart, blood and survey paint in its grooves.
5. Elias's broken claim + `ev_quarry` → the driver confirms it, and the beacon bar is recovered with the wallet → **WHO = Calvin Wamalwa**, **HOW = struck with a survey beacon bar at the farm, then moved to the roadside**, **WHY = Titus refused to sign a re-survey that would make the forged plots legal**.

Hannah Chesang: at the records office until 17:00, then on the Nakuru bus (ticket). Wesley Koros: collecting milk from 05:30, found Titus at 06:40.

| "fell into the roadside ditch" | Autopsy |

- Red herring: the farmer who threatened Titus at the market.
- **Twist:** a twelve-year-old crime repeated in the same place, the same way, for the same land. The player has been reading Joseph's file since the prologue.

**Charge sheet.** Four groups:

> **WHO / HOW / WHY:** `{who} killed Titus Kibiwott by {how}, because {why}.`
> **SPINE:** `The survey Titus refused to falsify was first made, twelve years ago, by {pin}.`

- WHO: Calvin Wamalwa, Elias Kipkoech, Simon Gacheru, Nicholas Kemboi, Hannah Chesang (5).
- SPINE (Pattern File pins): *Joseph Mwenda — the closed file in the drawer* ✔, *Rashid Omar Bakari — River Road (case 10)*, *Naomi Chepkemoi — Shimanzi (case 30)*, *Hezekiah Onsongo — Ziwani Gardens (case 33)*, *Daniel Gichuru — Pwani Clearing (case 30)* (5).

- **Joseph's evidence box** is released from the Nakuru evidence store, unopened for twelve years: his surveying compass, a pencil, a photograph of a younger Amani on his shoulders at a beacon, and a carbon copy of his own field-book summary for Block 9. The **closing officer's name on Joseph's file has been cut out** of the copy in the box with a blade, neatly.

- **Collectible:** **Joseph Mwenda's surveying compass.** It sits on the desk from now on, next to the dhow compass from Lamu, pointing a slightly different north.

**Clock plan.** OB pair and autopsy (0 h), widow (2 h), Titus's car (1 h), records office and Hannah (2 h), records on Titus (4 h, 1 stamp), contract (1 h), records on Calvin (4 h, 1 stamp), soil to the lab (1 h; back at 8 h), warrant on the pickup (3 h, 1 stamp; trace back 12 h later). **Detain Calvin** once the pickup is searched (hour ~18 of the case). Within his 24 hours: interview Elias (2 h) → quarry (3 h) → bar comparison → trace result → press Calvin. About 17 h of the detention used without any rush. Validator rule 16 passes.

**Kenyan texture.** Bahati's highland farms and red soil, survey beacons and field books, land companies subdividing old family land, records offices and microfilm readers, dowry negotiations (ruracio) as an alibi, "robbery with violence" as the easiest OB entry to write.

Evidence photos: the microfilm photocopy of FB 4471 with "J. ## Open questions for the cultural reader (region 4)

1. **Case 34:** does the depiction of pastoralist herders, the ranch and the radio's prejudice land as intended (the herders exonerated with dignity), or does any detail still lean on a stereotype? Is "ole Sopia" a plausible name?
2. **Case 31:** is "planting before the valuation cut-off" well known enough to feel real to Kenyan players?
3. **Case 36:** the extended-bag fight in Molo: are the bag weights, county enforcement and co-op roles accurate today?
4. **Case 38:** lactometer reading ranges and how graders really reject milk at collection centres.
5. **Case 40:** survey beacons, field books, microfilm at survey records offices, and "re-establishment" of boundaries: is the procedure plausible to a Kenyan surveyor? A professional surveyor's read is worth paying for here.
6. **Kenyan-European characters (case 34):** naming, ranch inheritance and conservancy trusts: plausible and fair?
7. Forensic realism across the region: Kenyan pathologist practice, county forensic lab capabilities, how long tests take, the 24-hour rule in practice.
8. Name-origin tags for all region-4 names, especially Nandi vs Kipsigis and Teso.

## Part F — Region 5: Kisumu & Lake Victoria (cases 41–50)

**Region frame.** December into January: the end of the short rains, Christmas and New Year, families going home to the villages. Amani is posted to Kisumu. The lake is the region: fish landings at dawn, omena drying on nets, water hyacinth choking the bays, islands reached by ferry, beach management units with their levy books. Dr. Chebii has been seconded to the regional lab in Kisumu for the season, so the pathologist's voice stays the same; Eric's results come by courier from Nakuru with the same lab hours. Mwalimu calls twice in this region, unprompted, both times late at night. Both times she asks about the weather and hangs up.

### F1. Region 5 rules

- **The WHEN group arrives (case 41).** Charge sheets read `On {when}, {who} killed X by {how}, because {why}.`
  - **Cases 41–42:** WHEN is a single blank: a time window chosen from at least 5.
  - **From case 43:** WHEN becomes a **timeline strip**: 3 to 5 events the player drags into order onto a clock strip, each into a time slot. Graded as one group. With 3 events and 4 slots the combinations are well above the 12 that rule 9 asks for.
- **The timeline rail (case 41).** Along the bottom of the corkboard, ungraded, like the rest of the board. Any fact with a time can be pinned to it. This is the player's thinking space; the strip on the charge sheet is the graded answer.
- **Time sources** become a craft: landing levy books, market fee receipts, radio schedules, dose memories in medical pens, DJ playlists, the phase of the moon. Every case teaches one new kind of clock.
- **Liars: 1–2 per case. Herrings: 1–2.** Twists: 4 (cases 43, 46, 48, 50).
- **Region casting rule.** The lake is mostly Luo and Suba country, and most victims, witnesses and helpers here are Luo or Suba. To keep §A5 honest, **no more than 2 culprits in the region have Luo-origin names** (cases 43 and 47), and the region's helpers (a beach chairman, a radio listener, a fisheries clerk, a ferry clerk, a journalist) are written as the people who solve things, not the people who cause them.

### Case 41 — The Levy Book

`case-041` · Lake Victoria · 22 min · suspects 4 · chain 3 · herrings 1 · liars 1 (culprit) · groups WHEN, WHO, HOW, WHY · stamps needed 1 (records)

**OB entry.** OB 08/08/12, 08:20 (Monday 8 December). The chairman of Dunga Beach Management Unit reports the BMU treasurer found dead behind the BMU office among the stored boat engines.

**Setting.** Dunga beach, just south of Kisumu city: wooden canoes pulled up on the sand, omena spread to dry on nets, hyacinth in the shallows, a papyrus fringe. The fictional **Dunga BMU** office: a desk, a levy book where every landing is written down (time, boat number, catch, levy paid), and a locked store where outboard engines are chained at night against theft.

**Victim.** **Phoebe Awuor**, 44, BMU treasurer. Struck with a boat propeller.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Geoffrey Ombui | 36 | Suspect | Outboard-engine mechanic with a workshop in town | **Culprit** |
| Dismas Ojwang | 52 | Suspect | BMU chairman; quarrelled with Phoebe last week about a levy shortfall | Innocent (red herring): at the county fisheries office |
| Elisha Amollo | 40 | Suspect | Boat owner who bought a "reconditioned" engine from Geoffrey | Innocent: out on the lake |
| Benta Ayieko | 58 | Witness | Chai seller at the landing | Innocent |
| Seline Awuor | 39 | Witness | Phoebe's sister, also a fish trader | Innocent |
| Fanuel Opiyo | 27 | Witness (statement only) | Boda rider at Dunga | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Engine theft is a plague on the lake: outboards stolen at night from moored boats, repainted and sold on. Geoffrey ran such a ring. Last week Elisha bought a "reconditioned" 15-horsepower engine from him and brought it to the BMU to register. Phoebe checked its serial number against the BMU's stolen-engine register: it was an engine reported stolen from Usenge in October. She told Geoffrey on Sunday that she'd take it to the beach police post when it opened at 08:00 on Monday. At 07:10 he came to the BMU office to talk her out of it. At about 07:15 he hit her with a spare propeller from his tool bag, threw the propeller into the shallows and left on a boda at 07:27.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Behind the office | Struck with a heavy blade-edged object |
| ev_levybook | Physical (found paper) | BMU desk | Landings logged in Phoebe's hand: 06:10, 06:25, 06:40, **06:52 (last entry)**. Boat **KSM-2214 landed at 07:30** (crew statement) but isn't in the book |
| ev_benta | Witness | Chai seller | Sold Phoebe her morning chai at **07:05**; "she was worried, she said a mechanic was coming" |
| ev_crew | Witness | Crew of KSM-2214 (statement only) | Landed at 07:30. Phoebe always meets every landing at the water with her book; this time she didn't come; the office door was pulled shut |
| ev_seline | Witness | Sister | Phoebe always spreads her own omena on the drying net by 07:00. Seline found her basket still full and wet at 08:00 |
| ev_register | Physical (found paper) | BMU office | Stolen-engine register: **serial 6Y4-…-1187**, stolen from a boat at Usenge, 14 October. Phoebe's pencil note beside it: "Elisha's new engine — same number! Geoffrey Ombui sold it. Police post Monday 8am." |
| ev_engine | Physical | BMU store | Elisha's "reconditioned" engine: fresh paint, serial **6Y4-…-1187** |
| ev_propeller | Physical | Shallows near the office (found by divers from the BMU) | A three-blade aluminium propeller, scratched **"G.O."** on the hub, the way Geoffrey marks his workshop stock |
| ev_records | **Records request** (Geoffrey's line; probable cause: `ev_register` + `ev_benta`) | Jamii Mobile + PesaPap | Mast **Dunga 07:02–07:29**; Kisumu CBD from 07:45. **PesaPap 07:27: KSh 150 to FANUEL OPIYO** |
| ev_fanuel | Witness | Boda rider | Picked up "the mechanic" outside the BMU at 07:27; he was carrying a tool bag and "wet to the knees" |
| ev_fisheries | Physical (found paper) | County fisheries office | Meeting sign-in: D. Ojwang 06:55; meeting 07:00–09:30 |
| ev_elisha | Physical (found paper) + witness | BMU landing record of the afternoon before | Elisha's boat left at 04:00, landed 08:15 with his crew of three |
| ev_levyshortfall | Physical (found paper) | BMU office | The shortfall Dismas complained about: a counting error found and corrected on Saturday, both signatures |

**Forensics**

| Test | Sample | Lab hours | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Autopsy | Body | Immediate | Two curved, blade-edged wounds, spacing consistent with a boat propeller. No water in the lungs. Time of death **06:45–08:00** |
| Comparison | Wounds vs `ev_propeller` | Immediate | Blade curvature and spacing match |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Geoffrey Ombui | Cooperative | **"I was at my workshop in town from half past six."** / "That engine was reconditioned from scrap. I have papers." | First claim | `ev_records` or `ev_fanuel` | *"I went to Dunga to explain the papers. She wouldn't listen. I left her at her desk."* |
| Dismas Ojwang | Cooperative | "I was at the fisheries office by seven." | True | — | Shows `ev_levyshortfall`: "We fought about numbers. The numbers were wrong. Mine, not hers." |
| Elisha Amollo | Guarded (talks when shown `ev_engine`) | "I was on the lake." | True | — | *"I paid him 180,000 for that engine. I didn't know."* |

**WHEN (single window).** Options: *05:30–06:15*, *06:15–07:00*, ✔ ***07:05–07:30***, *07:30–08:00*, *08:00–08:30*.
- Not before 07:05: `ev_benta` (alive buying chai).
- Not after 07:30: `ev_crew` (she didn't meet KSM-2214, the first landing she ever missed) + `ev_levybook`.
- `ev_seline` supports (omena never spread by 07:00).

**Proof**
1. `ev_benta` + `ev_crew` + `ev_levybook` → she died between 07:05 and 07:30 (**WHEN**).
2. `ev_register` + `ev_engine` → the engine Geoffrey sold is a stolen one, and Phoebe was taking it to the police at 08:00.
3. `ev_records` + `ev_fanuel` + Geoffrey's broken claim + `ev_propeller` → he was at Dunga 07:02–07:29, left wet to the knees at 07:27, and the propeller in the shallows carries his workshop mark → **WHO = Geoffrey Ombui**, **HOW = struck with a boat propeller**, **WHY = she'd matched the engine he was selling to a stolen-engine report**.

**Eliminations**
- *WHO:* Dismas Ojwang: `ev_fisheries`. Elisha Amollo: `ev_elisha`. Benta Ayieko: at her chai stall serving the landing crowd. Seline Awuor: at the Kisumu fish market from 06:00 (her stall receipts).
- *HOW:*

| Method word | Refuted by |
|---|---|
| "drowned" | Autopsy (no water in lungs) |
| "crushed by an engine falling from the store rack" | The rack is intact, every engine still chained (scene) + wound shape |
| "struck with a wooden paddle" | Wound edges blade-sharp; no splinters |
| "a heart attack" | Autopsy |
| ✔ "struck with a boat propeller" | — |

- *WHY:*

| Motive word | Refuted by |
|---|---|
| "the levy shortfall" | `ev_levyshortfall` (and that was Dismas's quarrel) |
| "an unpaid repair bill" | BMU paid Geoffrey's last invoice in full (receipt) |
| "a quarrel over landing space" | Geoffrey doesn't own a boat |
| "a fight about Elisha's engine price" | Elisha's grievance, not Geoffrey's |
| ✔ "she'd matched the engine he was selling to a stolen-engine report" | — |

**Red herrings / twist.** Red herring: the chairman's levy quarrel.

**Charge sheet.** `On {when}, {who} killed Phoebe Awuor by {how}, because {why}.` WHO: Geoffrey Ombui, Dismas Ojwang, Elisha Amollo, Benta Ayieko, Seline Awuor (5).

**Clock plan.** No detention required. Levy book (1 h), Benta (2 h), crew (1 h), Seline (2 h), register and engine (2 h), records on Geoffrey (4 h, 1 stamp), boda rider (2 h), divers find the propeller (2 h).

**Credibility path.** 1 stamp.

**New interface beat.** **The WHEN blank and the timeline rail.** The rail slides out from under the corkboard; Benta's 07:05 and the crew's 07:30 snap onto it and the window shades in between them. Mwalimu: *"Every fact has a time. Line them up and the gap will tell you."*

**Kenyan texture.** Beach management units and landing levies, omena drying on nets, outboard-engine theft and serial-number registers, chai at the landing, papyrus and hyacinth.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** omena (small silver fish, dried), BMU (beach management unit), injini (engine), chai.

**Images (6).** Portraits: Phoebe, Geoffrey, Dismas, Elisha. Location: Dunga beach at dawn, canoes and omena nets. Evidence photo: the propeller with "G.O." on the hub.
