### Case 79 — Empty Slot

`case-079` · Northern frontier · 42 min · suspects 5 · **chain 6** · herrings 2 · liars **3** · groups WHEN, WHERE, WHO, HOW, WHY, ABSENCE · stamps needed 2 (records, warrant)

**OB entry.** OB 02/31/07, 07:15 (Friday 31 July). The morning shift reports a nurse found dead on the floor of the laboratory annex at Moyale sub-county hospital. **Suspected fall on a wet floor.**

**Setting.** Moyale, the border town where Kenya meets Ethiopia: a busy crossing, lorries queuing for customs, Ethiopian coffee and injera in the cafés, Borana, Gabra, Burji, Garre and Somali traders. The sub-county hospital is small: one lab annex with a fridge where samples wait for the morning vehicle to the Marsabit lab, each in a numbered rack slot and logged in a **chain-of-custody book**.

**Map.** Hospital ↔ the crash site on the Moyale–Marsabit road: 3 km · Hospital ↔ Mahat's house: 2 km · Hospital ↔ police station: 1 km.

**Victim.** **Kavata Mutua**, 30, nurse; on night duty in casualty and responsible for the lab fridge overnight.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mahat Dekow | 34 | Suspect | Transporter; elder brother of the driver in last night's fatal crash | **Culprit** (liar 1) |
| Yusuf Dekow | 24 | Suspect | His younger brother; drove into a pedestrian at 01:30 and was brought in injured | Innocent of the killing; **liar 2** (says he wasn't drinking) |
| Adano Sharamo | 49 | Suspect | Hospital night watchman | Innocent; **liar 3** (took a bribe to let Mahat into the annex) |
| Fatma Hassan | 36 | Suspect | Clinical officer; argued with Kavata last week over night rotas | Innocent (red herring 1) |
| Cpl. Daniel Musyoka | 33 | Suspect | Kavata's ex-boyfriend, a soldier posted at Moyale; she'd ended it a month ago | Innocent (red herring 2) |
| Cpl. Ali Galgallo | 40 | Witness | Traffic officer who brought Yusuf in | Innocent |

**What really happened.** At 01:30 Yusuf, drunk, drove the family pickup into **Mzee Bonsa Tura**, a 64-year-old man walking home from night prayers, killing him, then hit a pole. Cpl. Galgallo brought Yusuf to casualty at 02:00 and asked for a blood-alcohol sample. Kavata took it at 02:10, sealed it, labelled it, logged it in the chain-of-custody book and put it in **rack slot B4** in the lab fridge for the 06:00 vehicle to Marsabit. Mahat arrived at 02:40. At 03:00 he offered Kavata KSh 100,000 to "lose" the sample. She refused and told him it would be in Marsabit by noon. At 03:20 he called the watchman, Adano, and sent him KSh 5,000 to unlock the lab annex's side door for "a family matter". At about 03:40, as Kavata checked the fridge, Mahat came in. He tried to take the sample; she held on to the rack; he hit her with the steel fire extinguisher from the corridor wall. He took the tube from slot B4, tore off its label, poured water on the floor around her to make it a slip, and left by the side door at 03:50.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Lab annex floor | Head injury; water pooled around her |
| ev_slot | Physical | Lab fridge | Rack B: **slot B4 empty**. Every other logged sample in its slot *(Expected: the custody book)* |
| ev_custody | Physical (found paper) | Chain-of-custody book | **02:10 — Y. Dekow — blood (alcohol) — police request Cpl. Galgallo — B4 — K. Mutua.** No signature for removal |
| ev_galgallo | Witness | Traffic officer | "I asked for the sample. The nurse took it in front of me. The brother arrived at about twenty to three and was asking everyone where it goes." |
| ev_floor | Physical | Lab annex | The water on the floor is **clean tap water**, not from any spill: the annex has no sink or mop bucket, and the jerrycan from the corridor is **empty**, its cap off *(Expected: a floor gets wet from something)* |
| ev_extinguisher | Physical | Corridor | The fire extinguisher's **wall bracket is empty**; the extinguisher stands in a corner of the annex, its base **wiped** |
| ev_side_door | Physical | Annex side door | Unlocked from outside with the watchman's key (lock shows no damage) |
| ev_records | **Records request** (Mahat's line; probable cause: `ev_slot` + `ev_galgallo`) | Jamii Mobile + PesaPap | The Moyale mast covers the whole town (location useless). **03:20 call to Adano Sharamo; 03:25 PesaPap KSh 5,000 to Adano** |
| ev_car | Physical, **warrant** (probable cause: `ev_records` + Adano's reveal) | Mahat's car | Under the driver's seat, a torn **sample label**: *"B4 — Y. Dekow — 02:10"*; fragments of a plastic tube in the footwell; drops of blood on the floor mat |
| ev_yusuf_bar | Physical (found paper) | A Moyale bar | Yusuf's tab: 21:00–01:15, eleven beers |
| ev_fatma | Physical (found paper) | Rota and ward book | Fatma off duty, at home (her husband and children); she was called in at 07:30 |
| ev_daniel | Physical (found paper) | Army camp gate log | Cpl. Musyoka inside camp all night; gate log, no exit |

**Forensics**

| Test | Sample | Lab hours | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Post-mortem (Dr. Chebii, Marsabit) | Body | Immediate (Marsabit, 3.5 h) | One heavy blow from a curved metal base, not a fall against the bench edge (the bench edge is square). Time of death **03:30–04:30** |
| Blood | Extinguisher base seam; car floor mat | 6 + 4 h | Kavata's |
| Fingerprints | Extinguisher handle (partial under the trigger) vs Mahat (**refuses → detention**) | 6 + 4 h | Match |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mahat Dekow | Cooperative, controlled | **"I sat with my brother in casualty until morning. I never went near the lab."** | Yes (liar 1) | `ev_records` + Adano's reveal + `ev_car` | *"My brother made one mistake. That sample was ten years of his life. I asked her nicely first."* |
| Yusuf Dekow | Guarded, in pain | **"I hadn't been drinking. The old man walked into the road."** | Yes (liar 2) | `ev_yusuf_bar` + `ev_galgallo` | *"I was drunk. I killed Mzee Bonsa. My brother kept saying 'I'll fix it.' I was asleep from four with the drip."* |
| Adano Sharamo | Guarded, frightened | **"I patrolled. Nobody went into the annex."** | Yes (liar 3) | `ev_records` (the KSh 5,000) | *"Mahat called and sent five thousand. He said a family matter, his brother's papers. I opened the side door at twenty to four and went to the gate. I didn't know."* |
| Fatma Hassan | Cooperative | "We argued about rotas. I was at home." | True | — | Shows `ev_fatma` |
| Cpl. Daniel Musyoka | Guarded | "We were finished. I was in camp." | True | — | Shows `ev_daniel` |

**ABSENCE.** Missing: ✔ ***slot B4 is empty and the custody book has no removal signature***, *there's no sink or mop for the water on the floor*, *the extinguisher is missing from its bracket*, *the side door wasn't forced*, *there's no sample on the morning vehicle's list*. Conclusions: ✔ ***someone took Yusuf's sample without signing for it***, *the sample went to Marsabit early*, *the nurse slipped on a wet floor*, *a stranger broke in*, *the sample was never taken*, *the clinical officer moved it*.
*(Accepted alternative under rule 18: "there's no sample on the morning vehicle's list", same conclusion.)*

**WHEN (strip).** *Yusuf hits Mzee Bonsa* (01:30) · *Kavata takes the sample* (02:10) · *Mahat offers the bribe* (03:00) · *Mahat pays the watchman* (03:25) · *Kavata is killed* (about 03:40). Decoy: 05:00 ("slipped near the end of her shift").

**WHERE.** ✔ *the lab annex*, *casualty*, *the hospital corridor*, *the crash site*, *Mahat's car*.

**Proof**
1. `ev_custody` + `ev_galgallo` + `ev_slot` → Yusuf's alcohol sample was taken, logged in B4, and removed without a signature. **(ABSENCE.)**
2. `ev_floor` + `ev_extinguisher` + post-mortem → not a slip: the floor was wetted on purpose, and she was struck with the extinguisher.
3. `ev_records` + Adano's reveal + `ev_side_door` → Mahat paid to be let into the annex at 03:40.
4. Yusuf's reveal + `ev_yusuf_bar` → the sample would have convicted his brother.
5. `ev_car` (warrant) + blood + fingerprints → **WHO = Mahat Dekow**, **HOW = struck with the lab corridor's fire extinguisher**, **WHY = to destroy his brother's blood-alcohol sample after a fatal crash**, **WHERE = the lab annex**.

**Eliminations**
- *WHO:* Yusuf: on a drip in casualty from 03:00, asleep (the other night nurse's observation chart every 30 minutes). Adano: at the gate from 03:42 (gate book, a lorry driver he let in). Fatma: `ev_fatma`. Cpl. Musyoka: `ev_daniel`. Cpl. Galgallo: at the crash site with the body until 05:00.
- *HOW:* "slipped on a wet floor and hit the bench" (bench edge square; wound curved; the water is staged); "struck with a stool" (stools are light plastic); "a seizure and a fall" (post-mortem); "strangled" (post-mortem).
- *WHY:* "a rota quarrel" (Fatma's; eliminated); "an ex-boyfriend's jealousy" (Musyoka's; eliminated); "a bribed watchman covering a theft" (Adano opened a door; he wasn't in the annex); "theft of hospital drugs" (the drugs cupboard locked and full).

**Red herrings / twist.** Herrings: the clinical officer she argued with and the ex-boyfriend soldier. No twist.

**Charge sheet.** Full sheet + ABSENCE. WHO: Mahat Dekow, Yusuf Dekow, Adano Sharamo, Fatma Hassan, Daniel Musyoka, Ali Galgallo (6).

**Clock plan.** Annex (1 h), fridge and custody book (1 h), Galgallo (1 h), floor and extinguisher (30 min), Yusuf (1 h), records (4 h, 1 stamp), Adano (1 h), warrant on the car (3 h, 1 stamp). **Detain Mahat**; blood and prints 10 h each. Post-mortem in Marsabit runs in parallel. Rule 16 passes.

**Credibility path.** 2 stamps.

**New interface beat.** **The rack.** The fridge view shows the rack as a grid of slots with tube icons; the custody book sits beside it. Dragging each book line onto its slot fills the grid. B4 stays empty, and the empty square pulses once.

**Kenyan texture.** Moyale's border crossing and customs queues, Ethiopian coffee, sub-county hospitals with one lab fridge, chain-of-custody books, the morning vehicle to Marsabit, blood-alcohol samples on a traffic officer's request, night watchmen and their gate books, soldiers posted on the border.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** sampuli (sample), friji (fridge), mlinzi (watchman), hongo (bribe), kizima moto (fire extinguisher), mpaka (border).

**Images (6).** Portraits: Kavata (nurse's uniform), Mahat, Yusuf, Adano, Fatma. Location: a small hospital lab annex at night, a fridge glowing, one empty slot.

**Audit tags.** Culprit M, 30s, Somali-origin name, motive protecting someone. Victim F, 30s, Kamba-origin name.

### Case 80 — BOSS: Drawer 14

`case-080` · Northern frontier · **boss** · 48 min · suspects 6 · **chain 7** · herrings 2 · liars 3 · lawyered: 1 · groups WHEN (strip), **WHERE (two blanks)**, WHO, HOW, WHY, FORGERY, ABSENCE, **SPINE** · stamps needed 3 (records ×2, warrant) · **twist: the registry man; and what's in his drawer**

**OB entry.** OB 09/08/08, 09:10 (Saturday 8 August). A family in Isiolo reports their daughter missing since Friday evening: **Abdia Golicha**, records clerk at the Isiolo county land registry. She never came home from work.

**Setting.** The **Isiolo county land registry**, a single-storey government building with a records room of steel cabinets and shelves of buff file folders, and a back room converted three months ago into the **"digitisation room"** for a team from Nairobi: two scanners, a laptop with a scan log, archive boxes, and one locked steel cabinet whose drawers the team keeps the keys to. Every file that leaves the building is supposed to go out with a **dispatch note** and a line in the **dispatch book**. Every scan gets a **sequence number** in the scan log. A guard keeps a **sign-out book** at the door after 17:00.

**Map.** Registry ↔ Abdia's family home: 2 km · Registry ↔ the murram pit on the Garba Tula road: 32 km (40 min) · Registry ↔ the team's guesthouse: 1 km.

**Victim.** **Abdia Golicha**, 32, records clerk at the Isiolo county land registry for nine years. (Her letter to Ubah Osman was found in case 77.)

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Julius Emojong | 54 | Suspect | Senior records officer, Ministry of Lands, Nairobi; leader of the "digitisation team" touring northern registries | **Culprit** (liar 1); **lawyered** (Advocate Sharon Kiprop, Nairobi). **The registry man** |
| Hassan Guracha | 57 | Suspect | County land registrar, Isiolo; Abdia's boss | Innocent of the killing; **liar 2** (says every file left with a dispatch note; he signed blank dispatch forms for the team) |
| Omar Hiribae | 41 | Suspect | Driver of the team's project vehicle | Innocent of the killing; **liar 3** (says the vehicle was parked all weekend; he lent Emojong the key for KSh 10,000) |
| Jattani Halkano | 34 | Suspect | Abdia's fiancé; their families were arguing over the wedding | Innocent (red herring 1) |
| Kennedy Mulwa | 44 | Suspect | Waso Range's former liaison officer (case 74), visited the registry on Friday afternoon | Innocent (red herring 2): came to hand Abdia a copy of the false minutes for the police file |
| Florence Atieno | 29 | Suspect | Scanner operator on the digitisation team | Innocent |
| Galma Shune | 60 | Witness | Registry night guard | Innocent |

**What really happened.** For eleven years Julius Emojong has been the man at the national lands registry who makes files disappear: a file "withdrawn" for "review", "digitisation" or "verification" never comes back, and a forged replacement can take its place. Eleven years ago he withdrew Joseph Mwenda's official field book, **FB 4471** (case 40). Twelve years ago, after Joseph's death, someone gave him something else to destroy: **Joseph's own working field book**, taken from his body on the Bahati road. He didn't destroy it. He kept it, locked in whatever drawer he was working from, as insurance. This year he was sent north with a "digitisation team" to clean the community-land records that stood in the way of Mvua-funded leases (the Garba Tula file, case 74, was one). He scanned the files, deleted the scans from the log, and locked the paper files in **drawer 14** of the team's cabinet to take back to Nairobi. Abdia noticed. She started a **shadow list** in a green notebook: every file she handed to the team, and whether it came back. Thirty-seven didn't. On Friday afternoon she stayed late, found drawer 14's key in the scanner tray where Emojong had left it, and opened the drawer. At about 18:30 Emojong came back for his key and found her photographing the files with her phone. He hit her with the heavy steel two-hole binding punch from the scanning table. He switched off her phone, locked her green notebook in drawer 14, and waited for the building to empty. At 19:55 he signed out at the guard's book with "project vehicle — archive boxes", carried her out in an archive box trolley to the vehicle (whose key he'd got from Omar), drove 32 km out on the Garba Tula road, and left her in an abandoned murram pit. He was back at the guesthouse at 21:30.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_missing | Witness | Abdia's mother and the tuk-tuk driver | The driver waited at the registry gate from 17:30 to 18:15, as every evening; **she never came out**. Her mother: "She said on Thursday, 'I've found something at work. I'm writing it down.'" |
| ev_signout | Physical (found paper) | Guard's sign-out book | Friday after 17:00: Florence 17:20, Registrar Guracha 17:45, **Emojong 19:55 "project vehicle — archive boxes"**. **No sign-out for Abdia** *(Expected: every staff member signs out after 17:00; Galma)* |
| ev_galma | Witness | Night guard | "Mr. Emojong pushed out a trolley with a big archive box at five to eight. He said it was going to Nairobi. Abdia? I thought she'd gone at five with the others. I don't check the book for faces, only names." |
| ev_phone | **Records request ①** (Abdia's line; probable cause: `ev_missing` + `ev_signout`) | Jamii Mobile | Her phone on the Isiolo mast until **18:41**, then **off**. It never moved |
| ev_scanlog | Physical | Digitisation laptop (Florence unlocks it) | Scan log sequence 0001–4,812. **37 sequence numbers missing** in the middle of runs *(Expected: the software numbers scans consecutively; Florence)* |
| ev_index | Physical (found paper) | Registry index cards | 37 files on the index cards **absent from the shelves**; the dispatch book has **no entry** for any of them leaving |
| ev_dispatch | Physical (found paper) | Registrar's tray | A pad of dispatch notes, **pre-signed by Registrar Guracha** with the details blank; three already used, with typed details: "Dispatched to Nairobi for digitisation" |
| ev_typed_over | Physical (document view) | One used dispatch note under the raking light | The **typing lies on top of the signature's ink**: the form was signed blank and filled in later |
| ev_room | Physical | Digitisation room | The steel binding punch on the scanning table, **wiped**; a **missing floor tile's grout** stained and scrubbed; a tiny **phone-camera lens cap** (Abdia's, from her phone case) under the cabinet |

**Charge sheet.** Eight groups:

> **WHEN:** the 5-event strip.
> **WHERE:** killed in {where_1}; her body left at {where_2}.
> **WHO / HOW / WHY:** `{who} killed Abdia Golicha by {how}, because {why}.`
> **FORGERY:** `{document} was forged, as shown by {tell}.`
> **ABSENCE:** `{what's missing} shows that {conclusion}.`
> **SPINE:** `The man who removed the Isiolo files also withdrew {pin} eleven years ago.`

- WHEN (strip): *Emojong withdraws FB 4471* (eleven years ago) · *Abdia starts her shadow list* (three months ago) · *Abdia overhears "the fourth floor"* (Thursday 16:10) · *Abdia is killed in the digitisation room* (Friday, about 18:35) · *Emojong signs out with "archive boxes"* (19:55). Decoy: Friday 17:00 ("left with the others").
- WHERE: where_1 ✔ *the digitisation room*, *the records room*, *the registry gate*, *the guesthouse*, *the tuk-tuk stage*, *the registrar's office* (6). where_2 ✔ *the murram pit on the Garba Tula road*, *the guesthouse*, *the Isiolo river*, *drawer 14*, *the project vehicle*, *her family's home* (6). 36 combinations.
- WHO: Julius Emojong, Hassan Guracha, Omar Hiribae, Jattani Halkano, Kennedy Mulwa, Florence Atieno (6).
- HOW: ✔ *struck with a steel binding punch*, *struck with a file-cabinet drawer*, *strangled with a scanner cable*, *a fall in the records room*, *hit by the project vehicle*.
- WHY: ✔ *she'd found and listed the files he was removing from the registry*, *a dispute over her wedding*, *a registrar protecting his pre-signed forms*, *a company's anger over the Garba Tula case*, *a theft of her phone*.
- FORGERY: documents ✔ *the pre-signed dispatch notes*, *the scan log*, *the sign-out book*, *the vehicle work ticket*, *the withdrawal requisition*. Tells ✔ ***the typing lies on top of a signature made on a blank form***, *a retired stamp*, *a parcel missing from the index map*, *a witness who was dead*, *a batch number that doesn't exist*, *an index number belonging to someone else*.
- ABSENCE: missing ✔ ***37 scan numbers and 37 files, with no dispatch entries***, *no sign-out for Abdia*, *no journey on the vehicle's work ticket*, *no signal from his phone for an hour*, *her phone never moved after 18:41*. Conclusions ✔ ***the files were being removed from inside the registry without a record***, *Abdia ran away*, *the files were sent to Nairobi properly*, *the software lost the scans*, *the vehicle was never used*, *Abdia left with the others at five*. (Rule 18 accepted alternatives: none for this group; the other missing facts serve the WHEN and WHERE groups.)
- SPINE (Pattern File pins): *field book FB 4471, Bahati Block 9 (case 40)* ✔, *Doreen Kathambi's commissioner stamp (case 70)*, *the oval "MV" seal (case 66)*, *the REGISTRAR OF TITLES seal proof (case 10)*, *the container of "printing paper", Shimanzi (case 30)* (5). (The Garba Tula file, case 74, is deliberately **not** an option: it's this case's own evidence, not eleven years old.)
- Halima, all eight groups: *"A clerk kept a list in a green notebook because nobody else would. Put her name on the first page of whatever we build from this, Amani."*

**Proof**
1. `ev_missing` + `ev_signout` + `ev_phone` → Abdia never left the building alive; her phone died inside at 18:41. **(ABSENCE.)**
2. `ev_scanlog` + `ev_index` + `ev_dispatch` + `ev_typed_over` + Guracha's reveal → 37 files removed without record, on pre-signed dispatch forms. **(ABSENCE; FORGERY.)**
3. `ev_galma` + `ev_signout` → Emojong left at 19:55 with a trolley and a large box.
4. `ev_odometer` + Omar's reveal + `ev_records_emojong` → the project vehicle went 32 km out and back while his phone was off-network (also Emojong's reopening).
5. `ev_pit` → her body at km 32 of the Garba Tula road.
6. `ev_room` + blood + fingerprints → killed in the digitisation room with the binding punch → **WHO = Julius Emojong**, **HOW = struck with a steel binding punch**, **WHY = she'd found and listed the files he was removing from the registry**, **WHERE = the digitisation room → the murram pit on the Garba Tula road**.
7. `ev_drawer` (warrant) + `ev_notebook` + `ev_withdrawal` + handwriting → **SPINE = FB 4471 (case 40)**: the same officer code withdrew Joseph's field book eleven years ago. **(Twist: the registry man; and in his drawer, Joseph's own working field book.)**

**Eliminations**
- *WHO:* Guracha: signed out 17:45; at a mosque committee meeting 18:00–20:00 (the imam). Omar: at the guesthouse from 19:00 (cook), without the vehicle. Jattani: `ev_jattani`. Kennedy: `ev_kennedy`. Florence: `ev_florence`.
- *HOW:* "struck with a file-cabinet drawer" (wound is a narrow edge; drawer edges are rolled); "strangled with a scanner cable" (post-mortem); "a fall in the records room" (killed in the digitisation room; blood in the grout); "hit by the project vehicle" (no vehicle injuries).
- *WHY:* refuted per option: wedding dispute (Jattani in Garissa; the families' argument was settled on Thursday by phone, his sister confirms); registrar protecting his forms (he was at the mosque; his reveal shows fear, not violence); a company's anger (Kennedy was cooperating with the police at the time); theft of her phone (the phone is in drawer 14, unsold, switched off).

**Red herrings / twist.** Herrings: the fiancé in a family wedding dispute, and the company man from case 74. **Twists:** the polite Nairobi civil servant is the registry man; and in his drawer is the field book taken from Joseph Mwenda's body twelve years ago.

**After the verdict.**
- Abdia's 37 files go back on the Isiolo shelves, each with a new index card in Halake's handwriting: *"Returned. Abdia Golicha's list."* The Garba Tula community's registration file is among them, and the lease is cancelled at a community assembly; the women's group chair reads Abdia's name out first.
- Emojong is charged with Abdia's murder. He says nothing more. The line *"I'm a drawer. Desks don't get opened"* is pinned to `t_kivuli`.
- **Joseph's working field book** goes into the evidence store under the new OB number from case 70's reopened file. The player can open it: Joseph's handwriting, beacon angles, a sketch of Block 9, and on the last used page, in pencil: *"Visited again today by the man from Lands, 4th floor. Offered money to change BH9/14. Refused. Told Ch. Insp. Wairimu."* The date is three weeks before his death.
- The phone rings. Mwalimu, very quietly: *"Fourth floor. Yes. That's the floor."* A pause. *"Come home, Amani. The rest is in Nairobi."*
- The Pattern File: `t_registry` closes as **identified: Julius Emojong** (with a note: "statement pending"); `t_kivuli` gains *"the fourth floor"* (from Abdia, Joseph and Mwalimu: three sources now); `t_joseph` gains the working field book.
- **Collectible:** **the key to drawer 14**, a small brass key on a ring with a cardboard tag in Abdia's handwriting: *"Ask him."* (She'd tagged it in the scanner tray before she opened the drawer.)

**Clock plan.** Missing-person interviews (2 h), registry and sign-out book (1 h), Galma (1 h), records ① (4 h, 1 stamp), Florence and the scan log (1 h), index cards and dispatch book (2 h), Guracha (1 h), the vehicle and Omar (1 h), records ② (4 h, 1 stamp; ① and ② can run in parallel once probable cause exists for each), Emojong lawyered → reopened with the vehicle facts, Ewoi and the Garba Tula road (40 min + 2 h search), post-mortem (1 h), warrant on drawer 14 (2 h, 1 stamp). **Detain Emojong** when the body is found; blood and prints 10 h, document exam 14 h, handwriting 14 h. About 16 h of the detention used. Rule 16 passes.

**Credibility path.** 3 stamps (the maximum).

**New interface beat.** **The gap ruler.** The scan log scrolls as a long strip of numbers; the player drags a ruler along it and every missing number drops out as a dotted gap. Matching each gap to an index card lights a file-shaped hole on the shelf photo. Thirty-seven holes.

**Kenyan texture.** County land registries and their steel cabinets, "digitisation" projects that move paper to Nairobi, pre-signed forms, dispatch books and guard sign-out books, government vehicles and work tickets, murram pits along the Garba Tula road, a clerk who kept a list.

**Spine.** Boss. SPINE group needs case 40 (`t_joseph`, `t_registry`). Threads: `t_registry` closes as identified; `t_kivuli` ("the fourth floor"); `t_joseph` (the working field book and Joseph's last note); `t_mvua` (the Garba Tula file was one of Mvua's leases). Notebook, final line of the region: *"Fourth floor. Three people have said it now. Dad wrote it down first."*

**Glossary.** sajili ya ardhi (land registry), faili (file), droo (drawer), dispatch, kitabu cha kutoka (sign-out book), shimo la murram (murram pit).

**Images (9).** Portraits: Abdia (green notebook), Emojong (grey suit, reading glasses on a cord), Guracha, Omar, Florence, Galma. Locations: the Isiolo land registry's digitisation room at night, one cabinet drawer ajar; the Garba Tula road at dusk, an empty pit beside it. Evidence photo: Joseph's working field book, cloth-bound, water-stained, open at the pencil note (reuses Joseph's handwriting style from case 40).

**Audit tags.** Culprit M, 50s, Teso-origin name, motive commissioned (removing records for Mvua; cover-up of that work). Victim F, 30s, Borana-origin name.

### Region 8 questions for the cultural reader

1. **General:** the region is cast mostly from Borana, Turkana, Samburu, Rendille, Gabra and Somali names. Are the names plausible (especially the Rendille and Gabra names in cases 75 and 77, which are the least certain), and does any community come across as defined by violence?
2. **Case 71:** stock theft by a young herder, and a sister who kills to protect him. Is the Isiolo livestock market's counting clerk and ear-notch detail right?
3. **Case 72:** are Lake Turkana's night winds, landing registers at Loiyangalani, fish buyers' advances and the alkaline crust described accurately? Is "akala" right for tyre-sole sandals in Turkana?
4. **Case 73:** is a Samburu women's beadwork group moving its lodge money away from a male "manager" plausible and respectfully told? Are the homestead routines (water in the afternoon, milking at dusk) right?
5. **Case 74:** community land committees, assemblies, minute books and county filings under the Community Land Act: accurate? A Borana elder poisoned by his cousin: does it handle drought loss and the bribe with dignity?
6. **Case 75:** a child killed by a lorry, settled with no driver found, and a mother who waits nine years. Is this too heavy, and is the "bandits" story (which the evidence clears) handled without stigmatising herders?
7. **Case 77:** an elders' compensation settlement for a child's death, which the county then treats as a crime. Does the case respect customary settlement while still showing why a death record can't be falsified? Is Shanko's line ("Why should Marsabit undo what the elders did?") fair to that view?
8. **Case 78:** teacher postings far from home, and a relationship between a teacher and the school cook. Respectful to both?
9. **Case 79:** a border-town hospital, blood-alcohol samples and the morning vehicle to Marsabit: plausible?
10. **Case 80:** is a Ministry of Lands "digitisation team" removing community-land files plausible fiction, and does it avoid implying that the real ministry or its digitisation programme is corrupt as an institution? The card names a fictional officer and a fictional "fourth floor" only.

Second cook added: both paddles are used every morning, and Nakiru alone holds the kitchen key. Pauline's alibi comes from her own interview. Nakiru's later claim: the paddle "broke weeks ago". | Strip limit (3–5 events); one lab table |
| 79 | OB 02/31/07 (Fri 31 July; card said 02/07/08); everything happens in the small hours of Friday. Act window tightened to 03:40–03:55 using two new anchors: Kavata's last fridge-temperature entry at 03:38, and the other night nurse (Halima Boru, new) who saw the bribe at the lab door at 03:00 and saw Mahat come back to casualty with wet sleeves at 03:55. Blood runs as a trace test, 12+4 h (card said 6+4). Beer bottles in the cab added as a second breaker for Yusuf. "The hospital corridor" is a separate place outside the annex, so the WHERE options stay distinct. | Rule 6; the act window needs anchors on both sides |

## Part J — Region 9: Westlands / Karen / Runda (cases 81–90)

**Region frame.** Mid-August to late September of the second year: the cool, grey Nairobi "winter" giving way to sunshine, jacaranda not yet in bloom. Amani is back at the SCU desk at Tausi Lane, and the cases move into the city's money: Westlands' glass towers and rooftop bars, Karen's old stone houses, paddocks and polo grounds, Runda's and Lavington's gated homes, private clinics, maisonettes with baby monitors and alarm panels. Evidence is plentiful here (private CCTV, alarm logs, electric-fence logs, guard books, app records) and it is also **curated**: people with money have staff, lawyers, and the means to arrange what the police will find. Mwalimu's card in the Pattern File says *"Witness. Promised to testify."* She calls rarely; when she does, it's to ask if Amani has eaten. Halima is in court every week on the Emojong file, facing the same defence advocate who keeps appearing in Amani's cases: **Advocate Sharon Kiprop**.

### J1. Region 9 rules

- **Accomplices arrive (case 81).** A crime can now have a **principal** (who killed) and an **accomplice** (who knowingly helped). The WHO group gains a second sentence: `{who} killed X, helped by {accomplice}, who {role}.` Roles are verbs: *had a key cut*, *gave a false alibi*, *lured the victim*, *drove the killer*, *deleted the footage*, *disposed of the weapon*, *planted evidence*. The accomplice blank always includes **nobody**. A person who helped **without knowing** (a bribed guard who opened a door "for a family matter") is not an accomplice: the game refutes that pairing with the evidence of what they knew. At least 6 names (with "nobody") × 5 roles = 30 combinations.
- **Joint principals (case 85).** Two people can kill together. The WHO blank becomes `{who_1} and {who_2}`; order doesn't matter. Physical evidence must show two people (two grips, two sets of prints, two phones).
- **Framed suspects and the PLANTED group (case 83).** Some evidence is **planted** to point at an innocent person. The player can mark a fact as *suspected planted*; it stays on the board with a red-edged frame. The **PLANTED** group: `{item} was planted, as shown by {tell}.` At least 5 items × 6 tells = 30 combinations. Planted-evidence tells are physical and fair: *a wiped transfer, not spatter*; *prints under the printed text*; *dust under the object, not on it*; *a timestamp before the item existed*; *the wrong-handed knot*; *placed where the framed person couldn't reach*.
- **The REAL TARGET group (case 84).** Sometimes the person who died wasn't the one the killer meant to kill. `The killer meant to kill {target}.` Single blank, at least 5 options. WHY then describes the motive against the **intended** target; the verdict reconstruction shows both.
- **Private evidence.** Gated homes add new records: **alarm-panel logs** (which sensor, which code, what time), **electric-fence logs**, **guard gate books**, **home CCTV** (which can be switched off or deleted, so its gaps become ABSENCE facts), **app logs** (a betting app, a smart lock, a car's tracking app). Records requests to private companies need probable cause like any other.
- **Lawyers.** Lawyered suspects are common here (cases 83, 86, 88, 90). **Advocate Sharon Kiprop** (from case 80) represents the suspect in 83 and 86. Other advocates: **Advocate Lucas Gachoki** (88). The reopening-fact rule from region 7 applies.
- **Liars: 3 per case. Herrings: 2–3. Twists: 7** (cases 82, 83, 84, 86, 87, 88, 90). Suspects 5–7, proof chain 5–7.
- **Charge sheet:** WHEN, WHERE, WHO (+ ACCOMPLICE where relevant), HOW, WHY, + FORGERY / ABSENCE / PLANTED / REAL TARGET when the case uses them, + SPINE (boss). No case uses more than eight groups.
- **Region casting rule (from the region 8 audit).** The region's risk is two stereotypes at once, "the rich did it" and "the help did it". So: **no more than 3 wrongdoers (culprits or accomplices) who are domestic or security workers**; wealthy culprits from **at least 5 communities**; **at most 2 wrongdoers from any one community**; **at least 1 culprit in their 70s**; **at least 4 women culprits**; **at most 2 Luo and 2 Kikuyu victims**. Every case has at least one domestic or security worker who is **a key honest witness** (a housekeeper, a guard, a groom, a nanny, a driver), so staff appear here as the people who notice things.

**Region curve at a glance**

| # | Title | Setting | Suspects | Chain | Herrings | Liars | Lawyered | New group / feature | Twist | Stamps | Est. min |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 81 | Two Keys | Karen, an old stone house | 5 | 5 | 2 | 3 | — | ACCOMPLICE | — | 2 | 40 |
| 82 | The Driver's Story | Lavington and a Kileleshwa studio gym | 5 | 6 | 2 | 3 | — | Accomplice + lure | The lure came from the wife's phone; she never sent it | 2 | 42 |
| 83 | Planted | Westlands jewellery workshop | 5 | 6 | 2 | 3 | Yes | PLANTED | The fired man was framed | 2 | 44 |
| 84 | Wrong Glass | Karen, Sunday lunch | 6 | 6 | 2 | 3 | — | REAL TARGET | The dead woman wasn't the target | 2 | 44 |
| 85 | The Guest List | Runda pool party | 6 | 6 | 3 | 3 | — | Joint principals | — | 3 | 46 |

### Case 81 — Two Keys

`case-081` · Westlands / Karen / Runda · 40 min · suspects 5 · chain 5 · herrings 2 · liars 3 · groups WHEN, WHERE, WHO + ACCOMPLICE, HOW, WHY · stamps needed 2 (records, warrant)

**OB entry.** OB 07/16/08, 10:30 (Sunday 16 August). An advocate for a school trust reports that his client, an elderly man in Karen, died in his sleep on Saturday night, two days before he was due to sign a land sale, and asks for an investigation. The family doctor had been ready to certify "natural causes, age 79".

**Setting.** Karen, on Nairobi's south-western edge: big plots under old trees, stone houses from the 1950s, paddocks, dirt lanes, a shopping centre with a key-cutter's kiosk in the car park. **Mzee Kamande's house:** a long stone bungalow on 12 acres, a housekeeper's cottage behind it, a house alarm with internal motion sensors, and a master bedroom with a heavy **mortice lock**, fitted after a burglary two years ago. There are **two keys**: Mzee's own, on his bedside table at night, and a spare kept by the housekeeper in a tin in her cottage.

**Map.** Main house ↔ housekeeper's cottage: 60 m · House ↔ Karen shopping centre: 3 km · House ↔ Stephen's club in Westlands: 40 min.

**Victim.** **Mzee Josiah Kamande**, 79, retired veterinary surgeon, widower, diabetic (evening insulin by pen, which he gives himself).

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lilian Kamande | 53 | Suspect | His daughter-in-law; lives in the house and manages his medicines and appointments | **Culprit** (liar 1) |
| Brian Kamande | 24 | Suspect | Lilian's son, his grandson | **Accomplice** (liar 2): had a copy of the bedroom key cut |
| Stephen Kamande | 55 | Suspect | His son; heavily in debt; would get only the house under the new plan | Innocent (red herring 1); **liar 3** (says he was at his club until 01:00) |
| Rehema Atieno | 58 | Suspect / key witness | Housekeeper for 22 years; keeps the spare key | Innocent (red herring 2); **honest staff witness** |
| Dr. Anne Mbithi | 50 | Witness | Director of the school trust buying 8 acres | Innocent |
| Advocate Simon Maina | 61 | Witness | The trust's advocate, and Mzee's friend | Innocent |

**What really happened.** Mzee Kamande planned to sell 8 of his 12 acres to the fictional **Ngong Hills Academy Trust** on Monday and put the money into a trust for his grandchildren's education and a veterinary scholarship. Stephen would keep the house but not the land he'd been borrowing against for years. Lilian, who had nursed the old man for six years and expected the land to save the family, decided he must not reach Monday. On Saturday afternoon Brian borrowed Rehema's spare key ("Grandpa wants his reading glasses from the drawer") and had a copy cut at the key-cutter's kiosk at Karen shopping centre at 16:12, then returned the original within the hour. At about 23:35 Lilian let herself into the bedroom with the copy while Mzee slept, and injected a large dose of insulin from his own pen into his upper arm. She locked the door behind her. He died in the early hours. Brian threw the copied key into the pit latrine behind the old stables on Sunday morning.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Master bedroom | In bed, peaceful; the door was **locked** when Rehema came with tea at 06:30 and she opened it with her spare |
| ev_maina | Witness | Advocate Maina | "He told me on Thursday: 'If anything happens to me before Monday, look at my family.' I thought he was joking." |
| ev_sale | Physical (found paper) | Mzee's desk | The sale agreement for 8 acres, signing set for Monday; a draft trust deed for the grandchildren's education; a letter to Stephen: *"You will have the house. The land has carried your debts long enough."* |
| ev_pen | Physical | Bedside | His insulin pen. The pharmacy dispensed a **new, full pen on Friday**; his own logbook shows **20 units on Friday night** and **20 units at 20:00 Saturday**. The pen's dose counter shows **far more than 40 units used** |
| ev_logbook | Physical (found paper) | Bedside | Mzee's careful insulin log for six years: dose, time, and site, **always "stomach, left/right"** |
| ev_site | Forensic (post-mortem) | Body | Two fresh injection points: one in the **stomach** (his evening dose) and one in the **upper left arm**, a site he never used |
| ev_alarm | Physical (found paper) | Alarm panel log (house in "night mode": perimeter armed, internal sensors log only) | **Corridor sensor outside the master bedroom: 23:34 and 23:41.** No other internal movement between 22:30 and 05:50 |
| ev_rehema | Witness | Housekeeper | "Brian came at about four and asked for the spare key for Mzee's glasses. He brought it back before five. It's always in my tin." |
| ev_kiosk | Physical (found paper) | Key-cutter's kiosk, Karen shopping centre | Receipt book: **Saturday 16:12, one mortice key, KSh 600**; the key-cutter remembers "a young man, a Kamande, he said it was his grandfather's spare". The car-park camera shows Brian's car |
| ev_records | **Records request** (Brian's PesaPap and line; probable cause: `ev_kiosk` + `ev_rehema`) | PesaPap + Jamii Mobile | **KSh 600 to the key-cutter's till at 16:14**; a call from Lilian at **15:40**: 3 minutes; Sunday 07:05 a call from Brian to Lilian: 40 seconds |
| ev_latrine | Physical, **warrant** (probable cause: `ev_records` + `ev_alarm`) | Old stables pit latrine (Brian's reveal points there; the warrant covers the property's outbuildings) | A **freshly cut mortice key**, still bright, matching the bedroom lock |
| ev_stephen | Witness | Rehema (after Stephen's lie is pressed) and Stephen's club bar tab | Stephen's tab closes at **21:55**; Rehema heard him shouting at his father in the sitting room at about **22:30** ("Just sign over two acres to me!"), then his car door and his room door |
| ev_stephen_room | Witness | Lilian's own first statement | "Stephen came in drunk and went to bed." |
| ev_mbithi | Physical (found paper) | School board meeting minutes | Dr. Mbithi chairing a parents' meeting until 21:00 Saturday, then home in Langata |

**Forensics**

| Test | Sample | Lab hours | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Post-mortem (Dr. Chebii) | Body | Immediate | No heart attack; signs consistent with **severe low blood sugar**; injection site `ev_site`. Time of death **01:30–04:00** |
| Toxicology (insulin assay) | Blood near the arm site vs elsewhere | 18 h | Very high insulin concentration at the arm site |
| Fingerprints | Insulin pen | 6 h | Mzee's, and a partial **Lilian's** on the dose knob (she handles his medicines daily, so the print alone proves little; see Proof) |
| Key comparison | `ev_latrine` key vs the bedroom lock and the kiosk's blank stock | 6 h | Cut on the kiosk's machine from the same blank brand; opens the lock |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lilian Kamande | Cooperative, tired, devoted-sounding | **"I went to bed at ten and didn't leave my room all night."** | Yes (liar 1) | `ev_alarm` + Brian's reveal | *"I've washed that old man, fed him, counted his tablets for six years. And on Monday he would give the land to strangers' children."* |
| Brian Kamande | Guarded, scared | **"I never touched Grandpa's key. I was in Westlands all afternoon."** | Yes (liar 2) | `ev_rehema` + `ev_kiosk` + `ev_records` | *"Mum asked me to get a copy. She said Grandpa kept locking himself in and one day he'd fall and we couldn't reach him. On Sunday morning she called and said 'throw it away'. I threw it in the old latrine. I knew then."* |
| Stephen Kamande | Cooperative, ashamed | **"I was at my club until one in the morning."** | Yes (liar 3) | `ev_stephen` (bar tab + Rehema) | *"I came home at half past ten and begged him for two acres. He said no. I went to my room and drank. I didn't go near him after that, I swear it."* |
| Rehema Atieno | Cooperative, grieving | "I lent the key to Brian for the glasses and he brought it back." | True | — | *"Mzee locked his door because he said a house full of debt is a house full of thieves."* |

**ACCOMPLICE.** Names: *Brian Kamande* ✔, *Stephen Kamande*, *Rehema Atieno*, *Dr. Anne Mbithi*, *Advocate Simon Maina*, *nobody*. Roles: ✔ ***had a copy of the bedroom key cut***, *gave a false alibi*, *lured the victim*, *disposed of the weapon*, *switched off the alarm*.
Refutations: "Rehema lent the key" is true but she didn't know why (`ev_rehema` and her immediate honesty: an unknowing helper); "Stephen gave a false alibi" (he lied for himself, not for Lilian); "switched off the alarm" (the alarm logged everything; nobody disarmed it); "disposed of the weapon" (the weapon, the insulin pen, stayed at the bedside; what Brian threw away was the copied key).

**WHEN (strip).** *Lilian calls Brian* (15:40) · *Brian has the key cut* (16:12) · *Stephen shouts at his father* (22:30) · *Lilian enters the bedroom* (23:34) · *Mzee dies* (about 02:30). Decoy: 01:00 (Stephen's "home from the club").

**WHERE.** ✔ *Mzee's bedroom*, *the sitting room*, *the housekeeper's cottage*, *the key-cutter's kiosk*, *the old stables*.

**Proof**
1. `ev_maina` + `ev_sale` → he was about to sell the land and cut the family's debts off from it.
2. `ev_pen` + `ev_logbook` + `ev_site` + post-mortem + toxicology → a huge extra insulin dose, injected in a place he never used: not his own hand.
3. `ev_body` (locked door) + `ev_rehema` + `ev_kiosk` + `ev_records` → a copy of the only spare key was cut on Saturday by Brian, at Lilian's request.
4. `ev_alarm` + Lilian's broken claim → someone stood at the bedroom door at 23:34 and 23:41; Lilian says she never left her room.
5. `ev_latrine` (warrant) + key comparison + Brian's reveal → **WHO = Lilian Kamande**, **helped by Brian Kamande, who had a copy of the bedroom key cut**, **HOW = an overdose of insulin injected from his own pen**, **WHY = to stop him selling the family land and putting the money in a trust**, **WHERE = Mzee's bedroom**.

**Eliminations**
- *WHO (principal):* Stephen: drunk in his room from 22:35 (the corridor sensor fires only twice, at the bedroom door, and his room is in the other wing, whose sensor never fires). Brian: back at his flat in Westlands by 21:00 (his building's gate log); he didn't enter the house. Rehema: her cottage is outside the alarmed building; the corridor sensor log needs someone inside after 22:30, and she had no copy. Dr. Mbithi and Advocate Maina: elsewhere.
- *HOW:* "died in his sleep of old age" (post-mortem, insulin assay); "took too much insulin by mistake" (`ev_logbook` shows 20 units at 20:00 in the stomach; the second dose is in the arm, at about 23:35, after he was asleep); "smothered" (post-mortem); "his heart tablets doubled" (toxicology).
- *WHY:* "a son's drunken anger over two acres" (Stephen's; eliminated); "a housekeeper's theft" (nothing missing; she raised the alarm); "the school trust wanted the land cheaply" (the trust gains nothing by his death: the sale dies with him); "an inheritance for the grandson" (Brian gains nothing under either plan beyond school fees, which the trust would have paid).

**Red herrings / twist.** Herrings: the drunk son who shouted at his father that night, and the housekeeper who held the spare key. No twist; this case teaches the accomplice group plainly.

**Charge sheet.** Full sheet + ACCOMPLICE. WHO: Lilian Kamande, Brian Kamande, Stephen Kamande, Rehema Atieno, Anne Mbithi (5).

**Clock plan.** Bedroom (1 h), Rehema (1 h), Advocate Maina (1 h), desk papers (1 h), pen and logbook (30 min), post-mortem (2 h), alarm log (1 h; the alarm company's office), Lilian (1 h), kiosk (1 h), records (4 h, 1 stamp), Brian (1 h), Stephen and the club (2 h), warrant on the outbuildings (2 h, 1 stamp). **Detain Lilian**; toxicology 18 h, key comparison 6 h. Rule 16 passes.

**Credibility path.** 2 stamps.

**New interface beat.** **The second sentence.** When the WHO group is filled, a second line slides out beneath it on the charge sheet: *"…helped by ____, who ____."* The first time, Mwalimu calls (her first hint call in weeks, unprompted): *"Most people who kill don't do it alone, Amani. Find who held the door."*

**Kenyan texture.** Old Karen houses on big plots, land as a family's bank, a son borrowing against land that isn't his yet, house alarms and mortice locks after a burglary, the key-cutter in the shopping-centre car park, a housekeeper of 22 years, school trusts buying land, insulin pens and a veterinarian's careful logbook.

**Spine.** None.

**Glossary.** ufunguo (key), sindano ya insulini (insulin pen), mkwe (in-law), shamba, mtumishi wa nyumbani / housekeeper.

**Images (6).** Portraits: Mzee Kamande, Lilian, Brian, Stephen, Rehema. Location: a 1950s Karen stone bungalow under old trees at dawn, one bedroom window with its curtain closed.

**Audit tags.** Culprit F, 50s, Kikuyu-origin name, motive land/inheritance. Accomplice M, 20s, Kikuyu-origin name. Victim M, 70s, Kikuyu-origin name.

### Case 82 — The Driver's Story

`case-082` · Westlands / Karen / Runda · 42 min · suspects 5 · **chain 6** · herrings 2 · liars 3 · groups WHEN, WHERE, WHO + ACCOMPLICE, HOW, WHY · stamps needed 2 (records ×2) · **twist: the lure came from the wife's phone, and she never sent it**

**OB entry.** OB 15/26/08, 07:45 (Wednesday 26 August). A cleaner reports a personal trainer found dead in his private studio gym in Kileleshwa.

**Setting.** Kileleshwa and Lavington: leafy hills of apartment blocks and maisonettes west of the city, a short drive from Westlands. **Andrew's studio** is a converted garage at the back of an apartment compound: mirrors, racks of kettlebells, a rowing machine, a side door to a lane. Wealthy clients book sessions by app.

**Map.** Studio ↔ the Onyangos' house in Lavington: 12 min drive · Studio ↔ the Westlands book-club venue: 15 min · Onyango house ↔ Felix's office in Westlands: 15 min.

**Victim.** **Andrew Simiyu**, 38, personal trainer with a private studio and a client list from Lavington to Runda.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Felix Onyango | 46 | Suspect | Investment banker; client of Andrew's for a year | **Culprit** (liar 1) |
| Josphat Kiprono | 35 | Suspect | Felix's driver for eight years | **Accomplice** (liar 2): drove Felix to the studio and back, and swore he'd driven him straight home |
| Nyokabi Onyango | 41 | Suspect | Felix's wife; Andrew's client, and in a relationship with him for six months | Innocent (red herring 1); **liar 3** (denies the affair) |
| Ian Waweru | 39 | Suspect | Andrew's former business partner; owed him KSh 900,000 | Innocent (red herring 2) |
| Mama Grace Wekesa | 55 | Key witness | The compound's caretaker; lives by the gate | Innocent; **honest staff witness** |
| Purity Wangari | 31 | Witness | Felix's personal assistant; keeps his calendar | Innocent: confirms he left the office at 18:40, not 19:00 |

**What really happened.** Nyokabi had been seeing Andrew for six months, using a **second phone** she kept in her dressing-table drawer. Felix found it on Sunday. He said nothing. On Tuesday evening, while Nyokabi was at her book club in Westlands (she left her main phone in her bag and the second phone, as always, in the drawer at home), Felix took the second phone and texted Andrew from it at 20:12: *"Can you open the studio at 9? I need to see you. Side door."* At 20:40 his driver Josphat drove him from the house to the lane behind the studio, waited with the engine off, and at 21:25 drove him home. Inside, Felix struck Andrew with a 16 kg kettlebell from the rack. He took the second phone home and put it back in the drawer. When police came, Josphat told them he'd driven Felix home from the office at 19:00 and "Bwana never left the house".

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_body | Physical | Studio floor | One crushing blow to the side of the head; a **16 kg kettlebell** back on the rack, its handle **wiped**; every other kettlebell has chalk-dust handprints |
| ev_text | Physical | Andrew's phone | Tuesday 20:12 from a number saved as **"N."**: *"Can you open the studio at 9? I need to see you. Side door."* Andrew: *"On my way."* Months of messages from "N." |
| ev_n_number | Physical (found paper) | Jamii Mobile subscriber check (part of `ev_records_n`) | "N." is registered to **Nyokabi Onyango** (a second line) |
| ev_records_n | **Records request ①** ("N." line; probable cause: `ev_text` + `ev_body`) | Jamii Mobile | At 20:12 the "N." phone was on the **Lavington mast** (the Onyango house), **not** in Westlands |
| ev_bookclub | Physical (found paper) | Westlands café booking and host's statement; Nyokabi's main phone | Nyokabi at the book club **19:30–22:15**, in front of eleven women; her **main phone** on the Westlands mast all evening |
| ev_grace | Witness | Caretaker | "A dark Mercedes stopped in the back lane at about quarter to nine, lights off. A tall man in a cap went in the side door. Twenty minutes later he came out walking fast and the car went. The driver never got out." |
| ev_tracker | **Records request ②** (vehicle tracking company for Felix's car; probable cause: `ev_grace` + `ev_records_n`) | Fleet-tracking app log | Felix's Mercedes: **left the Lavington house 20:40, stopped in the lane behind the studio 20:52–21:20, home 21:33** |
| ev_josphat_claim | Witness | Josphat's first statement | "I drove Bwana home from the office at seven. He never left. I washed the car and slept in my quarters." |
| ev_drawer | Physical | Nyokabi's dressing table | The second phone, **switched off**, in the drawer. Its last-used time: **20:14** |
| ev_cap | Physical | Felix's car (seen during a voluntary look at the car, with Felix's consent, while he's still cooperative) | A dark cap in the back seat; **chalk dust** on the rear mat |
| ev_chalk | Forensic | Chalk on the mat vs the studio's chalk bucket | Same gym chalk (magnesium carbonate with the studio's added scent) |
| ev_ian | Physical (found paper) | Mombasa hotel and flight | Ian in Mombasa since Monday |
| ev_affair | Physical | Months of "N." messages; a hotel booking at Naivasha in Andrew's email for "Mr & Mrs Simiyu" on a weekend Felix was in London | Proof of the relationship |

**Forensics**

### Case 83 — Planted

`case-083` · Westlands / Karen / Runda · 44 min · suspects 5 · **chain 6** · herrings 2 · liars 3 · lawyered: 1 · groups WHEN, WHERE, WHO, HOW, WHY, PLANTED · stamps needed 2 (records, warrant) · **twist: the fired man was framed** · **spine background: Advocate Kiprop's retainer till**

**OB entry.** OB 09/04/09, 08:20 (Friday 4 September). A building manager in Westlands reports a jewellery designer found dead in her third-floor workshop. A former employee is named by staff within the hour.

**Setting.** Westlands, Woodvale Grove: an older commercial block among new glass towers, with a lobby guard and a **sign-in book**, a lift with a camera, a basement car park with an **access-card barrier** that logs every card. On the third floor, fictional **Shah & Mghanga Studio**: jewellers' benches with pegs and torches, a gold scale and its weight ledger, a safe, a staff locker room. Staff lockers have individual keys; the two partners hold a **master key**.

**Map.** Workshop ↔ lobby: 3 floors (lift or stairs) · Building ↔ Kevin's bedsitter in Kangemi: 20 min by matatu · Building ↔ Priya's flat in Parklands: 10 min.

**Victim.** **Wakesho Mghanga**, 34, jewellery designer and co-founder of the studio; the designs are registered in her name.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| Kevin Otieno | 29 | Suspect (framed) | Workshop manager, fired two weeks ago by Wakesho for "missing gold" | Innocent (red herring 1; the framed man); **liar 2** (says he never came to the building on Thursday) |
| Hezron Wafula | 44 | Suspect | Lobby guard, evening shift | Innocent of the killing; **liar 3** (wrote a false sign-in entry for money, not knowing why) |
| Lenny Mwandoe | 38 | Suspect | Wakesho's ex-husband; owed her maintenance | Innocent (red herring 2) |
| Zawadi Kerubo | 26 | Key witness | Apprentice jeweller | Innocent; **honest staff witness** |

**What really happened.** For a year Priya had been skimming gold: recording smaller weights for her own batches on the scale ledger and selling the difference. When the losses showed, she pointed Wakesho at Kevin, who handled the scale; Wakesho fired him. Then Wakesho rechecked the ledger herself and found the missing weights all sat in Priya's batches. She also learned Priya was negotiating to take the studio's biggest client, a hotel group's corporate-gifts contract, to a new company of her own using Wakesho's designs. On Thursday at 17:00 Wakesho told Priya she'd see a lawyer on Friday about both. At 21:12 Priya drove into the basement with her access card, walked up the stairs, and found Wakesho working late. They argued at the bench. Priya hit her with a **steel ring mandrel**. Then she framed Kevin: she wiped Wakesho's blood onto Kevin's old workshop apron (still in his locker, uncleared since he was fired) and locked it back inside with her **master key**, and on the way out paid the lobby guard KSh 5,000 to write *"K. Otieno — 21:05 — collect tools"* in the sign-in book, telling him it was "so HR can close Kevin's file". She drove out at 22:04.

**WHEN (strip).** *Wakesho rechecks the ledger* (Wednesday) · *Kevin collects his dues and leaves* (19:02) · *Priya drives into the basement* (21:12) · *Wakesho is killed* (about 21:20) · *Priya drives out* (22:04). Decoy: 21:05 ("Kevin signs in").

**WHERE.** ✔ *the workshop bench*, *the locker room*, *the lobby*, *the basement car park*, *Kevin's bedsitter in Kangemi*.

**Proof**
1. `ev_smear` + blood-pattern analysis → the apron was wiped with blood, not worn in the attack. **(PLANTED.)**
2. `ev_locker_key` → Kevin couldn't open his own locker; someone with a master key did.
3. `ev_lift` + `ev_kevin_dues` + Kevin's broken claim + Hezron's broken claim → Kevin left at 19:02; the 21:05 entry was bought. **(Twist: framed.)**
4. `ev_ledger` + `ev_zawadi` + `ev_client` → Priya had stolen the gold, blamed Kevin, and was taking the client and designs.

Hezron: at his desk on the lobby camera all evening. Lenny: `ev_lenny`. Zawadi: left at 18:00 (lift camera), at her evening class.

**Red herrings / twist.** Herrings: the fired workshop manager everyone named, and the ex-husband. **Twist:** the man the staff named in the first hour was framed, with his own apron.

Planted items can't be used to press a suspect until the player either proves or clears them, so the game rewards checking before accusing.

### Case 84 — Wrong Glass

`case-084` · Westlands / Karen / Runda · 44 min · suspects 6 · **chain 6** · herrings 2 · liars 3 · groups WHEN, WHERE, WHO, HOW, WHY, REAL TARGET · stamps needed 2 (records, warrant) · **twist: the dead woman wasn't the target**

**OB entry.** OB 21/06/09, 22:10 (Sunday 6 September). A retired diplomat collapsed and died at her home in Karen on Sunday evening, after lunch at a neighbour's house. Her doctor reports no history of heart disease and asks for a post-mortem.

**Setting.** Karen, along a quiet murram lane: the **Carrow house**, a low stone farmhouse with a deep veranda, a paddock with two old horses, a kitchen garden, and a long **oleander hedge** (a common, beautiful, poisonous garden shrub in Nairobi). Sunday lunch on the veranda is a tradition: drinks come out on a tray, lunch at one, the neighbours walk over through a gap in the hedge.

**Map.** Carrow house ↔ Beatrice's house: 300 m (through the hedge gap) · Karen ↔ Marcus's flat in Kilimani: 30 min.

**Victim.** **Beatrice Achieng Oloo**, 63, retired diplomat; Desmond Carrow's neighbour and closest friend for twenty years.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Desmond Carrow | 74 | Suspect | Retired farmer and horse breeder; host | **Culprit** (liar 1) |
| Marcus Waweru | 31 | Suspect | Chloe's ex-boyfriend; invited himself to lunch | Innocent of the killing (red herring 1; **the real target**); **liar 2** (hides that he was blackmailing Chloe) |
| Chloe Carrow | 22 | Suspect | Desmond's granddaughter, a university student | Innocent; **liar 3** (denies being blackmailed) |
| Fiona Carrow | 48 | Suspect | Chloe's mother, Desmond's daughter | Innocent |
| Tobias Oloo | 36 | Suspect | Beatrice's nephew; inherits her house | Innocent (red herring 2) |
| Joyce Mbatha | 57 | Key witness | The Carrows' cook for fifteen years | Innocent; **honest staff witness** |

**What really happened.** In June, Chloe drove home drunk from a party and hit a parked car in Lavington, then drove off; nobody was hurt. Marcus, in the passenger seat, filmed it. After they split up in July he began demanding money: KSh 200,000 so far, and on Friday he asked for a million and announced he was coming to Sunday lunch "to discuss it with the family". Chloe told her grandfather everything on Saturday night. Desmond, who had buried his wife and son and had only Chloe left, decided Marcus would not leave Karen with that video. On Sunday morning he steeped **oleander leaves** from the hedge and strained the liquid into a jug in the pantry. Marcus had told Chloe on the phone that he wanted his juice "no ice", so at 12:50 Desmond poured one glass of passion juice **without ice** from the pantry jug, put it on the drinks tray among glasses with ice, and carried the tray out himself. Marcus had stepped onto the lawn to take a phone call. Beatrice, arriving late through the hedge, took the one glass without ice, as she always did: she has sensitive teeth and never takes ice. Nobody noticed. She went home at 16:00 feeling unwell, and died at 21:30.

**Evidence**

| ID | Type | Found | Facts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ev_doctor | Witness | Beatrice's doctor | No heart history; ECG normal in May; she called him at 19:00 with nausea, a slow pulse and "seeing yellow" |
| ev_joyce | Witness | Cook | "I made the passion juice in the big jug, with ice in every glass, like every Sunday. Mama Beatrice never takes ice, so I always keep her glass back and bring it separately. This Sunday Bwana Desmond said, 'I'll do the tray, Joyce,' and took it out himself. When I came with Mama Beatrice's glass without ice, she'd already got one. I thought, Bwana must have remembered." |
| ev_tray | Physical | Kitchen (unwashed glasses from Sunday stacked by the sink; Joyce washes on Monday) | Eight glasses: seven with **watermarks from ice**, one **without**; the one without carries Beatrice's lipstick |
| ev_pantry_jug | Physical | Pantry, back of a shelf | A small glass jug, rinsed, with a **faint green film** in the spout |
| ev_hedge | Physical | Oleander hedge by the kitchen garden | A patch **freshly stripped of leaves**, snapped stems still weeping white sap |
| ev_no_ice | Witness | Chloe (after her reveal) | "Marcus said on the phone Saturday, 'Tell your grandfather I'll want my juice without ice. I'm not catching a cold before my trip.' I told Grandpa that night." |
| ev_video | Physical | Marcus's phone (shown by Chloe's account and then found on his cloud folder by records) | The dashcam-style video of Chloe hitting the parked car |
| ev_records | **Records request** (Marcus's PesaPap; probable cause: Chloe's statement + `ev_no_ice`) | PesaPap | **KSh 200,000** from Chloe in four payments since July; Friday text to Chloe: *"One million or the video goes to your university and the police. See you Sunday."* |
| ev_desmond_house | Physical, **warrant** (probable cause: `ev_joyce` + `ev_pantry_jug` + `ev_hedge`) | Desmond's study and kitchen | A sieve and a muslin cloth in the outdoor bin, **green-stained**; in his study, an old library book, *Garden Plants of East Africa*, with a slip of paper marking the page on oleander |
| ev_tobias | Physical (found paper) | Kisumu hotel | Tobias in Kisumu all weekend for a wedding |
| ev_marcus_call | Physical (found paper) | Marcus's call log | A 9-minute call at 12:46–12:55 Sunday (he was on the lawn) |

**Forensics**

| Test | Sample | Lab hours | Result |
|---|---|---|---|

| Toxicology | Blood; the no-ice glass's dried residue; the pantry jug's film | 18 h | **Cardiac glycosides consistent with oleander** in all three |
| Fingerprints | The no-ice glass; the pantry jug | 6 h | Glass: Beatrice's and **Desmond's**. Jug: **Desmond's** only |

**Interrogation**

| Person | Stance | Claims | Lie? | Broken by | Reveals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Desmond Carrow | Cooperative, courtly, very tired | **"Joyce made the drinks. I only carried the tray."** / "I made nothing special for anyone." | Both (liar 1) | `ev_pantry_jug` + fingerprints + `ev_hedge` + `ev_joyce` | *"It was meant for that boy. Beatrice took the wrong glass. Beatrice. Of all the people at that table."* He asks to see her body. |
| Marcus Waweru | Guarded, charming | **"I'm a friend of the family. Chloe and I are on good terms."** | Yes (liar 2) | `ev_records` | *"It was a business arrangement. She had money, I had a video. Nobody got hurt."* (The verdict screen notes that blackmail is a separate charge, filed against him.) |
| Chloe Carrow | Guarded, frightened | **"Nobody is blackmailing me."** | Yes (liar 3) | `ev_records` (her payments to Marcus) | *"I told Grandpa on Saturday night. All of it. He held my hand and said, 'Leave it with me.'"* Gives `ev_no_ice` |
| Fiona Carrow | Cooperative | "I sat beside Beatrice. I didn't see who took which glass." | True | — | *"Daddy was strange all morning. He went to the hedge twice."* |
| Tobias Oloo | Cooperative | "I inherit her house. I was in Kisumu." | True | — | Shows `ev_tobias` |

**REAL TARGET.** `The killer meant to kill {target}.` Options: ✔ ***Marcus Waweru***, *Beatrice Oloo*, *Chloe Carrow*, *Fiona Carrow*, *Desmond Carrow himself*, *Joyce Mbatha*.
Refutations: "Beatrice" (Desmond had no motive against her, and the poisoned glass was set without ice for someone who'd asked for no ice: Marcus; Beatrice's no-ice glass was kept back by Joyce, as always); "Chloe" (she always takes ice; she was the one he was protecting); "Desmond himself" (he poured, carried and didn't drink; no suicide note; he made no attempt to take it); "Fiona" / "Joyce" (no link to the no-ice request).

**WHEN (strip).** *Chloe hits a parked car; Marcus films it* (June) · *Marcus demands a million* (Friday) · *Chloe tells Desmond* (Saturday night) · *the no-ice glass goes out on the tray* (12:50) · *Beatrice takes it* (about 12:55) · *Beatrice dies* (21:30). Decoy: 16:00 ("taken ill at home").

**WHERE.** ✔ *the Carrow veranda*, *the pantry*, *Beatrice's house*, *the oleander hedge*, *the paddock*.
*(Asked: where she was poisoned.)*

**Proof**
1. `ev_doctor` + post-mortem + toxicology → oleander poisoning, in the juice she drank at lunch.
2. `ev_tray` + `ev_joyce` → the poison was in the one glass without ice, which Desmond carried out himself.
3. `ev_pantry_jug` + `ev_hedge` + fingerprints + `ev_desmond_house` (warrant) → Desmond prepared it.
4. `ev_records` + Chloe's reveal + `ev_no_ice` → Marcus was blackmailing Chloe and had asked for his juice without ice. **(REAL TARGET: Marcus.)**
5. `ev_marcus_call` + `ev_joyce` → Marcus was on the lawn; Beatrice, who never takes ice, took the glass first. **(Twist.)** → **WHO = Desmond Carrow**, **HOW = oleander poison in a glass of passion juice**, **WHY = to stop Marcus blackmailing his granddaughter (the poison was meant for Marcus)**, **WHERE = the Carrow veranda**.

**Map.** Pool ↔ the house's party room: 25 m · House ↔ estate gate: 1.2 km · Runda ↔ Kilimani (Michelle's flat): 25 min.

**Victim.** **Faisal Hirsi**, 31, founder of the fictional sports-betting app **PataScore**; also lends large sums privately, at high interest, to people with famous names.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |

**What really happened.** Faisal had lent Allan and Michelle money for years: Allan to cover betting losses, Michelle to keep up a life she was paid to show online. On Friday he messaged both: pay by Monday, or on Tuesday he'd post "the list" (screenshots of their signed loan notes and their pleading messages) and file suits. At his party on Saturday night they talked in a corner and agreed. At 01:52 Michelle, who knew Faisal's phone PIN from their old friendship, took his phone from the bar and used his house-automation app to **switch off the pool-deck camera**. At about 02:05 Faisal, very drunk, went to sit by the pool. Allan and Michelle followed. Allan pushed him into the deep end; when he surfaced, Allan held his shoulders under and Michelle held his wrists to stop him grabbing the edge. Michelle broke a nail. Michelle threw Faisal's phone into the pool. Allan went back to the party with wet hair, laughing that he'd "jumped in for a dare". They scanned out together at 02:45 and left in one taxi.

### Case 86 — Second Opinion

`case-086` · Westlands / Karen / Runda · 46 min · suspects 6 · **chain 6** · herrings 2 · liars 3 · lawyered: 1 · groups WHEN, WHERE, WHO, HOW, WHY, FORGERY, PLANTED · stamps needed 3 (records ×2, warrant) · **twist: the angry patient's son was framed** · **spine background: a twelve-year-old photo from the fourth floor**

**OB entry.** OB 22/16/09, 07:10 (Wednesday 16 September). A cleaner reports a woman found dead in the medical-records room of a private heart clinic in Upper Hill. Staff name a patient's son who has been threatening the clinic online.

**Setting.** Upper Hill, Nairobi's hospital and office district: towers, private clinics, consultants' suites. Fictional **Mwamburi Heart Centre** occupies two floors of a medical plaza: consulting rooms, a catheterisation lab ("cath lab") where heart stents are fitted, a records room with rolling shelves, and a boardroom with photographs on the walls. The plaza has a lobby guard, staff access cards and a lost-and-found box at reception.

**Map.** Records room ↔ Dr. Mwamburi's office: same floor, 30 m · Clinic ↔ the plaza car park: lift · Upper Hill ↔ Elvis's flat in South B: 20 min.

**Victim.** **Grace Mumbua**, 41, fraud investigator for fictional **Imara Health Insurance**.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dr. Hamisi Mwamburi | 62 | Suspect | Cardiologist and owner of the clinic | **Culprit** (liar 1); **lawyered** (Advocate Sharon Kiprop) |
| Benson Mutua | 39 | Suspect | Cath-lab technician | Innocent of the killing; **liar 2** (falsified the cath-lab log for the fraud) |
| Elvis Karanja | 33 | Suspect (framed) | Son of a patient who died after a procedure at the clinic; has threatened Dr. Mwamburi online | Innocent (red herring 1; the framed man); **liar 3** (says he wasn't at the plaza that night) |
| Joan Akoth | 45 | Suspect | Practice manager; Grace had accused her of obstructing the audit | Innocent (red herring 2) |
| Mama Eunice Nafula | 52 | Key witness | Night cleaner | Innocent; **honest staff witness** |
| Dr. Paul Kibet | 47 | Witness | Imara's medical director, Grace's boss | Innocent |

**What really happened.** For four years the clinic billed insurers for **heart stents that were never fitted**: patients had a diagnostic test, and a forged "procedure report" was sent to the insurer claiming a stent. Benson kept the cath-lab log to match. Grace, auditing Imara's claims, noticed that 61 billed stents fell on dates the **cath-lab's maintenance record** showed the lab **closed for servicing**. She arranged to examine the original records on Tuesday evening after clinic hours, with Dr. Mwamburi's permission ("We have nothing to hide"). At about 20:40 Dr. Mwamburi came into the records room, saw what she had pulled out, and hit her with the heavy base of a steel drip stand from the corridor. Then he framed Elvis, who'd been shouting outside the plaza with a placard at 18:00 that evening. Two weeks earlier, Elvis had lost his **car key fob** at the clinic's reception; it sat in the **lost-and-found box**. Mwamburi took it from the box and dropped it under the body. He left by the car park at 21:15.

**FORGERY.** Documents: ✔ *the stent procedure reports*, *the cath-lab log*, *the maintenance record*, *the lost-and-found book*, *Grace's audit sheet*. ### Case 87 — Girth

`case-087` · Westlands / Karen / Runda · 46 min · suspects 6 · **chain 6** · herrings 2 · liars 3 · groups WHEN, WHERE, WHO, HOW, WHY, REAL TARGET · stamps needed 2 (records, warrant) · **twist: the rider wasn't the target**

**OB entry.** OB 11/19/09, 09:40 (Saturday 19 September). A rider is reported killed in a fall during morning practice at a riding club in Karen. **Suspected riding accident.**

**Setting.** Fictional **Mbagathi Riding Club**, off the Karen–Langata road: paddocks, a polo ground, a long stable block, a **tack room** where every owner's saddles hang on named pegs, and a stable gate with a **visitors' book**. Saturday mornings start early: grooms tack up at 06:30, riders school horses on the polo ground from 07:30.

**Map.** Stable block ↔ tack room: 20 m · Stables ↔ polo ground: 200 m · Club ↔ Ifrah's house in Karen: 10 min.

**Victim.** **Tajeu Kipaa**, 29, exercise rider employed by trainer Gerald Kimani.

**Cast**

| Ifrah Warsame | 44 | Suspect | Logistics businesswoman; keeps two horses at the club | **Culprit** (liar 1) |

**What really happened.** Two years ago Gerald sold Ifrah's son **Zakaria**, then 18, a grey gelding called **Shamal**, warranted "bombproof". Gerald knew from a vet's report that Shamal had an old back injury and bucked under pain. Three months later Shamal bucked Zakaria off at a jump; he broke his spine and now uses a wheelchair. Gerald denied knowing anything; Ifrah's lawyers got nowhere. This month Ifrah found the old vet's report in a clinic's archive. Gerald rides his own big bay, **Kilele**, in his own saddle every Saturday at 07:30. At 06:10 on Saturday Ifrah came to the club "to see her mare", went into the empty tack room, and with a seam ripper cut most of the stitching that holds the **girth strap** to Gerald's saddle, under the saddle flap where nobody would look. At 06:45 Gerald phoned his head groom: he'd woken with a migraine and wouldn't ride; *"Let Tajeu school Kilele in my saddle."* At 07:50, at a canter on the polo ground, the girth tore away; the saddle slid and Tajeu was thrown head-first into a goalpost.

3. `ev_book` + `ev_mare` + `ev_records` + Ifrah's broken claim → Ifrah was in the tack room alone at 06:10–06:30, before anyone knew Tajeu would ride.
4. `ev_vetreport` + `ev_warranty` + Gerald's reveal → Gerald knowingly sold her son a dangerous horse.
5. `ev_car` (warrant) + tool-mark + leather dust → **WHO = Ifrah Warsame**, **HOW = she cut the stitching of the saddle's girth so it would tear at speed, and he was thrown**, **WHY = revenge on Gerald, who knowingly sold her son a dangerous horse that left him paralysed (the cut was meant for Gerald)**, **WHERE = the tack room**.

Susan: `ev_susan`. Kioko: tacked up the horse in front of two other grooms and checked the girth, as he always does.

**Red herrings / twist.** Herrings: the rival trainer seen near the tack room, and the trainer's wife. **Twist:** the cut was meant for the man who cancelled his ride with a hangover.

### Case 89 — Rooftop

`case-089` · Westlands / Karen / Runda · 46 min · suspects 6 · **chain 6** · herrings 3 · liars 3 · groups WHEN, WHERE, WHO + ACCOMPLICE, HOW, WHY, ABSENCE · stamps needed 2 (records, warrant)

**OB entry.** OB 14/27/09, 01:20 (Sunday 27 September). A woman falls from the eighth-floor rooftop bar of a Westlands building during an event. Staff tell police she was drunk and climbed the railing for a photo.

**Setting.** Westlands at night: rooftop bars, music, ride-hail cars double-parked. Fictional **Anga Rooftop**, eighth floor: a glass-fronted bar, a dance floor, and behind the bar a **service terrace** (kegs, a gas store, a waist-high railing) closed to guests. Cameras cover the bar, the lifts and the service terrace, recording to a PC in a small **security office** whose password the head bouncer holds.

**Map.** Dance floor ↔ service terrace: 15 m through a staff door · Rooftop ↔ the street below: 8 floors · Building ↔ Mukami's flat in Riverside: 10 min.

**Victim.** **Tracy Odhiambo**, 29, event photographer and crowd-safety officer.

**Cast**

| Name | Age | Role | Link | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mukami Njeru | 27 | Suspect | Event promoter (fictional **Skyline Socials**); organised the night | **Culprit** (liar 1) |
| Ezekiel Muriuki | 36 | Suspect | Head bouncer, hired by Skyline Socials for its events | **Accomplice** (liar 2): deleted the service-terrace footage and told police Tracy climbed the railing |
| Duncan Mwangi | 42 | Suspect | Anga's bar manager; let the event run over capacity | Innocent (red herring 1); **liar 3** (says the rooftop was under capacity) |
| Morris Ouma | 31 | Suspect | Tracy's ex-boyfriend; turned up and argued with her at 23:30 | Innocent (red herring 2) |
| Wesley Ngetich | 35 | Suspect | A guest Tracy photographed; demanded she delete the photos | Innocent (red herring 3) |
| Pendo Mwakio | 24 | Key witness | Bartender | Innocent; **honest staff witness** |

**What really happened.** In March, at a Skyline Socials concert in another venue, a crush on an overcrowded staircase injured fourteen people. The fire exit at the bottom was **padlocked** on Mukami's orders ("people are sneaking in free"). Tracy, working as crowd-safety officer that night, photographed the padlock and kept Mukami's WhatsApp order. The county inspectorate's inquiry stalled. This week Tracy told Mukami she'd hand her photos to the inquiry and a journalist on Monday. On Saturday Tracy came to Mukami's rooftop event to work, as booked, and at 00:25 texted the journalist: *"Meeting Mukami now on the service terrace. She wants to 'talk'. Monday still on."* On the terrace, Mukami asked for the memory card. Tracy refused. Mukami pushed her backwards over the waist-high railing. Then Mukami took Tracy's camera, which had fallen on the terrace, pulled out the memory card and dropped the camera over the railing too. She found Ezekiel and told him, "Tracy fell. She was drunk. The terrace camera can't show me there." Ezekiel, who'd worked her events for three years and was owed money, went to the security office and **deleted the terrace footage from 00:20 to 00:55**, and told the police Tracy had been drinking and had climbed the railing for a skyline photo.

I deleted it. She sent me sixty thousand at quarter past one. I'm not a killer. I'm a man who did what his boss said."* |
| Duncan Mwangi | Guarded | **"We were under capacity all night."** | Yes (liar 3) | `ev_capacity` | *"Four hundred and twelve. The promoter pays us per head. I didn't want a fine. That girl didn't fall because of a crowd."* |
| Morris Ouma | Cooperative | "We argued about getting back together. I left before midnight." | True | — | Shows `ev_morris` |
